news.Title: Tower Semiconductor Q3 Earnings Call Highlights
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Tower Semiconductor Ltd.? Here are five stocks we like better.

Record Q3 performance: Revenue rose 33% year over year to $526 million, while net profit increased to $120 million and diluted EPS reached $1.05. Management expects approximately $600 million in Q4 revenue, implying about $2 billion in 2026 revenue.

Silicon photonics is driving expansion: Q3 silicon photonics revenue reached roughly $240 million, with annualized capacity expected to exceed $1.1 billion in Q4. Tower is expanding production across four sites and expects 2027 capacity to support a run rate above $2.8 billion, backed by customer commitments extending through 2029.

Strong outlook and investment plan: Tower is developing near-packaged optics and advanced heterogeneous-integration products while investing $920 million in additional capacity. The company raised its long-term model to $3.6 billion in annual revenue, $1.38 billion in operating profit and a 33% net margin.

NVIDIA Just Named AI's Next Bottleneck—And These 3 Stocks Sit Right In It

Tower Semiconductor (NASDAQ:TSEM) reported record third-quarter results for 2026, citing accelerating demand for silicon photonics used in AI infrastructure and data-center connectivity, along with growth across its broader analog technology portfolio.

Revenue for the quarter reached $526 million, up 33% from $396 million in the third quarter of 2025 and 14% from $460 million in the prior quarter. Net profit rose to $120 million, or a 23% net margin, compared with $54 million and a 14% margin a year earlier. Diluted earnings per share were $1.05, compared with $0.47 in the prior-year period.

→ Starbucks Says Its Turnaround Is Done—The Numbers Make a Strong Case (With 1 Catch)

Tower Semiconductor's AI Rally Is Built on a Light-Speed Bet

Chief Executive Officer Russell Ellwanger said the company expects fourth-quarter revenue at the midpoint of its guidance to reach $600 million. That result would bring full-year 2026 revenue to about $2 billion, compared with $1.57 billion in 2025.

Silicon Photonics Drives Growth Plans

Tower said silicon photonics revenue totaled approximately $240 million in the third quarter, representing an annualized rate near $1 billion. Ellwanger said the company expects its fourth-quarter silicon photonics annualized run rate to exceed $1.1 billion.

→ MarketBeat Week in Review – 10/26 - 10/30

Aeluma's Market Is Laser-Focused on Fresh Highs—Here's Why

The company is expanding silicon photonics production across four manufacturing sites to meet demand from customers serving AI-related optical interconnect markets. Tower expects year-end capacity to be about double the level that supported third-quarter silicon photonics revenue, with the additional capacity intended to support a revenue ramp during the first and second quarters of 2027.

Story Continues

Tower is also advancing its Track-1 300-millimeter expansion in Japan. Ellwanger said all tools for the expansion have been ordered and scheduled, with full production starts targeted for the third quarter of 2027. Including that expansion, the company expects silicon photonics start capacity to reach three times the level supporting third-quarter shipments.

→ 3 Robotics ETFs, 3 Different Ways to Bet on Humanoid Robots

Management said that capacity is substantially covered through signed agreements and contracts in advanced negotiation stages. Customer commitments now extend into 2029, when Tower expects its Track-2 expansion in Japan to be underway. The company said its planned expansions will continue to be self-funded.

In response to an analyst question, Ellwanger said capacity expected by the third quarter of 2027 could support a silicon photonics run rate "somewhere a bit above a $2.8 billion" on a start-rate basis. He noted that figure does not include potential revenue from integrated laser products and other initiatives.

New Product Opportunities

Tower highlighted growing customer activity around near-packaged optics, or NPO, a technology that can more tightly integrate optical and electrical functions than conventional pluggable transceivers. The company said it is prototyping NPO products with more than 10 top customers and expects NPO products to carry a higher initial average selling price than pluggable products.

Ellwanger said the company expects an "appreciable amount" of NPO shipments in the second half of 2027, though the timing will depend on market adoption. Tower's NPO customers are currently a subset of its existing pluggable-transceiver customer base, he said.

The company also discussed heterogeneous integration efforts, including initial production for NewPhotonics using indium phosphide laser chiplets attached to silicon photonics wafers. Tower said it is deploying similar die-to-wafer attachment techniques with materials including thin-film lithium niobate for next-generation 400-gigabit-per-lane products.

President Marco Racanelli said Tower expects competition in the expanding silicon photonics and silicon germanium markets, but cited the company's production yields, customer relationships and technology roadmap as factors supporting its position. He said customers have extended long-term agreements through 2029, providing visibility into future capacity requirements.

Other Businesses and Utilization

Beyond optical technologies, Tower reported its highest quarterly RF-SOI revenue to date from its 300-millimeter Agrate, Italy, production corridor. The company also recorded a new high in product tape-outs for Fab 10, which serves its RF-SOI business.

Demand for Tower's BCD technologies grew about 10% year over year, according to Ellwanger, supported by AI and cloud data-center applications as well as mobile and automotive markets. Several strategic customers have entered long-term agreements at higher average selling prices, with Tower forecasting blended BCD pricing in 2027 to be 20% above 2026 levels.

In image sensors and displays, Tower began production of a high-speed global shutter sensor for high-end video cameras and said it is preparing capacity for expected customer demand in OLED-on-silicon displays during 2027.

All of Tower's 200-millimeter fabs operated at utilization rates of 85% to 90% during the third quarter, while its 300-millimeter fab remained fully utilized and above the company's 85% utilization model.

Margins, Capital Spending and Long-Term Model

Chief Financial Officer Oren Shirazi said gross profit increased 92% year over year to a record $179 million, while operating profit rose 2.5 times from the prior-year period to $127 million.

Tower is executing a previously announced $920 million capital investment program for silicon photonics and silicon germanium capacity and capabilities across facilities in Israel, Newport Beach, Texas and Japan. About 65% of the investment had been paid through the third quarter, with the remaining 35% expected to be paid in the fourth quarter of 2026 and the first half of 2027.

Shirazi said Tower expects a full return on investment from the $920 million program within one year. He added that quarterly incremental gross margin of roughly 62% was elevated because not all new equipment had begun depreciation, and reiterated a longer-term expectation for incremental gross profit margins of 55% to 58%.

The company updated its long-term financial model to target annual revenue of $3.6 billion, gross profit of $1.63 billion and operating profit of $1.38 billion. The model calls for annual net profit of $1.2 billion, representing a 33% net margin, based on assumptions including 85% fab utilization after planned capacity installations and qualifications are completed.

About Tower Semiconductor (NASDAQ:TSEM)

Tower Semiconductor Ltd. is an Israeli specialty semiconductor foundry that manufactures integrated circuits for fabless semiconductor companies, integrated device manufacturers and system companies. The company provides process technologies and production services rather than selling branded end-user electronics.

Its offerings include analog and mixed-signal technologies, radio-frequency and high-voltage circuits, power management solutions, image sensors, and specialty memory products.

news.Title: 1 of Greg Abel's Favorite Stocks and a Top 5 Berkshire Hathaway Holding Just Suffered a Devastating Decline
news.Content:
In Greg Abel's 10 months as CEO of Berkshire Hathaway , arguably his most notable move has been loading up on Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG)(NASDAQ: GOOGL) stock.

While former Berkshire CEO Warren Buffett acknowledged that he initiated the position last year, Abel has purchased tens of billions worth of stock this year and built it into a top five position, with Alphabet consuming 8.2% of Berkshire's massive roughly $364 billion portfolio.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

While it has generated strong gains for shareholders in recent years, Alphabet stock just experienced its worst single-day decline in history.

What set the market ablaze with fear?

Following the release of its third-quarter results, Alphabet's shares fell roughly 12.3% on Oct. 29, marking the stock's worst single-day performance ever.

It was a double miss for Alphabet, as the company reported adjusted earnings per share of $2.67, well below the $3.02 expected by Wall Street analysts. Revenue of nearly $127.6 billion missed consensus estimates of $128.2 billion.

Revenue was still up 25% year over year, while cloud revenue more than doubled, showing that artificial intelligence adoption is benefiting certain parts of the business.

However, free cash flow deteriorated worse than the Street expected. Negative free cash flow came in at over $9 billion, while analysts had modeled negative $2.7 billion.

But the real concerns stemmed from how AI may be cutting into one of Alphabet's largest businesses that has made the company what it is today. Google services revenue, which includes Search, YouTube advertising, subscriptions, and more, came in at $96.3 billion, more than $2 billion below analysts' forecasts.

Search revenue also appears to be slowing, with year-over-year growth of 12% in the quarter, down from 19% in the first quarter and 17% in the second quarter.

While several factors impacted search revenue, such as foreign exchange fluctuations, Alphabet's chief business officer, Philipp Schindler, also noted that "that the strong growth in AI Mode queries had an impact because of the lower monetization we were seeing in AI Mode."

This has investors spooked about the overall ramifications for search from AI, as search is the company's largest revenue line item and Google previously controlled a 90% market share in the traditional search market.

Story Continues

According to MarketWatch, J.P. Morgan analyst Doug Anmuth said the "results and the stock's sharp move lower show us the margin for error when a hyperscaler spending hundreds of billions on the AI infrastructure build-out and flipping to negative [free cash flow] posts disappointing results in the core."

Although Alphabet remains a leader in AI and its models are considered among the best, the space is highly competitive, and Alphabet likely won't be able to dominate the large language model (LLM) realm as it did with search.

BNP Paribas analyst Nick Jones wrote in a research note that investors are also worried that AI agents could cut into Google's advertising revenue if the agents are doing browsing and online shopping instead of people.

I also believe it's concerning that queries in AI Mode are more difficult to monetize.

Are Buffett and Abel wrong?

The rough day may make investors wonder if Abel and Buffett were wrong about Alphabet. After all, while Buffett will likely go down in history as the greatest investor ever, even the Oracle of Omaha makes mistakes.

Still, one concerning quarter is not enough to make a call, as nobody can say for certain what will happen. Alphabet still owns many strong, fast-growing businesses, including Google Cloud, YouTube, and Waymo.

Furthermore, Alphabet's Gemini models still hold significant market share, so they should continue to benefit from AI adoption.

But on days like Oct. 29, it's important for all investors, even the greats at Berkshire Hathaway, to step back and consider the scenarios that could play out with AI. If it does make traditional search irrelevant, where does that leave Alphabet? Or what if AI is simply difficult to monetize?

There are no easy answers, but AI is moving fast, so you can't sit around and hope things simply work out for the best.

news.Title: Oracle stock slides as it borrows another $10 billion for AI spending
news.Content:
Five days after Oracle (ORCL) promised to rein in its fundraising, it raised the full $20 billion in a single day.

Oracle kicked off a $10 billion bond sale Monday and, at the same time, filed to sell $10 billion of stock . Together, that's every dollar of new debt and stock it said at last week's investor day it would raise through fiscal 2030.

Investors didn't love the speed. Oracle stock fell as much as 6.5% to its lowest level since July, while Microsoft ( MSFT ), Amazon ( AMZN ), and Alphabet ( GOOGL ) rose. That wiped out what was left of last week's 11% investor-day pop.

It's been a rough year. Oracle has lost more than half its value over the past 12 months, while Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, and Meta ( META ) are not too far from where they started.

So is Oracle Big Tech's canary in the coal mine? Not really.

The company's big drops haven't been an early warning for the rest of the group. After Oracle's nine previous three-day plunges of 12% or more since 2016, Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, and Meta fell over the following month only four times, by Yahoo Finance's calculations. And at the tops of the dot-com bubble in 2000 and the pandemic boom in 2021, Oracle peaked after the Nasdaq, not before.

What sets Oracle apart is how it pays for the AI build-out. Follow the debt.

Oracle burned through about $24 billion in cash in its last fiscal year. It owed about $125 billion as of August, nearly twice its shareholders' equity , roughly what would be left for shareholders after its debts were paid. Monday's bonds add $10 billion more.

Lenders have noticed. It costs about five times as much to insure Oracle's debt against default as Microsoft's, using credit default swaps — contracts that work like insurance, paying out if a company stops paying its debts.

Futurum CEO Daniel Newman called Microsoft "the AI adults in the room, the company that's really done this with the least collateral damage to their balance sheet" on Yahoo Finance last week.

Oracle also pays more to borrow. Its bonds due 2066 yield about 8.4% — the yearly return a buyer locks in at today's price — compared with about 6.1% for Apple's and Microsoft's bonds due 2062, according to a BofA note cited by The Market Ear. CoreWeave ( CRWV ), a debt-heavy AI cloud provider, pays more than 14%.

The credit raters are giving Oracle the benefit of the doubt, for now.

Fitch kept Oracle's BBB credit rating , two notches above junk , and said in a statement Monday that "following this capital raise, Fitch does not expect Oracle to raise material incremental capital over the rating horizon." Moody's affirmed its rating too but kept its outlook at negative, a sign a downgrade is still possible.

Story Continues

Oracle isn't the only one tapping lenders. Alphabet sold euro bonds Monday for the second time this year. And BofA economists warned Monday that a lasting AI sell-off is one of the biggest risks to the economy , adding that all that AI borrowing is part of why interest rates are up.

Fitch thinks Oracle is done asking, for now. Lenders are still charging like they're not so sure.

news.Title: Apple Q4 earnings live: iPhone 18 sales in the spotlight
news.Content:
Apple ( AAPL ) will report its fourth quarter earnings after the bell today, providing investors with a glimpse of early iPhone 18 Pro sales.

The iPhone Duo went up for preorder on Oct. 16 and went on sale Oct. 23, missing Apple's fiscal Q4, though the company could still offer color on demand.

This will also be Apple's first earnings call with new CEO John Ternus , who took over the role from Tim Cook on Sept. 1.

For the quarter, Apple is expected to report earnings per share (EPS) of $2 on revenue of $113.46 billion, according to Bloomberg analyst consensus estimates. The company saw EPS of $1.85 and revenue of $102.46 billion in the same period last year.

Apple's iPhone sales are projected to hit $56.48 billion, up 15% year over year. Services, the company's second-largest segment, is set to top $31.58 billion in revenue, while the company's Mac business is expected to see sales of $9.69 billion.

news.Title: ETFs to Watch as Amazon Shares Slip Following Q3 Earnings Miss
news.Content:
Shares of Amazon.com AMZN slipped 1.4% in the last trading session, recovering from a plunge of more than 6% in after-hours trading on Oct. 29, following the release of its third-quarter results. The tech giant's rising free cash outflow marred the AWS unit's fastest sales growth of 39.3% in nearly five years, a tension directly reflected in the stock's volatility.

Amazon also failed to meet Wall Street's expectations on both top and bottom-line fronts, further fueling investors' skepticism.

Nevertheless, soaring sales growth in AMZN's cloud segment, combined with a steady full-year capital expenditure outlook, offered a temporary breather to market participants, helping the stock recover some losses by Friday's close.

While some investors might see this dip as an opportune moment to invest in Amazon stock, others wary of its growing free cash outflow might not want direct exposure.

For them, exchange-traded funds (ETFs) with Amazon among their top holdings offer a strategic middle ground. Exposure to such funds enables investors to capture AMZN's upside while benefiting from a diversified basket of assets.

But before diving into the specifics of these ETFs, let us take a closer look at how the world's largest e-commerce platform performed in the third quarter across other key metrics.

A Brief Analysis of AMZN's Q3 Results

Amazon's third-quarter earnings of $1.89 missed the consensus estimate by 6%. Sales missed the consensus mark by a whisker.  On a year-over-year basis, the company's earnings dropped 3.1%, while its sales grew 12%.

The company's advertising business delivered solid growth in the third quarter, with revenues increasing 12% year over year.

Its grocery business is also delivering solid growth, with fresh groceries and everyday essentials growing about 3x faster than the rest of the store and representing about half of all units sold in the third quarter.

As customers continue migrating to the cloud and expanding their use of Amazon Web Services ("AWS") core offerings, the segment's annualized revenue run rate reached $184 billion at the end of the third quarter.

Beyond standard cloud infrastructure, Amazon's custom silicon segment is gaining significant traction, posting triple-digit percentage revenue growth year over year. Revenue commitments for its proprietary Graviton and Trainium chips have surged more than 20-fold in the reported quarter compared to the prior-year period.

Amazon expects net sales for the fourth quarter to be in the band of $240-$247 billion, including an estimated 60 basis point foreign exchange headwind. The midpoint of this sales guidance, $243.5 billion, lies below the consensus estimate of $245.13 billion.

Story Continues

To this end, it is imperative to mention that Amazon expects fourth-quarter 2026 profitability to be impacted by Project Kuiper (Leo), as most initial production and launch costs will continue to be expensed during the quarter, contrary to its earlier expectations. Despite the expense timing, the commercial satellite service remains on track to launch initial operations before the end of the year.

news.Title: 美股這波快跌完了？大摩：這個指數六成股票已跌過兩成
news.Content:
摩根士丹利(MS-US)認為，美股自6月展開的修正已接近尾聲。該行指出，羅素3000指數成分股中，已有六成自6月以來一度回檔至少20%，近期標普500指數也開始補跌。這類個股先跌、大盤指數隨後跟進的走勢，通常出現在修正後段。11月3日美國期中選舉結果出爐後，市場可望排除一項主要不確定因素。

摩根士丹利美股首席策略師Michael Wilson領軍的團隊周一(2日)表示，接近年底之際，若選舉等不確定因素陸續消退，先前估值下修、基本面仍佳的景氣循環股，可望為布局2027年的投資人提供加碼機會。

近期賣壓集中在科技股。市場擔心AI企業財報可能引發更大範圍的修正，以科技股為主的那斯達克100指數10月市值蒸發數兆美元，一度逼近修正區間。Wilson也從這波財報看見市場評價企業的方式正在改變：投資人過去往往願意容忍自由現金流不如預期，如今更在意企業能否持續獲利，以及帳面獲利能否真正轉化為現金。他認為，這種轉變符合經濟循環進入中後期的特徵。

就選舉而言，摩根士丹利指出，從歷史經驗來看，美國大型股在期中選舉結果揭曉後的六個月，漲幅通常約為15%。該行認為，投資人已將民主黨拿下參眾兩院的情境反映在價格中，較值得留意的是選後政策風險，包括美國與伊朗的軍事衝突可能再度升高，或美方推出新關稅。

Wilson預期，聯準會(Fed)不會急於降息或採取其他措施支撐市場。短期資金面的助力可能來自美國財政部：若財政部動用現金支付政府支出，其現金餘額可望從約1.05兆美元降至年底的8,500億美元，為市場挹注流動性。

news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Phillip Securities upgraded Amazon ( NASDAQ:AMZN ) to Buy from Accumulate on Monday and raised its price target from $320 to $330, arguing that demand for Amazon Web Services justifies the company's heavier spending. Amazon shares were up 5.22% as of 10:30 a.m. ET.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 4 Warning Signs with AMZN.

Is AMZN fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Analyst Helena Wang raised her fiscal 2027 revenue estimate by 2% and her net income forecast by 3%, citing AWS's strong growth. She lifted her 2027 capital expenditure estimate by 3% as well. The firm conceded that aggressive spending puts pressure on free cash flow, but it said strong demand visibility supports continued infrastructure investment. It also pointed to Amazon's model-agnostic approach to AI, its custom chips and its partnerships with large language model providers.

The case leans on last week's numbers. Amazon reported third-quarter net sales of $201.9 billion, up 12%, while AWS sales rose 39.3% to $46.0 billion, the unit's fastest growth in nearly five years. Operating income reached $28.1 billion, a 13.9% margin and the highest in the company's history. Net income still fell to $20.7 billion, or $1.89 per diluted share, because the year-ago quarter included $9.5 billion of pre-tax gains from Amazon's Anthropic investment. For the fourth quarter, Amazon guided to net sales of $240 billion to $247 billion and operating income of $28.5 billion to $33.5 billion.

news.Title: Microsoft Just Revealed a $677 Billion Reason to Buy Its Stock
news.Content:
Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) hit a fresh 52-week low in June, but the company has outperformed the broader equity market ever since. And by the looks of it, Microsoft's run may continue at least a little while longer. The company recently reported its first-quarter 2027 update, and it was impressive. Microsoft gave investors plenty more reasons to buy the stock. Here's what you need to know.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

An excellent quarterly update

Before looking at the numbers, let's review why Microsoft did not perform well through the first half of the year. Some investors think that artificial intelligence (AI) will disrupt the software industry and replace many services offered by software companies, such as Microsoft.

Some recent developments support that view. For instance, a single developer used AI to clone several legacy products in the Microsoft Productivity suite, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint, as well as products from other major software companies, such as Adobe (NASDAQ:ADBE). These knock-offs weren't fully functional. Still, it's quite a remarkable achievement, and it highlights why some people are worried about Microsoft's future.

The cost of developing software has fallen rapidly thanks to AI, which puts the company at risk. However, so far, Microsoft's financial results suggest that it is doing just fine. In the first quarter of its fiscal year 2027, which ended on Sept. 30, Microsoft's revenue of $92.3 billion increased by 19% year over year. Microsoft's operating income grew 21% year over year to $45.9 billion, while its non-GAAP net earnings per share were $4.89, up 18% year over year.

Microsoft debuted a new reporting structure with two segments this quarter. The first, Agents and Infra, did most of the heavy lifting. Revenue from this unit was $76.8 billion, up 25% year over year. Microsoft Cloud revenue jumped 30% year over year to $63.9 billion, while Azure revenue grew 48% year over year to $33.2 billion. Microsoft's results beat analyst estimates. But is there more growth ahead for the company?

There is more where that came from

One important metric for Microsoft is remaining performance obligations (RPO), or the amount of contracted revenue that hasn't yet been recognized. This metric indicates demand -- or lack thereof -- for the company's services. By the end of the first quarter of fiscal year 2027, Microsoft had $677 billion in RPO within its Agents and Infra business. Note that this figure grew by 73% year over year.

Story Continues

This suggests that AI is not displacing Microsoft's products. Even if the cost of making the kinds of products it has offered for decades has fallen dramatically, there are several advantages for Microsoft. First, it is offering new products that still cost quite a bit.

Microsoft offers various AI services through its cloud business, and supporting these products requires substantial investments in AI infrastructure. Second, reproducing a basic knockoff of some of Microsoft's products isn't the same as replacing these products. Millions of businesses have been using Word, Excel, and other Microsoft software services for decades.

These are deeply integrated into the day-to-day workflow of these companies. It's not so easy to switch to a clone. In other words, Microsoft benefits from a wide moat thanks to high switching costs and deep, long-standing relationships with enterprises. Third, Microsoft is integrating various AI features into its services, making them more powerful and even harder to replace.

There is another important advantage here. Microsoft has direct lines of communication with businesses and access to massive amounts of data, which can help the company determine the best way to improve its services with AI. A single skilled developer cannot easily replicate these advantages, and neither can most major corporations other than Microsoft.

So, despite the threat from AI, Microsoft's business remains strong, and the company is riding a tailwind in AI and cloud computing that may persist for a long time. Microsoft's shares are still worth investing in.

news.Title: 台股10月震到心驚　法人買盤竟藏在這10檔！
news.Content: 市場呈現高檔震盪格局之際，市場資金則流向主動式ETF，根據證交所資料，10月以來三大法人買超前十大有過半為主動式ETF，顯示在波動格局，由經理人主動操作的主動ETF更受資金青睞。10月的投資市場很不平靜，先是從月初一路向上至6日、創下49822.55的收盤新高價，隨後指數在8個交易日內修正約7%，甚至外資及陸資在15日單日賣超達3,025.55億元，創下台股有紀錄以來最大單日賣超。 進一步觀察三大法人買超前十大主動式ETF，國內及海外主題各半。其中，在10月初的台股加權指數向上波段，主動凱基台灣(00407A)、主動復華未來50(00991A)，及主動第一金台股優(00994A)以逾6%的含息報酬率成為追漲前段班；而在整個風雨10月中，主動安聯美國科技(00402A)及主動凱基台灣(00407A)則以低於-4%的績效表現、成為抗波動首選。 雖然近期部分主動式ETF面臨三大法人調節，但從10月以來的資金流向來看，法人買盤仍不時回流主動式ETF，顯示資金並未因短線波動而全面撤出，反而有逢回布局的跡象。不過10月以來投資市場呈現先漲後跌，正好是投資人檢視投資標的在快速波動下，是否能追漲抗跌的良機。 10月以來的股市回檔屬於評價與籌碼的調整，主動凱基台灣(00407A)ETF研究團隊表示，不是景氣的轉折，不僅台廠出口額持續創新高，9月美國聯準會也上修經濟成長率至2.3%，代表目前基本面無太大警訊。 建議投資人關注10月下旬召開的美國聯準會利率會議、10月底將接力登場的大型雲端業者財報，以及我國財政部每月公布的出口總額；只要指數未有效跌破季線、企業獲利預估未下修，回檔可視為分批布局的良機，惟投資人仍須衡量自身風險承受度。

news.Title: Why Amazon Stock Rallied Monday Morning
news.Content:
Shares of Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) rallied on Monday, adding as much as 5.6%. As of 11:52 a.m. ET, the stock was still up 4.6%.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

The catalyst that sent the e-commerce and cloud computing specialist higher was a vote of confidence from Wall Street after last week's slump.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

You gotta spend money to make money

Phillip Securities analyst Helena Wang upgraded Amazon stock to buy from accumulate (a step above hold), while raising her price target to $330 per share, up from $320. The analyst points to the company's "strong demand visibility" for its cloud services and its growing suite of artificial intelligence (AI) offerings.

Amazon stock dove last week when the company reported its Q3 results and reiterated its plans to increase its capital expenditures (capex) to $220 billion for 2026. Perhaps as importantly, CEO Andy Jassy said Amazon expects to spend "meaningfully more in 2027," to capitalize on the opportunity represented by AI. That pronouncement, combined with negative free cash flow of $42 billion, gave investors pause and sent the stock plunging.

Spending on AI continues to escalate with no end in sight, and some investors wonder if Amazon will be able to recoup that heavy spending with higher future revenue. Jassy addressed this on the earnings call and said the company has "even more conviction" than before that these investments in Amazon Web Services (AWS) and AI "will yield a much larger revenue and free cash flow-generating business."

We've seen this movie before. There have been numerous times in Amazon's past when the company spent heavily to capture an opportunity -- AWS, fulfillment, same-day delivery, etc. In each case, that spending resulted in higher revenue and a stronger business. I have no reason to believe this time will be any different.

And at 20 times earnings, Amazon's valuation sits near an all-time low, allowing savvy investors to profit from the sell-off.

That makes Amazon stock a buy.

Price Decline Still Elevated Valuation

Hold ARM Stock Ahead of Q2 Earnings

Arm Holdings' strong position in semiconductor architecture, growing adoption of energy-efficient chip designs and increasing exposure to artificial intelligence present attractive long-term growth opportunities. Rising demand for advanced computing solutions and continued momentum in royalty and licensing businesses should support its prospects. However, ARM's elevated valuation, despite the recent share price decline, remains a concern. Moreover, the absence of a favorable earnings beat prediction limits near-term optimism. Although ARM's growth potential remains promising, its premium valuation leaves little room for disappointment. Given these mixed factors, existing investors should retain ARM shares, while prospective investors may await a more attractive entry point.

Story Continues

How Do NVIDIA and Intel Compare With ARM?

NVIDIA NVDA represents an important comparison given its leadership in AI accelerators and data-center computing. NVIDIA benefits from demand for GPUs that power AI training and inference, while Arm provides CPU architectures that support complementary computing workloads. NVIDIA's established AI ecosystem highlights the scale of infrastructure opportunities available to semiconductor companies.

Intel INTC offers another useful comparison as Arm expands into higher-performance CPUs. Intel maintains an established presence in processors for personal computers and data centers, making its competitive positioning relevant to Arm's expansion strategy. However, Intel's manufacturing-intensive operations differ substantially from Arm's traditional intellectual property licensing model, creating different profitability and capital requirements.

news.Title: Meta Stock Slips as S&P Delivers Stark Warning Over AI Spending
news.Content:

Meta Platforms ( META ) shares slipped 0.5% in morning trading after S&P Global Ratings shifted its outlook on the company to negative from stable, citing uncertainty surrounding its AI spending plans and future cash generation.

The revised assessment raises questions about whether Meta can moderate its capital investments as it pursues a multiyear expansion of AI infrastructure. S&P said the spending program has complicated its assessment of when investment levels may ease and how much free operating cash flow the company can preserve.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 4 Warning Sign with XOM.

The agency also flagged an increase in Meta's financial leverage. The measure climbed from approximately 0.1 times in 2025, with much of the increase associated with leasing data center capacity rather than taking on new debt.

news.Title: FOXA Q1 Earnings & Revenues Surpass Estimates, Both Increase Y/Y
news.Content:
Fox Corporation FOXA reported adjusted earnings of $2.54 per share for the first quarter of fiscal 2027, up 68.2% year over year. The figure topped the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $1.99 by 27.64%, supported by World Cup broadcasts and higher political advertising.

Revenues climbed 22.3% year over year to $4.57 billion, surpassing the $4.23 billion Zacks Consensus Estimate by 8.01%. Companywide advertising revenues rose 47.4%, with Tubi's digital growth adding to demand from sports and election-related programming.

FOXA's Revenue Mix Shifts Toward Advertising

Distribution revenues increased 8.8% year over year to $2.08 billion from $1.92 billion. They accounted for 45.6% of total revenues, down from 51.2% a year earlier as advertising became a larger contributor to the sales mix.

Advertising brought in $2.08 billion, representing 45.5% of total revenues against 37.8% a year ago. Content and other revenues fell 1.2% to $406 million from $411 million, contributing 8.9% of consolidated sales.

Fox Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Fox Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Fox Corporation Quote

Fox's Cable Networks Post Higher Revenues

Cable Network Programming revenues grew 8.5% to $1.80 billion from $1.66 billion in the year-ago quarter. Distribution sales climbed 10.1% to $1.20 billion, reflecting contractual price increases and a rise in the average number of subscribers.

Advertising revenues rose 8.1% to $373 million, driven by sports advertising related to the World Cup, partly offset by weaker digital news advertising. Content and other revenues advanced 1.3% to $230 million. Cable segment EBITDA improved 7.4% to $859 million, although higher sports rights amortization, production expenses and news programming costs tempered profit growth. The segment's EBITDA margin edged down to 47.6% from 48.1%.

FOXA's Television Segment Powers Q1

Television revenues climbed 32.3% year over year to $2.71 billion from $2.05 billion. Advertising revenues reached $1.71 billion, up 60.1%, benefiting from World Cup broadcasts, political ad spending and continued digital growth led by Tubi.

Television distribution revenues grew 3.5% to $850 million, supported by higher average rates at owned-and-operated stations and increased subscriber counts. Content and other revenues declined 4.3% to $155 million due to lower entertainment content revenues. Segment EBITDA surged 134.1% to $934 million despite elevated sports rights and digital content costs. Lower NFL expenses tied to the timing of games provided a partial offset. The segment's EBITDA margin expanded to 34.4% from 19.5%.

Story Continues

Fox's Operating Costs Trail Sales Growth

Operating expenses rose 11.4% year over year to $2.36 billion, reflecting higher sports programming rights amortization and production costs alongside increased digital content spending. However, operating expenses as a percentage of revenues declined to 51.7% from 56.7% in the prior-year quarter.

Selling, general and administrative expenses grew 2.7% to $567 million, while their share of revenues contracted to 12.4% from 14.8%. Total adjusted EBITDA increased 54.1% to $1.64 billion, lifting the adjusted EBITDA margin to 35.9% from 28.5%.

GAAP net income rose 57.1% to $957 million. Net income attributable to stockholders increased to $943 million from $599 million, while GAAP earnings per share rose to $2.20 from $1.32. Adjusted net income attributable to stockholders totaled $1.09 billion, compared with $686 million a year ago.

FOXA's Operating Cash Flow Turns Positive

Operating activities generated $616 million in cash, reversing a $130 million outflow a year earlier. Changes in inventories net of programming payable used $567 million of cash, compared with $525 million in the prior-year period. Changes in receivables and other assets used another $192 million, versus $437 million a year ago.

Property and equipment spending totaled $113 million versus $104 million a year earlier. Net cash used in investing activities narrowed to $139 million from $255 million, while cash used in financing activities fell to $146 million from $598 million. Fox made no share repurchases during the quarter compared with $250 million in the year-ago period.

Fox's Liquidity and Management Commentary

As of Sept. 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents totaled $4.54 billion, up from $4.21 billion at June 30. Borrowings were $6.61 billion, essentially unchanged from fiscal year-end. Total assets rose to $23.09 billion from $22.48 billion, while stockholders' equity increased to $12.47 billion from $11.63 billion.

Chief executive officer Lachlan Murdoch highlighted first-quarter records for revenues and adjusted EBITDA. He cited the kickoff of college football and NFL seasons and pointed to contributions from across the company's businesses. Murdoch also emphasized ongoing momentum and a thoughtful, disciplined approach to delivering shareholder value.

news.Title: Analysis-October dive for AI-related shares tests broader US stock market's resilience
news.Content:
By Lewis Krauskopf

NEW YORK, Nov 2 (Reuters) - A steep decline in the prices of US AI and technology stocks is testing investors' enthusiasm to shift into other equity areas, a rotation that has propped up broader indexes in recent weeks.

Disappointing results from Alphabet, Amazon and Intel dealt the latest blow to the AI trade. Investors ‌worry about the hefty financing needed to fund massive investment spending. They are also starting to question whether returns will be robust enough to justify that spending.

The broader ‌market in October held up far better than tech- and AI-exposed equities did, but it may not be able to endure a more severe pullback in the massive AI trade. The tech sector alone accounts for a 38% weight in the ​S&P 500.

Investors are wary of signs that the selling will spread. A main alarm would be indications that the AI hyperscalers pull back significantly on spending plans. Their investment in data centers and other infrastructure has been a key driver for overall economic growth.

"You can have a month of a significant shift in leadership and tech weakness and relative strength in everything else," said Mark Hackett, chief market strategist for Nationwide. However, "if you have another month of (a steep) drop ... it's so big that mathematically it's difficult, but I think even more importantly, psychologically it's difficult."

Friday's action illustrated such worries. A whopping 4.2% drop ‌on the day for the tech sector, which included a nearly ⁠29% tumble for Intel, drove a 1.8% decline for the S&P 500.

For October, the S&P 500 tech sector slid 6.8%, its biggest monthly drop since March 2025. Yet nine of the S&P 500's 11 sectors gained in October — allowing the benchmark index to end with a monthly decline of less ⁠than 1%.

ROTATIONS BETWEEN AI AND EVERYTHING ELSE

The S&P 500 is up more than 10% so far in 2026. Yet rotations have been a theme for the past year. Leadership has often vacillated between heavyweight tech and AI stocks on one hand, and a broader group of sectors on the other.

September, for example, showed opposite trends to October, with dominance that month from tech and AI stocks.

"This year has been unbelievably stable at ​the ​index level," Hackett said. "But there's so much volatility beneath the surface."

October trading indicated a sign of broadening. Despite ​sharp declines in AI names, more than 70% of S&P 500 constituents ‌were up on the month. Indexes representing small- and mid-cap stocks also rose in October.

"Both corporate and consumer fundamentals remain healthy," said Angelo Kourkafas, senior global investment strategist at Edward Jones. "In this backdrop, investors want to maintain equity exposure. But now they want to reduce AI concentration risk and are adding to areas that offer differentiated sources of return."

Story Continues

AI SPENDING IN FOCUS FOR BROADER FALLOUT

That desire to maintain equity exposure could be challenged in the near term, if the AI theme falters more severely.

AI investment spending has not only driven profits for semiconductors and companies involved in building data centers, it has also been central to overall US economic growth.

If big tech companies "start pulling back on capex, which has supported economic growth, it has boosted earnings across many different areas of ‌the economy — that can be something that may be more impactful in terms of driving a broader risk-off ​sentiment," Kourkafas said.

Oxford Economics estimates that about one-third of recent US economic growth stems from AI. That includes the ​net impact of direct investment to support expansion of AI infrastructure as well as some ​contribution from the wealth effect from stock market gains that has lifted consumer spending.

"The consumer is fine, but the consumer isn't the reason the economy ‌looks good. The economy looks good because of AI," said Marta Norton, chief ​investment strategist at retirement and wealth services provider ​Empower. "So you start pulling the rug out from under AI in an actual meaningful way, I think that changes the dynamics for the markets."

Meanwhile, the market action could start to cause broader worry. The S&P 500 on Friday closed below its 100-day moving average — a medium-term trendline — for the first time since April.

While the index has bounced off that ​trendline several times in the past two years, "when it has broken ‌below ... in any material way, it was followed by a much further drop over the following weeks," said Matthew Maley, chief market strategist at Miller Tabak.

"If the major ​averages begin to drop in a more compelling manner, it is very likely that investors will stop rotating into other sectors ... and start rotating into cash," Maley ​said in a note on Friday.

(Reporting by Lewis Krauskopf; Editing by Megan Davies and David Gregorio)

Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) Amazon ( AMZN ) is the leading e-commerce company, with operating sprawling across North America and the globe. After gaining a dominant position in the North American e-commerce market, Amazon is applying its winning blueprint internationally. Amazon Has a Durable Business

Although most investors think of the e-commerce business when they think of Amazon, the company has successfully diversified its revenue stream across several high-growth businesses. Amazon Delivers Dependable Growth

While many stocks can deliver the occasional double-digit revenue growth quarter or year, Amazon has done it consistently. Revenues have grown each year over the past 5 years and are expected to be close to $1 trillion next year.

Last week, Amazon staged a classic high-volume bear trap/shakeout after briefly crashing below the 200-day moving average and recovering it.

Amazon's dominant market presence across cloud computing, global e-commerce, and emerging AI infrastructure positions it as a resilient long-term growth driver. news.Title: What's Going on with Alphabet Stock? 3 Things Investors Should Know
news.Content:
Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOGL) delivered another quarter of impressive revenue growth. Its third-quarter 2026 revenue increased 25% year over year to $127.6 billion. Google Cloud more than doubled its revenue, while Google Search continued to grow.

Yet, Alphabet shares came under pressure following the earnings announcement. Investors are increasingly concerned about the company's advertising business and the enormous amount of money it is spending on artificial intelligence.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

So, what's happening with Alphabet? Here are three things investors should understand.

Google's advertising business faces challenge.

Google's advertising business remains its biggest revenue contributor. In the third quarter, Google Search generated $63.4 billion, an increase of 12% from a year earlier. YouTube advertising revenue grew 9% to $11.2 billion.

These are respectable growth rates for businesses of this size. However, investors are increasingly questioning how artificial intelligence could change the economics of traditional search. Google is introducing AI-powered features that allow users to ask more complicated questions and receive comprehensive answers without visiting multiple websites. This makes Google Search more useful, but it also creates a monetization challenge.

During its latest earnings call, Google's management acknowledged that AI Mode queries currently generate less ad revenue than traditional Search queries. This contributed to the slowdown in Search advertising growth during the third quarter.

Google is working to address this by introducing more advertisements into AI-generated responses and expanding these features internationally. However, it remains to be seen whether AI-powered Search can eventually generate advertising revenue at the same rate as traditional Search.

For investors, the important question isn't simply whether people continue using Google. It's whether Google can continue making money from those searches.

Google Cloud is becoming a much bigger growth engine

While investors worry about Search, another part of Alphabet's business is gaining momentum. Google Cloud revenue increased 103% to $30.7 billion in the third quarter. Its operating income also increased substantially, exceeding $11 billion.

Demand for AI computing infrastructure and enterprise AI services is helping drive this growth. Businesses increasingly need computing power, data storage and access to advanced AI models. Google Cloud provides these services, giving Alphabet another opportunity to benefit from the AI boom.

Story Continues

Its cloud backlog also reached $561 billion, providing significant visibility into future demand. Management expects to recognise more than 55% of this backlog as revenue over the next 24 months. This is important because Alphabet is no longer relying entirely on advertising to drive its growth. Google Cloud could become another major source of revenue and profits over time.

However, strong revenue growth doesn't automatically translate into attractive investment returns. The company still needs to demonstrate that it can maintain its growth while generating healthy profits. So far, the numbers suggest it's moving in the right direction, with Google Cloud more than tripling its operating profit in the latest quarter.

Alphabet is spending enormous amounts on AI.

Perhaps the biggest concern is how much Alphabet is investing to compete in artificial intelligence. The company expects capital expenditures to range from $195 billion to $205 billion in 2026. Management also indicated that spending could increase substantially again next year.

These investments are going toward data centers, servers, networking equipment and other infrastructure needed to support growing AI demand. The spending is already affecting cash flow. Alphabet reported negative free cash flow of $9.1 billion in the third quarter as capital expenditures exceeded the cash generated from operations.

However, this doesn't necessarily mean the business is becoming less profitable. Operating income actually increased 30% to $40.6 billion, with operating margins improving to 32%.

Still, the enormous infrastructure spending deserves attention. Alphabet needs to demonstrate that these incremental investments will generate sufficient additional revenue and profits to justify the capital being deployed.

What should investors make of Alphabet?

Alphabet is undergoing an important transformation. Its traditional advertising business remains enormous, Google Cloud is growing rapidly, and its AI capabilities are creating new opportunities across the company.

However, the transition isn't without risks. AI could change how Google monetizes Search, while enormous infrastructure investments could put pressure on free cash flow.

For long-term investors, three things deserve attention: the resilience of Search advertising, the profitability of Google Cloud, and the returns Alphabet generates from its AI investments. They should keep an eye on all three of these in the coming quarters to track Alphabet's progress in transformation.

news.Title: Apple's iPhone faces a $190 memory problem
news.Content: Most people don't think about what's inside their phone. They think about the price on the box and whether the upgrade is worth it, and that's usually where the story ends. Apple has always made that math work in its favor. It charges premium prices, and it keeps a fat slice of every sale. I'm clearly not alone in relying on an iPhone every day. Apple (AAPL) has a customer base of more than 2.5 billion active devices, and its June-quarter revenue rose 16% to $109.4 billion, according to its July 30 earnings call. "This is the most powerful and most popular iPhone lineup we've ever had," said Tim Cook on that call, his last as CEO, as Six Colors reported in the transcript. However, a subtle shift has emerged inside the iPhone itself. The chips that store your photos and run your apps have gotten far more expensive. According to a Bank of America research report shared with TheStreet, rising memory costs could push Apple's gross margins well below what Wall Street expects, just as the company prepares to report earnings after the close on Monday, Nov. 2. What Bank of America's numbers show Apple already flagged the problem. Gross margin was 50.1% in the June quarter, including about two percentage points from tariff refunds. For the September quarter, Apple guided gross margin to "between 47 percent and 48 percent," said CFO Kevan Parekh. That includes about one point from tariff refunds. He said the drop to roughly 46.5% excluding tariff refunds "is really driven by memory." Cook was blunter. He called it "a hundred-year flood on the memory pricing" and said Apple "reluctantly raised prices." Bank of America analyst Wamsi Mohan put numbers on Cook's "flood" in an Oct. 30 note titled "Is consensus mis-modeling the staggered launch and risk to gross margins?" In his model, memory in an iPhone will cost about $245 in 2027, up from about $55. That's roughly 4.5 times as much, by my math. Related: MKBHD drops a blunt verdict on Apple's touchscreen MacBook Pro "We see a gross 900bps impact from memory on iPhone GMs which is netted down to a negative impact of 500bps based on price, mix, and cost actions," wrote Mohan. A basis point is one-hundredth of a percentage point, so 500 basis points is 5 points. By March, Mohan estimates total company gross margin at 43.6% to 44.6%, "much lower than current St. ests [Street estimates] (47.7%)." Why memory chips cost so much more The squeeze isn't unique to Apple. More Apple: MKBHD drops a blunt verdict on Apple's $1,999 iPhone Duo Apple's $1,999 iPhone Duo appears to have an app problem Apple cuts iPhone 18 Pro orders as AI raises the bill Story Continues Memory makers have shifted production toward chips for AI data centers. That has left less supply for phones and PCs. PC DRAM contract prices kept rising in the fourth quarter, though gains are narrowing, as suppliers cut PC memory output in favor of servers, according to TrendForce . TrendForce forecast that conventional DRAM contract prices would rise 10% to 15% in the fourth quarter from the third, Tech Insider reported. Apple has already passed some of that on to you. The base iPhone 17 now costs $899, up from $799, and the iPhone 17e, iPhone Air and iPhone 16 also rose $100, WhistleOut reported. Given that backdrop, it's easy to understand why Mohan thinks the Street is too optimistic. Even after those price hikes, his math says Apple can't fully offset the memory bill. Cook said in July that "primarily the DRAM market has three suppliers," which leaves even a buyer as big as Apple with limited bargaining power. Bank of America sees a lighter holiday quarter Mohan's bigger call is about timing. Apple launched the iPhone 18 Pro, Pro Max and Duo in September, but the base iPhone 18 and next iPhone Air won't arrive until early 2027. He expects that staggered launch to shift sales out of the holiday quarter. Mohan models December-quarter revenue of $135.7 billion, versus the $153 billion analysts expect. That's about $17 billion, or 11%, below consensus, by my math. A year ago, Apple's December quarter brought in $143.8 billion. "Customers would defer purchasing the base iPhone 17 (if they can) and either buy Pro… or wait for the iPhone 18 base model launch in 1H2027," wrote Mohan. He also flagged a slowdown in services. App Store revenue grew just 1.8% year over year in the September quarter, down from 3.8% in the June quarter, according to his note. Here's how Mohan's December-quarter estimates compare with Wall Street's, according to the note: Revenue: $135.7 billion vs. $153 billion iPhone revenue: $69.9 billion vs. $88.9 billion Gross margin: 45.6% vs. 46.6% Earnings per share: $2.59 vs. $2.93 Much will likely depend, however, on how fast memory prices cool and how many buyers wait for the cheaper iPhone 18. Mohan himself said his December numbers "could prove conservative." If that $190 hit applied to all 247 million iPhones Mohan expects Apple to sell in fiscal 2027, it would add about $47 billion in costs before price hikes and savings. I'd treat that as a ceiling, not a forecast. But it shows why a few points of margin matter so much at Apple's scale. Mohan still rates the stock a Buy with a $370 price target, about 6% above its $348.91 close on Oct. 30. "We view margin pressure as transitory and model higher margins starting end of F27 into F28," wrote Mohan. Related: Bank of America finds a quicker path to Apple's iPhone Duo This story was originally published by TheStreet on Nov 2, 2026, where it first appeared in the Technology section. news.Title: International Business Machines vs. Synopsys: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
news.Content:
As enterprises rush to integrate artificial intelligence, choosing between a legacy services giant and a specialized software provider is a difficult task for investors. Should you buy International Business Machines (NYSE:IBM) or Synopsys (NASDAQ:SNPS)?

International Business Machines is a leader in enterprise services, with a strong focus on hybrid cloud and consulting. In contrast, Synopsys provides the specialized software and intellectual property needed to design the chips powering modern computing. Both companies are central to the digital economy, yet they offer very different financial profiles and market exposures for you to consider.

The case for International Business Machines

International Business Machines focuses on providing software, consulting, and infrastructure solutions to a global client base. The company serves critical sectors like financial services and healthcare, helping them manage complex hybrid cloud environments. Its strategic ecosystem includes partners such as Adobe (NASDAQ:ADBE), Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN), Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT), Oracle (NYSE:ORCL), Palo Alto Networks (NASDAQ:PANW), Salesforce (NYSE:CRM), Samsung Electronics , and SAP (NYSE:SAP). Additionally, it maintains unique long-term relationships, such as its partnership with the United States Tennis Association.

In FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $67.5 billion, which was an increase of roughly 7.6% over the prior year. The company reported net income of approximately $10.6 billion for the same period. This resulted in a net margin of nearly 15.7%, a significant improvement over earlier years. These figures suggest that the transition toward higher-margin software and consulting services is having a tangible impact on the bottom line.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was nearly 2.1x, indicating a significant level of total debt relative to shareholder equity. The current ratio, which measures the ability to pay short-term obligations using assets expected to be converted to cash within a year, was approximately 0.9x. For the fiscal year ended in December 2025, the company generated free cash flow of roughly $12.1 billion. This cash generation, defined as cash from operations minus capital expenditures, supports its ability to fund operations and return capital to shareholders.

The case for Synopsys

In the competitive landscape of semiconductor stocks , Synopsys provides essential electronic design automation software and silicon intellectual property. Its tools are used by chip manufacturers and systems companies to design and test complex integrated circuits. The company has secured key relationships, including an intellectual property agreement with Amazon and a strategic partnership with OpenAI. Synopsys also utilizes a global network of channel partners to distribute its specialized engineering software to various vertical markets.

Story Continues

In FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $7.1 billion, representing a significant 15.1% increase over the previous year. The company reported net income of nearly $1.3 billion for the fiscal year. This resulted in a net margin of roughly 18.9%, reflecting the high profitability inherent in specialized software licensing. While revenue growth remains robust, the company continues to navigate the complexities of a changing semiconductor market.

As of its October 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was approximately 0.5x, suggesting a relatively conservative capital structure. The current ratio was roughly 1.6x, indicating a comfortable margin for meeting short-term financial obligations. For the fiscal year ended in October 2025, free cash flow was nearly $1.3 billion.

Note that stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 58.8% of Synopsys' operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation, since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

Image source: Getty Images.

Risk profile comparison

IBM faces intense competition in the hybrid cloud and artificial intelligence markets from rivals like Microsoft and Amazon. It depends heavily on research and development innovation to maintain its competitive edge and faces constant threats from cybersecurity incidents. Big Blue also faces risks related to integrating various acquisitions and potential goodwill impairments. Global regulatory pressures regarding data privacy and exposure to currency fluctuations add further layers of risk to its international operations.

Synopsys faces significant risks from its substantial debt burden following its merger with Ansys. The company is exposed to macroeconomic and geopolitical tensions, particularly regarding its operations in China and potential restrictions on technology exports. Revenue volatility is a constant concern due to its dependence on the cyclical semiconductor industry and competition from firms like Keysight Technologies (NYSE:KEYS). Furthermore, Synopsys is currently managing pending securities class action litigation related to the performance of its Design IP segment.

Valuation comparison

International Business Machines trades at a lower Forward P/E , based on future earnings estimates, and a lower P/S ratio, measuring market value against sales over the past twelve months.

Metric

International Business Machines

Forward P/E

Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

Which stock would I buy for 2027?

Spoiler alert: I have been an IBM shareholder since 2015, but I have never owned a share of Synopsys. After comparing the two companies head-to-head in November 2026, I'm not inspired to reverse that balance.

IBM is cheaper, more profitable, and pays a generous dividend. Its annual sales are an order of magnitude larger. The same is true for free cash flow, where IBM generated $14.7 billion over the last four quarters, while Synopsys lagged at $2.7 billion.

I'll admit that Synopsys' sales growth is impressive, and I like the company's AI-assisted engineering expertise. But it can't hold a candle to Big Blue's decades of innovative business growth, and IBM's 36% return on equity puts Synopsys' 3.7% ROE to shame.

I'm comparing a proven cash machine to a barely profitable growth story here. Synopsys deserves respect, but it's not the stock I would recommend in this duel.

news.Title: November Is Historically the Best Month for the Stock Market. Here Are My Best 3 Stocks to Buy.
news.Content:
If you're thinking about sitting out the stock market in November due to concerns like the election, the status of the Iran war, or any other item, don't. History is not on your side. Research from The Motley Fool shows that November is the best month of the year for the S&P 500 . It averages around a 1.9% gain in November, beating out April's and December's 1.4% gain. There's a midterm or regular election cycle in half of those years, so it's clear that this isn't an effect investors need to consider.

With November being the best month to invest in historically, what are the three best stocks to buy? Well, I think Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA), Micron Technology (NASDAQ: MU), and Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG) (NASDAQ: GOOGL) top the list, and each looks pretty attractive right now.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Nvidia

Nvidia is the world's largest company, so it may seem odd to think it can get bigger. But that's what all the projections point to. Nvidia posted monster 106% revenue growth in the second quarter, and Wall Street analysts expect 91% growth in Q3 and 83% in Q4. Next year, Nvidia expects 70% revenue growth, clearly indicating that the AI build-out is going as strong as ever.

There are no signs of weakness in Nvidia's business; however, the stock has been fairly weak this year. As a result of strong business growth and weak stock gains, the stock is pretty attractively priced right now.

NVDA PE Ratio (Forward 1y) data by YCharts

With Nvidia at 27 times earnings and 13.4 times next year's earnings, it's clear that next year's growth hasn't been priced into the stock. In fact, if Nvidia hits analyst estimates and maintains its 27 price-to-earnings ratio, the stock could double over the next year. The market doesn't quite realize this yet, but it could in November.

Micron

Micron is in a similar boat as Nvidia. It makes memory chips, which are in huge demand and short supply thanks to insatiable AI workloads. Micron's results are even more extreme than Nvidia's. Micron's fiscal year ends in August, so it's already in its 2027 fiscal year. Wall Street analysts expect Micron to grow at a 107% rate this year, although it's not an easy company to predict growth for.

Memory chip pricing is largely driven by market demand, and with conditions expected to worsen in 2027 and 2028, prices could continue to rise. That would mean a faster growth rate than Wall Street projects, which could further exaggerate how cheap Micron's stock is.

Story Continues

The stock trades for just 5.3 times this year's earnings, which means a massive gain could be in store if the market comes back around to Micron's stock .

Alphabet

Last on my list is Alphabet. Alphabet is a staple in the AI world, but the market didn't take kindly to its latest earnings report. Investors sold off the stock by over 10% the day after earnings due to negative cash flow. This is a sign that Alphabet is spending more than it brings in, but it's doing it for a reason.

Alphabet's cloud computing division, Google Cloud, grew at a 103% pace during Q3, a simply incredible rate. This division is one of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI build-out, as it runs workloads for several major clients. Alphabet is spending big to continue boosting its cloud revenue, and with that revenue growing as fast as it is, this spending makes a ton of sense. I'm not as worried as the market is, as the company's long-term financial picture supports this major spending.

As a result, I think Alphabet is a smart stock to buy on the dip in November.

news.Title: Chamath flags a hidden risk building under the AI boom
news.Content: The largest IT businesses in America have the money to accomplish almost everything at once for many years. According to conventional wisdom, Microsoft (MSFT), Meta Platforms (META), Alphabet (GOOGL) and Amazon (AMZN) could build data centers, repurchase billions of dollars of stock and still maintain some of corporate America's strongest balance sheets. However, artificial intelligence is starting to test that paradigm. According to billionaire investor Chamath Palihapitiya, the spending boom poses a less obvious risk. He said on the Oct. 30 All-In Podcast that technology companies may need outside capital to finance AI infrastructure, competing with the U.S. government, another huge borrower. Palihapitiya estimates that the broader AI industry already owes roughly $340 billion to $400 billion to capital markets. Even if demand for AI is still high, that is significant. Big Tech is returning less to shareholders while investing more in infrastructure. Investors may need to pay considerably more attention to borrowing costs and free cash flow. The quest to develop the greatest technology is no longer the main focus of the AI race. The issue of financing has taken over. Big Tech's AI spending is eating into cash returns Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta and Oracle generated a combined $542.9 billion in operating cash flow during the first nine months of 2026, according to Reuters . Their capital spending doubled, reaching $556.9 billion, exceeding the cash flow the five firms generated for the first time, according to data going back to 2011. Shareholders are already feeling the squeeze. The group's total stock buybacks dropped 83% to $13.6 billion. Microsoft accounted for the majority of the remaining buybacks at that time, while Alphabet and Meta did not make any repurchases. This eliminates a long-standing financial windfall for investors. By lowering the number of outstanding shares, repurchases enable earnings per share to increase more quickly than overall profits. "The entire United States economy is levered to the AI complex," Palihapitiya said. AI is not necessarily a bad investment because of the enormous expenditure. In the end, stockholders may benefit if new infrastructure generates sufficient income and profit. However, the barrier is becoming higher. Reuters found the five companies swung from $143.5 billion of free cash flow a year earlier to a $14 billion deficit during the first nine months of 2026. In exchange for possibly higher AI earnings in the future, investors are giving up some cash returns today. Story Continues Meta shows how the AI equation can change Meta serves as an example of how soon investing on AI may put strain on even a solid balance sheet. S&P Global Ratings changed Meta's credit outlook to negative on Oct. 30, citing rapidly increasing capital spending and uncertainty around future free operating cash flow. Meta expects capital expenditures of $135 billion to $145 billion this year. S&P forecasts free operating cash flow deficits of $39 billion in 2026 and $71 billion in 2027 and expects the company could eventually use more debt to finance expansion. Meta disagreed with S&P's evaluation and highlighted the commercial prospects brought forth by AI. That encapsulates the main tension. Whether Meta can afford its present buildout is not the issue. It is able to. How soon such investments begin to produce enough revenue to cover the expenditures is the issue. More Artificial Intelligence: AI's biggest business opportunity may not look like AI AI racks are outgrowing old power: 2 chipmakers have a strategy BofA splits software into winners and losers as AI agents arrive What happens when more AI businesses borrow is Palihapitiya's wider worry. According to his projections, their funding requirements until the end of 2027 may account for almost 30% of the anticipated issuance of new U.S. Treasury notes and bonds during that time. The exact proportion should be interpreted with caution since it is Palihapitiya's estimate rather than an official government measurement. However, the idea is simple. Many of the same investors provide funding to both corporations and the federal government. To attract capital, corporations may need to provide higher returns due to increased corporate borrowing. This increases the required return on AI investments. Microsoft shows what AI investors need to watch Microsoft provides an example of why the bearish case is still unresolved. The most recent quarter growth of Microsoft's Azure of 48% indicates that the massive infrastructure buildout is supporting significant demand. Investors in Big Tech must see AI-related revenue and profit growth that is fast enough to support the money going into processors, data centers, and electricity. The most obvious test could be free cash flow. The strain on balance sheets and shareholder returns could lessen if Microsoft, Meta, Alphabet, and Amazon finally make money from AI more quickly than capital expenditure increases. Palihapitiya's reasoning is more difficult to reject if expenditure keeps rising while debt rises and free cash flow declines. Buybacks also provide another helpful hint. A steady increase in repurchases combined with ongoing AI investment would indicate that these businesses are once again making much more money than they need to finance growth. Palihapitiya's reasoning differs from prior warnings about an AI bubble because of this. The financial equation does not need to collapse for AI to become more challenging. It only has to become much more expensive to fund. Related: Microsoft is offering 60,000 employees a way out This story was originally published by TheStreet on Nov 2, 2026, where it first appeared in the Investing section. news.Title: Amazon is on a course to spend half a trillion dollars in a single year: JPMorgan
news.Content:
Amazon's ( AMZN ) big spending on AI investments is only just beginning, JPMorgan tech analyst Doug Anmuth warns.

"We do not expect capex growth to decelerate or slow next year, and as such we project capex of $395 billion in 2027 (+77% year over year) followed by $476 billion in 2028 (+20% year over year)," Anmuth wrote in a new note.

Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said last week the company would spend "meaningfully more" on capex in 2027, without providing a number. The company estimated its capex would hit $220 billion in 2026.

Anmuth added, "We believe management's strong visibility into demand gives it the confidence to underwrite 40%+ growth over the next two years and to invest even more aggressively in AI compute infrastructure."

The large checks Amazon cut to build out its AI infrastructure caught up with it in the third quarter.

Amazon's free cash flow decreased to an outflow of $42.4 billion for the trailing 12 months, driven primarily by a year-over-year increase of $94.8 billion in purchases of property and equipment. This increase primarily reflects investments in artificial intelligence, Amazon said.

This compares to a free cash flow inflow of $14.8 billion for the trailing 12 months ended Sept. 30 of last year.

Investors headed for the exit on Amazon stock post-earnings. Shares were down over 1% on Friday, but they bounced back Monday, taking the stock's year-to-date advance to 9%. The S&P 500 is up 11% on the year.

"Meaningfully more" now has a number next to it, thanks to Anmuth. A very, very large number.

news.Title: Are Options Traders Betting on a Big Move in Apple Stock?
news.Content:
Investors in Apple Inc. AAPL need to pay close attention to the stock based on moves in the options market lately. That is because the Jan. 15, 2027 $5 Call had some of the highest implied volatility of all equity options today.

What is Implied Volatility?

Implied volatility shows how much movement the market is expecting in the future. Options with high levels of implied volatility suggest that investors in the underlying stocks are expecting a big move in one direction or the other. It could also mean there is an event coming up soon that may cause a big rally or a huge sell-off. However, implied volatility is only one piece of the puzzle when putting together an options trading strategy.

What do the Analysts Think?

Clearly, options traders are pricing in a big move for Apple shares, but what is the fundamental picture for the company? Currently, Apple is a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) in the Computer - Micro Computers industry that ranks in the Top 28% of our Zacks Industry Rank. Over the last 30 days, no analyst increased the earnings estimates for the to-be-reported quarter, while one has dropped the estimates. The net effect has taken our Zacks Consensus Estimate for the to-be-reported quarter from $2.89 per share to $2.88 in that period.

Given the way analysts feel about Apple right now, this huge implied volatility could mean there's a trade developing. Oftentimes, options traders look for options with high levels of implied volatility to sell premium. This is a strategy many seasoned traders use because it captures decay. At expiration, the hope for these traders is that the underlying stock does not move as much as originally expected.
