news.Title: Should Shopify Stock Be in Your Portfolio Pre-Q3 Earnings?
news.Content:
Shopify SHOP is set to report third-quarter 2026 results on Nov. 3.

For the to-be-reported quarter, Shopify expects revenue growth in the low-30% range.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for revenues is currently pegged at $3.74 billion, suggesting growth of 31.4% from the year-ago quarter's reported figure.

The consensus mark for earnings is pegged at 45 cents per share, up by a penny over the past 30 days and indicating 32.4% growth from the figure reported in the year-ago quarter.

Consensus Estimate Trend

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

SHOP's earnings beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate in two of the trailing four quarters, matched once and missed once, with the earnings surprise being 3.05%, on average.

Shopify Inc. Price and EPS Surprise

Shopify Inc. price-eps-surprise | Shopify Inc. Quote

Let's see how things have shaped up prior to this announcement.

Key Factors to Note for SHOP's Q3

Shopify's third-quarter 2026 performance is likely to have benefited from sustained growth in gross merchandise volume (GMV), supported by increasing merchant adoption, higher transaction volumes and expanding penetration across sales channels. In the second quarter, GMV increased 32% year over year to $115.6 billion. Merchant Solutions revenues surged 37% year over year to $2.78 billion, reflecting the growing contribution from payment processing and other merchant services. Continued momentum across businesses of different sizes, geographies and sales channels is expected to have supported transaction-driven revenues in the to-be-reported quarter.

Increasing adoption of Shopify Payments and Shop Pay is expected to have boosted Shopify's third-quarter performance. Shop Pay GMV grew 53% year over year in the second quarter, supported by expanding payment options, financing capabilities and improved checkout experiences. The integration of additional local payment methods into Shopify Payments and Shop Pay is likely to have improved payment conversion and supported transaction growth. Moreover, expanding adoption of Shop Pay Installments and Shopify's merchant financing solutions is expected to have strengthened its ability to monetize growing merchant transaction volumes.

Shopify's accelerating investments in AI-enabled commerce are expected to have supported merchant engagement and platform adoption during the third quarter. In the second quarter, AI-driven traffic and orders originating from AI searches tripled year over year. Daily active merchants using Sidekick increased 3.6 times, while the platform handled nearly 34 million conversations and helped create more than 36,000 custom applications. Shopify Catalog, which structures data for more than 1 billion products and the Universal Commerce Protocol are strengthening product discovery across AI platforms. These capabilities are likely to have enhanced merchant productivity, customer acquisition and conversion opportunities in the to-be-reported quarter. However, direct revenue contributions from agentic commerce remain at an early stage.

However, Shopify's increasing dependence on Merchant Solutions revenues is likely to have pressured its gross margin in the third quarter of 2026. Shopify Payments carries structurally lower gross margins than Subscription Solutions because of third-party payment processing expenses. Although greater payment penetration supports revenue growth and operating leverage, the increasing contribution from transaction-based services creates an unfavorable revenue mix. Shopify expects gross profit dollars to grow at a mid-to-high twenties percentage rate in the third quarter, below its projected revenue growth in the low thirties, reflecting this continuing mix shift.

Shopify's continued investments in AI infrastructure, product development and merchant acquisition are likely to have kept operating expenses elevated during the to-be-reported quarter. Although operating leverage has improved, the company continues to invest in Sidekick, agentic commerce capabilities and its broader platform. These initiatives may have limited near-term margin expansion despite strong revenue growth.

Story Continues

SHOP Shares Lag Sector

SHOP shares have dropped 2.1% year to date (YTD), underperforming the Zacks Computer & Technology sector's rise of 9.7%.

Shopify has outperformed peers, including Wix.com WIX and Commerce.com CMRC, but lagged Amazon AMZN. YTD, Amazon shares have returned 4.1% while Wix.com and Commerce.com shares have dropped 25.8% and 20.2%, respectively.

SHOP Stock's Price Performance

Moreover, the Value Score of F suggests a stretched valuation for Shopify at this moment.

SHOP stock is trading at a premium with a forward 12-month price/sales of 11.06X compared with the sector's 5.17X, Amazon's 2.77X, Wix.com's 1.82X and Commerce.com's 0.82X.

Shopify's Current Valuation

AI Push, Expanding International Footprint to Aid SHOP

Shopify's growing presence in AI-enabled commerce represents one of its most significant long-term growth opportunities. Partnerships with OpenAI, Google, Meta and Microsoft are expanding product discovery opportunities beyond traditional online storefronts. Shopify Catalog provides structured product information, including availability and product attributes, while the Universal Commerce Protocol enables AI agents to interact with merchant inventories and checkout infrastructure. Shopify's ability to position itself as the underlying transaction infrastructure for agentic commerce could strengthen its competitive moat and support long-term GMV growth as AI-powered shopping gains traction.

Shopify's investments in Sidekick and AI-powered development tools are expected to strengthen its merchant acquisition and retention capabilities over the long term. Sidekick simplifies store creation, marketing, analytics, inventory management and application development, lowering the technical barriers to starting and scaling a business. Greater adoption of AI tools could improve merchant productivity, accelerate successful business launches and strengthen Shopify's platform engagement.

Shopify's growing international presence offers considerable long-term growth potential as the company expands localized payment capabilities and cross-border commerce solutions. The company's presence across more than 175 countries, combined with continued investments in Shopify Payments, Shop Pay and Managed Markets, positions it to benefit from increasing global e-commerce adoption. International GMV growth of 37% in the second quarter highlights the opportunity to deepen penetration beyond North America.

Conclusion

Shopify's strong GMV growth, increasing adoption of Shopify Payments and accelerating AI-driven commerce initiatives position it well for the upcoming earnings release. The company's expanding international footprint, growing merchant ecosystem and investments in Sidekick and Shopify Catalog strengthen its long-term growth prospects. Although premium valuation and margin pressures remain concerns, Shopify's robust growth momentum and expanding opportunities in agentic commerce make the stock an attractive investment proposition for long-term investors.

Shopify currently has a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), which implies that investors should start accumulating the stock ahead of the third-quarter earnings. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

news.Title: Intel Gets Price Target Revamp but Keeps One Major Catalyst
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Intel ( NASDAQ:INTC ) remains under pressure after GF Securities cut its price target to $120 from $150 , citing the chipmaker's weaker-than-expected fourth-quarter outlook.

Shares fell nearly 1% in premarket trading Monday , extending the pressure after Intel's sharp post-earnings selloff.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 5 Warning Signs with INTC.

Is INTC fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

The downgrade in target reflects a much tougher near-term setup.

Intel guided for fourth-quarter revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion , below Wall Street expectations of roughly $17 billion, while gross margin guidance also weakened. Management has additionally warned that softness in the PC market could continue into the first half of 2027.

That is a meaningful problem because Intel's turnaround still depends on its core product businesses generating enough earnings and cash to fund a capital-intensive manufacturing rebuild.

Still, GF Securities is not abandoning the longer-term thesis.

The firm said Intel's foundry catalyst remains intact , even after lowering its target.

That distinction matters.

Intel Foundry has yet to deliver the kind of major external customer win that would fully validate its attempt to become a serious alternative to Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing.

But progress in areas such as advanced packaging and the company's 18A manufacturing process continues to give investors something to watch beyond the immediate weakness in PCs.

Intel also has a split demand picture.

The company said data-center demand remains strong and could continue beyond Q4, while client demand is expected to worsen. Industry-wide substrate and memory shortages are also limiting Intel's ability to fully satisfy some server demand.

Investor Takeaway

I think GF Securities' call captures the biggest tension in Intel right now.

The near-term numbers got worse, but the long-term foundry option is still alive.

That makes Intel increasingly a two-part story.

The product business needs to survive weaker PC demand and margin pressure, while the foundry business needs to finally produce a meaningful external customer that proves Intel can compete for advanced manufacturing work.

That catalyst has not arrived yet, and other analysts have made the same point: a major external foundry customer remains one of the clearest events that could materially strengthen the turnaround case.

For investors, the key things to watch are 18A execution, external foundry customer announcements, data-center supply, PC demand, gross margins and free cash flow .

Intel's weak Q4 outlook damaged the short-term story.

GF Securities is betting it did not kill the bigger one.

news.Title: Buy, Sell or Hold AMD Stock? Key Tips Ahead of Q3 Earnings
news.Content:
Advanced Micro Devices AMD is set to release its third-quarter 2026 results on Nov. 3.

AMD expects third-quarter 2026 revenues of $13 billion (+/-$300 million). At the midpoint of the revenue range, this represents year-over-year growth of 41% and 13% sequentially.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for AMD's third-quarter revenues is pegged at $13.12 billion, suggesting year-over-year growth of 42%. The consensus mark for third-quarter 2026 earnings is pegged at $1.94 per share, up a couple of cents over the past 30 days. The earnings estimate indicates growth of 61.7% on a year-over-year basis.

Consensus Estimate Trend

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

AMD beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate for earnings in all the trailing four quarters, the average surprise being 6.74%.

Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. Price and EPS Surprise

Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. price-eps-surprise | Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. Quote

Let's see how things have shaped up for the upcoming earnings announcement.

Factors to Note Ahead of AMD's Q3 Results

AMD's third-quarter 2026 performance is likely to have benefited significantly from accelerating adoption of EPYC server processors across hyperscale cloud providers and enterprise customers. Growing AI inference and agentic AI workloads are driving demand for high-performance CPUs capable of managing data retrieval, workflow orchestration and AI processing tasks. The company's fifth-generation EPYC Turin and fourth-generation EPYC Genoa processors have continued gaining traction across cloud and enterprise environments. The introduction of sixth-generation EPYC Venice processors, based on Zen 6 architecture and 2-nanometer technology, is expected to have strengthened AMD's competitive positioning.

The Data Center segment is likely to have benefited from increasing adoption of Instinct MI350-series GPUs across AI training and inference workloads. Demand for MI355X accelerators has strengthened as AI developers and cloud service providers expand deployments. The initial production shipments of AMD's Helios rack-scale AI platform, powered by MI450-series GPUs, EPYC Venice processors and Pensando networking, are also expected to have contributed to third-quarter revenues. However, Helios contributions are expected to have been relatively modest in the to-be-reported quarter.

AMD's Client business is likely to have benefited from continued Ryzen processor adoption, particularly across commercial notebooks, enterprise PCs and AI-enabled systems. Expanding adoption of Ryzen AI PRO 400-series processors across systems offered by Dell, HP, Lenovo and ASUS is expected to have supported market-share gains. Growing enterprise interest in local AI inference and AI-powered productivity applications may have provided additional opportunities for the Ryzen AI portfolio. Although management anticipated softer overall PC demand, AMD expected its Client business to outperform the broader market, supported by commercial customer adoption and product competitiveness.

Meanwhile, AMD's Embedded segment is expected to have aided third-quarter performance as demand recovered across networking, communications, aerospace and defense, test and measurement and industrial applications. The growing adoption of embedded x86 processors in data center networking and control-plane functions is likely to have strengthened the segment's growth trajectory. The third-quarter profitability is likely to have benefited from a growing contribution from higher-margin EPYC server processors and a recovery in the Embedded segment. Increasing Data Center revenues are expected to have supported gross profit expansion, while rising scale across AMD's product portfolio may have improved operating leverage.

However, AMD continues to face stiff competition from NVIDIA NVDA, Broadcom AVGO and Intel INTC. AMD faces intense competition from NVIDIA in AI accelerators and Intel in server and client processors. The growing adoption of internally developed AI accelerators by hyperscalers, along with Arm-based server processors, adds competitive pressure. Broadcom is increasing competitive pressure on AMD by strengthening its position in custom AI accelerators and high-performance networking for hyperscale customers.

Story Continues

AMD Stock Outperforms Sector & Peers

Advanced Micro Devices shares have surged 135.7% year to date (YTD), outperforming the Zacks Computer and Technology sector's return of 9.7%. The company's shares have outperformed Intel, NVIDIA and Broadcom YTD. Shares of Intel and NVIDIA have appreciated 78.2% and 9.8%, respectively, while Broadcom dropped 5.8%.

AMD's Share Price Performance

The AMD stock is not so cheap, as its Value Score of F suggests a stretched valuation at this moment.

In terms of the forward 12-month price/sales, AMD is currently trading at 10.27X, higher than the sector's 5.17X, NVIDIA's 8.03X and Intel's 4.85X, but lower than Broadcom's 14.64X.

AMD Stock's Valuation

AMD Rides on Strong Portfolio Amid Stiff Competition

AMD is positioned to capitalize on accelerating investments in AI infrastructure as hyperscalers, cloud providers and enterprises expand AI training, inference and agentic computing capabilities. The company expects the Data Center AI accelerator market to reach approximately $1.4 trillion by 2030, growing at an annual rate exceeding 45%. Increasing demand for GPUs, server CPUs and networking solutions provides AMD with a substantial opportunity to expand its presence across AI infrastructure. The company expects Data Center segment revenues to more than double year over year in 2027, supported by the increasing scale of AI deployments and strong demand for EPYC processors.

AMD's transition toward integrated rack-scale AI infrastructure represents a significant long-term growth catalyst. The Helios platform combines MI450-series GPUs, EPYC Venice CPUs, Pensando networking and ROCm software to deliver competitive AI inference performance and economics. The company expects substantial Helios shipment growth beginning in the fourth quarter of 2026 and accelerating throughout 2027. Strategic relationships with OpenAI, Meta and Anthropic provide multi-generation deployment opportunities, while Microsoft's Azure adoption broadens AMD's presence among major cloud providers. Beyond Helios, the planned MI500-series GPU platform, along with Verano CPUs and next-generation networking technologies, is expected to strengthen AMD's ability to compete for increasingly complex AI workloads.

Conclusion

AMD's strong AI infrastructure portfolio, accelerating EPYC adoption and expanding hyperscaler partnerships position it well for long-term growth. However, stiff competition from NVIDIA, Broadcom and Intel, alongside a stretched valuation, remains a concern. Moreover, the stock's impressive year-to-date rally suggests that much of the optimism surrounding its AI growth prospects may already be priced in. Investors should therefore adopt a cautious approach and wait for greater clarity on the Helios ramp and earnings growth before taking fresh positions in AMD stock.

AMD currently has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

news.Title: More Kroger and Albertsons locations will close in 2026
news.Content:
Back in the 1980s, my mother went grocery shopping at the Stop & Shop closest to our house.

On rare occasions, we went to a butcher shop, and a nearby town had a fruit and produce store I remember visiting sometimes. Still, most shopping trips went to the store closest to where we lived.

Over the years, the geographic loyalty began to erode. BJ's Wholesale entered that market, and eventually Whole Foods and Trader Joe's moved in. Still, with no Amazon, Instacart, Uber Eats, or other delivery services, most of our grocery spend went to Stop & Shop.

That's something that has radically changed, which has forced grocery giants Kroger and Albertsons to rethink their store footprints. Both chains have been closing stores in 2026 , and both have entered into a significant review of their ongoing operations.

It's a process that will lead to more shutdowns, partially driven by changing consumer behavior.

Consumers are skipping the grocery store

Americans have increasingly opted to buy their groceries online.

"Online food and beverage sales rose 15.5% during the four weeks that concluded Oct. 4 compared with the same stretch in 2025, according to data shared with Grocery Dive by Circana.

That's taking sales away from grocery stores.

"Food and beverage sales through brick-and-mortar channels declined 2.8% year-over-year during the period, while overall sales for the sector moved down by under 1%," the data showed.

Kroger has embraced this change and is trying to compete with digital rivals including Amazon and Walmart.

"When I look at the assets today, I believe our e-commerce business will grow to 30% of Kroger's business in the long term. To do that, we need to be 3 things for our customers: fresh, fast, and personal," Chief eCommerce Officer Nate Faust shared during the chain's recent Investor Day .

More Kroger:

Kroger and Costco shoppers refuse to let record gas prices win

Kroger's new offer helps you save on gas

Kroger isn't done pulling brands after Red Bull and Boar's Head

He does, however, see room for improvement.

"We will continue to get faster. Customer expectations on speed of delivery continue to increase every year, every month, every day. We already have the most important asset to deliver with speed, and that is our 2,700 stores. As we grow, we will add automation in our stores to fulfill orders faster, lower costs, and improve capital efficiency," Faust added.

Both Kroger and Albertsons are reviewing their store portfolios

While stores are a key part of both companies' delivery and digital plans, that does not mean all locations are safe.

Story Continues

Albertsons Executive Chair Meg Whitman shared fairly harsh remarks about the chain during its second-quarter earnings call .

"Market share trends have lagged, and despite many individual successes across the business, we're not delivering results consistent with the quality of our assets. We must turn things around," Whitman said.

Doing that will require making some cuts, which will include stores closing.

"We must also take a close look at our portfolio of banners, markets, assets, and businesses as well as at potential strategic actions we can take to enhance shareholder value," she added.

Kroger and Albertsons closures at a glance

Kroger: At least 50 locations across 18 states had closed or were scheduled to close by Oct. 22, 2026, according to a Fast Company review. Affected banners include Kroger, Fred Meyer, Harris Teeter, King Soopers, and Mariano's.

Albertsons : The company has not announced a specific nationwide closure target for 2026. It has continued evaluating underperforming locations following the failed merger. At least 12 locations across its banners had closed or were slated to close in 2026 as of May. This included Safeway, Vons, Acme, Randalls, and Albertsons stores, Fast Company reported.

Safeway has already been selectively closing locations, according to TheStreet .

Can Kroger and Albertsons compete with Amazon and Walmart?

CEO Susan Morris understands the challenge Albertsons faces in competing with lower-cost rivals Amazon and Walmart.

The "biggest leakage" of lower-income customers was to "big pure-price players such as Walmart and Amazon," she told Investing.com .

Mass marketers, which include Amazon and Walmart, have been gaining market share.

"Thirty-seven percent of shoppers consider mass retailers their primary destination for grocery purchases — up 6 percentage points YoY — compared with 36% who mainly visit supermarkets, according to FMI's US Grocery Trends 2026 report ."

Albertsons, Kroger, and Ahold Delhaize USA each lost share in the 12 months ended June 30, according to a Numerator analysis of 15 food retailers. Amazon and Whole Foods posted the largest share gains, followed by Costco and Walmart, eMarketer reported.

"That gulf is widening as online competition ramps up. More grocery dollars are flowing to Amazon and Walmart thanks to their investments in fast delivery: We expect Amazon and Walmart, including Sam's Club, to account for 75.7% of grocery ecommerce sales this year, up more than 3 percentage points from 2025," the site shared.

Kroger and Albertsons do have advantages

As a consumer, I have often opted to order online, and that's not always driven by price. Sometimes, I'll choose Amazon for items I can wait for, but for same-day delivery of bulky items, I use Uber Eats to purchase from Target.

That can happen on days when my wife or I actually go to our local Publix. It's just easier to have bottled water, cat food, and other heavy items delivered.

Grocery chains, however, do have some levers they can pull with consumers, according to RTM Nexus CEO Dominick Miserandino.

"Brand is a huge piece of this, but you have to understand what 'brand' actually means in grocery," he told TheStreet. "Walmart's brand is cheap. Costco's brand is bulk trust. Kroger's brand is convenience and reliability — it's the store five minutes from your house where the produce is fresh, the aisles are familiar, and you're in and out."

Price, he noted, is not the only factor shoppers consider.

"Throw in house brands like Simple Truth and Private Selection that people actually like, and Kroger gives you a reason to shop there that goes way beyond fighting over who has the cheapest loaf of bread. You don't need to be the flashiest giant on the block — you just need to be the easiest, most reliable choice in your own neighborhood," he added.

Related: Costco faces major food court complaints

news.Title: MKSI Gears Up to Report Q3 Earnings: What's in Store for the Stock?
news.Content:
MKS Inc. MKSI is scheduled to report its third-quarter 2026 earnings results on Nov. 4.

For the third quarter of 2026, MKS expects revenues of $1.35 billion, plus or minus $40 million. The consensus mark for the third quarter of 2026 revenues is pegged at $1.36 billion, indicating a 37.36% year-over-year increase.

On a non-GAAP basis, MKSI expects earnings of $3.58 (+/- 31 cents) per share. For the third-quarter of 2026, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for earnings is pegged at $3.64 per share, which has been unchanged over the past 30 days. This suggests a year-over-year increase of 88.60%.

MKSI beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate for earnings in three of the trailing four quarters while missing it once, with an average surprise of 8.22%.

MKS Inc. Price and EPS Surprise

MKS Inc. price-eps-surprise | MKS Inc. Quote

Let's see how things have shaped up for the upcoming announcement.

Factors Likely to Have Driven MKSI's Q3 Performance

MKSI's third-quarter 2026 performance is expected to have benefited from accelerating investments in semiconductor manufacturing equipment, driven by increasing demand for artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, advanced logic, DRAM and NAND memory. Strengthening demand for deposition and etch solutions, including RF power systems, vacuum subsystems, plasma generators and reactive gases, is likely to have supported semiconductor revenues.

Growing adoption of photonics and optical components for lithography, metrology and inspection applications is expected to have contributed to growth. Continued NAND upgrade activity, particularly in high-aspect-ratio dielectric etch applications and robust order backlogs are additional positives. MKS expects semiconductor revenues to grow more than 50% year over year to approximately $630 million in the to-be-reported quarter.

MKSI's Electronics and Packaging business is likely to have benefited from increasing AI server investments, rising advanced printed circuit board (PCB) complexity and robust demand for chemistry equipment. Growing requirements for higher-layer-count PCBs, advanced packaging and optical modules are expected to have supported demand for proprietary chemistry solutions and electroplating equipment.

Strong chemistry equipment orders, expanding customer investments and increasing adoption of higher-value equipment are likely to have strengthened revenues. Improving demand for rigid PCB drilling solutions is also expected to have contributed to growth. In the third quarter of 2026, MKSI expects Electronics and Packaging revenues to increase more than 30% year over year to approximately $385 million, despite seasonal softness in flexible PCB drilling equipment.

MKSI's Specialty Industrial business is expected to have gained from strengthening demand across datacom and defense applications in the to-be-reported quarter. Accelerating investments in AI data centers are likely to have boosted demand for communications testing solutions, while sustained defense spending is expected to have supported its specialized technology offerings. Improving industrial market conditions and higher semiconductor equipment utilization, supporting service revenues, are additional positives. MKSI expects Specialty Industrial revenues of approximately $335 million in the third quarter.

However, MKSI's third-quarter 2026 performance is likely to be hurt by seasonal weakness in flexible PCB drilling equipment demand. An unfavorable product mix, coupled with higher costs associated with capacity expansion and increased working capital investments, is expected to have pressured margins and cash flow.

news.Title: Can MELI's Cross-Platform Users Unlock Outsized Profit Growth?
news.Content:
MercadoLibre, Inc. MELI is strengthening its profitability potential by encouraging customers to engage with both its e-commerce marketplace and Mercado Pago fintech services. These customers, referred to as ecosystemic users, represent an increasingly important part of its business model, as deeper participation across both platforms creates opportunities for greater engagement and stronger customer economics.

Ecosystemic users demonstrate significantly higher shopping activity than marketplace-only customers, purchasing more products across a wider range of categories. Their engagement also extends to financial services, where they generate greater payment volumes, maintain higher assets under management and use more financial products. This interconnected activity strengthens the relationship between commerce and fintech, making customers more valuable to the broader ecosystem.

We also note that profit contribution from ecosystemic users substantially exceeds the combined contribution of customers using the marketplace and fintech services separately. This suggests that integrating shopping and financial services creates economic value beyond what either business could generate independently. Mercado Pago credit cards reinforce this relationship by encouraging customers to remain engaged across both platforms.

The growing adoption of cross-platform services underscores MercadoLibre's ability to deepen customer relationships and strengthen monetization opportunities. Management believes this interconnected ecosystem provides a structural competitive advantage that is difficult to replicate.

How Does MercadoLibre Stack Up Against Its Industry?

MercadoLibre, which competes with Amazon.com, Inc. AMZN and Sea Limited SE, has seen its shares tumble 14.4% over the past three months compared with the industry's 15.7% decline. While Amazon shares have fallen 15.4%, Sea Limited has plunged 33.2% in the aforementioned period.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

What Does MercadoLibre's Current Valuation Suggest?

From a valuation standpoint, MercadoLibre's forward 12-month price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio is 30.99, higher than the industry average of 18.96. The stock is also trading below its 12-month median level of 34.07. MercadoLibre is trading at a premium to Amazon (forward 12-month P/E of 21.85) and Sea Limited (14.75).

What Do Earnings Estimates Signal for MercadoLibre?

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for MercadoLibre's current fiscal-year sales indicates year-over-year growth of 44.5%, while the consensus estimate for earnings per share suggests a 3.3% decline. For the next fiscal year, the consensus estimates project sales and earnings growth of 29% and 44.9%, respectively.

For the third quarter, the consensus estimates for sales and earnings stand at $10.66 billion and $9.41 per share, suggesting year-over-year growth of 43.8% and 13.1%, respectively.

Story Continues

MELI's Investment Case

MercadoLibre's expanding marketplace presence, strong buyer engagement and integrated commerce-fintech ecosystem support its long-term growth potential. However, persistent margin pressures from strategic investments, softer consumer demand in key markets and a premium valuation remain concerns.

MELI currently carries a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell).

news.Title: Analyst models potential market reaction to a SpaceX-Tesla all-stock merger
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Piper Sandler revealed in a client note that it has built a model to assess how Tesla and SpaceX shares might react to a potential all-stock merger.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

The firm said client interest in a deal has deepened since Elon Musk confirmed on Oct. 20 that both companies had formed special committees.

Analyst Alexander Potter noted Piper is unsure what terms any merger might carry, or whether a deal will be proposed at all. However, he identified the three most critical variables as the buyout premium, synergies and the discount for deal risk.

The most important factor is any premium SpaceX pays for Tesla and the implied exchange ratio. Potter noted that a 30% premium would not mean 30% upside for Tesla shares, because SpaceX stock, the currency for the deal, would instantly reprice. Any initial gain would also be discounted based on the likelihood of approval.

Piper believes a merger is more likely than not, given that Musk has called it a good idea.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

"Given the above, we think it's likelier than not that a merger will be proposed," Potter wrote.

However, the firm expects investors to be skeptical that synergies are worth hundreds of billions of dollars. "Many believable scenarios imply initial re-pricing of less than +/-15%," the analyst added.

With limited upside, Potter said Tesla shareholders may push for a favorable exchange ratio. He expects them, excluding Musk, to need to be the largest ownership group in a combined company.

"Regardless, in most scenarios, Musk would have >70% voting control of any new entity," the analyst said.

Piper rates Tesla Overweight and SpaceX Neutral.

news.Title: Is UCTT Worth Buying as Growth Accelerates but Cash Flow Weakens?
news.Content:
Ultra Clean Holdings, Inc. UCTT is benefiting from accelerating semiconductor equipment demand, with earnings and profitability moving sharply higher. The investment question is whether that operating momentum can overcome weak cash conversion and a capital-intensive expansion cycle.

That trade-off is especially important because stronger reported profits have not yet translated into equally strong cash generation or capital returns. Investors must weigh improving estimates and margins against funding needs, customer concentration and execution risk.

UCTT's Earnings Momentum Is Building

Third-quarter 2026 adjusted earnings reached $1.15 per share, topping the Zacks Consensus Estimate of 91 cents by 26.4%. Revenues increased 48.8% year over year to $759 million and exceeded the consensus estimate by 4.6%.

The outlook points to another step up if current expectations hold. The Zacks Consensus Estimate calls for fiscal 2027 revenues of $3.788 billion and earnings of $6.63 per share, compared with projected 2026 revenues of $2.768 billion and earnings of $3.40 per share.

Ultra Clean Holdings, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Ultra Clean Holdings, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Ultra Clean Holdings, Inc. Quote

Ultra Clean Has a Clear Margin Opportunity

Profitability is improving as higher volumes increase factory utilization. Non-GAAP gross margin reached 17.3% in the third quarter, up from 16.7% sequentially, while non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 9% from 7%.

Management continues to target roughly 20% gross margin at about $4 billion of annual revenues. Higher utilization, greater vertical integration, a richer mix of engineered products and more production in lower-cost regions are expected to support that goal as capacity fills.

UCTT's Cash Conversion Is the Main Warning

The earnings improvement has not yet produced healthy cash conversion. Trailing 12-month cash-flow conversion was negative 244.4%, while free-cash-flow conversion was negative 418.5%, well below UCTT's historical medians.

Working capital is absorbing substantial cash. Inventory rose to $723.3 million, and operating activities used $42.3 million in the third quarter as Ultra Clean built critical components and safety stock. Trailing 12-month return on invested capital of 4.6% also remained below its 10-year company median of 9.8%.

Ultra Clean Still Carries Concentration Risk

Customer concentration remains a structural risk. Lam Research Corporation LRCX represented 39% of third-quarter revenues, while Applied Materials, Inc. AMAT accounted for 22%. Together, the two customers contributed 61%, leaving UCTT sensitive to their production schedules, sourcing decisions and wafer-fab-equipment spending.

Both customers are operating in supportive end markets. Lam reported September-quarter revenues of $8.22 billion and said AI was driving higher semiconductor demand and device complexity. Applied Materials posted record fiscal third-quarter revenues of $9.12 billion and cited AI-driven demand across leading-edge foundry-logic, DRAM and advanced packaging. Their strength supports the industry backdrop, but it does not remove UCTT's dependence on a small customer base.

Story Continues

UCTT's Ratings Favor Momentum Over Growth Quality

The bottom line is that UCTT offers accelerating earnings and a credible margin-expansion path, but the investment case is not clean. Cash conversion, low capital returns and concentration risk argue for discipline even as semiconductor demand strengthens.

UCTT currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), which is favorable from an earnings-estimate revision perspective. Its Momentum Score of A adds support for near-term price and earnings momentum. However, the Growth Score of D, Value Score of C and VGM Score of C indicate a less consistent profile across growth quality, valuation and combined style characteristics. That mix favors investors who prioritize momentum while recognizing that cash-flow and execution issues remain unresolved. news.Title: 5 Best Meme Stocks to Invest In
news.Content:
Nobody has to double their money every year to build real wealth. An investor who puts $10,000 into a stock that returns 15% annually and holds it for 40 years ends up with about $2.7 million. That takes patience, not a lucky guess.

Reaching for stocks that promise to multiply overnight makes that outcome less likely, not more, because a single collapse can wipe out years of compounding. That tension is the subject of our look at whether Sandisk can keep climbing after a 1,322% gain in a year .

Hedge funds work from the opposite instinct. On average, they don't load up on lottery-ticket stocks. They back companies they judge most likely to deliver higher returns for an amount of risk they can live with.

Bubble Warnings Spread as Retail Traders Pull Back

Veteran voices are urging care. Yahoo Finance reported on October 9 that Bridgewater Associates' Ray Dalio said the market is close to bubble territory. Panmure Liberum head market strategist Joachim Klement expects the AI bubble to burst in either 2027 or 2028, according to Bloomberg . Meanwhile, Bank of America Securities' Jill Carey Hall wrote in a client note that retail clients were net buyers, the first retail inflows since late July.

Everyday traders have cooled off since then. Goldman Sachs strategist Ben Snider wrote in a note that retail trading volumes have fallen about 20% since mid-summer, and retail made up 9% of US equity volume, near its lowest level since 2020, according to Yahoo Finance on October 26. You might also be interested in reading our piece on whether Palantir can justify a multiple five times its sector's .

The speculative money has not gone quiet, though. Snider's note showed retail trading in leveraged index funds running at roughly double the pace of ordinary funds tracking the same indexes, and Robinhood data pointed to retail options trading nearly doubling over the past year.

So, what are the best meme stocks to buy? For an expanded list, check out 10 Best Meme Stocks to Invest In . We provided the top 5 meme stocks below. As you will notice last year's meme stocks such as AMC, GameStop (GME), and Opendoor (OPEN) didn't make our list.

Our Methodology

To compile this list, we searched Instagram Reels for stocks promoted by financial influencers and tallied how often each one was pitched. We kept the 20 most frequently pitched stocks, excluding any company with a market cap above $500 billion, and ranked the 10 with the most hedge fund holders in ascending order. Hedge fund data is as of Q2 2026, from our database of 1,006 hedge funds.

Story Continues

Why are we interested in the stocks that hedge funds pile into? The reason is simple: our research has shown that we can outperform the market by imitating the top stock picks of the best hedge funds. Insider Monkey's quarterly newsletter strategy selects 14 small-cap and large-cap stocks every quarter and has returned 599.2% since May 2014, beating its benchmark by 372 percentage points ( see more details here ).

5 Best Meme Stocks to Invest In

5. Arista Networks (NYSE:ANET)

Market Cap: $212.97 billion

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 91

Arista Networks' second quarter was its first above $3 billion in revenue, at $3.036 billion. Sales grew 37.7% from a year earlier and 12.1% from the first quarter, and the company's own forecast calls for about $3.3 billion this quarter. Chief executive Jayshree Ullal said customers see networking as the center of how their infrastructure runs.

Arista makes the switches that connect servers inside data centers, and AI clusters need a lot of them. The company has built a line of AI networking products that sit at the heart of its strategy, and its balance sheet shows the demand building. Current deferred revenue stood at $5,100.7 million at the end of June, up from $4,002.6 million at the end of 2025. The long-term portion grew too, from $1,369.8 million to $1,765.2 million. Both balances were higher at the end of June than at the start of the year.

Arista reports its next quarter this week, so fresh numbers are only days away.

Readers can see how that cash cushion plays out in our breakdown of Arista's deferred revenue and cash flow .

4. Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL)

Market Cap: $172.22 billion

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 96

Marvell chief executive Matt Murphy said AI-related bookings remain exceptionally strong and that he expects revenue growth to speed up through the rest of the fiscal year. The quarter already shows it in the numbers. Revenue rose 37% from a year earlier to a record $2.739 billion, about $39.0 million above the midpoint of the company's own guidance, and growth in the data center business accelerated to 46%.

For the current quarter, Marvell guided to $3.150 billion in revenue, plus or minus 5%. Murphy pointed to strong demand for its connectivity products and a significant acceleration in the custom chip business starting in the second half of the fiscal year.

Murphy described the strength as broad-based across the data center portfolio. Marvell also raised its revenue outlook again, for both this fiscal year and the next, compared with the guidance it gave last quarter. With connectivity and custom chips both gaining at once, the company has two growth drivers feeding the same data center buildout.

Our analysis of whether Marvell's growth can justify its premium covers that story in more depth.

3. GE Vernova (NYSE:GEV)

Market Cap: $227.06 billion

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 106

GE Vernova's orders nearly doubled in the third quarter. They reached $29 billion, up 96% on an organic basis, led by equipment orders at its Power business while services stayed strong. The backlog grew by $20 billion from the previous quarter to $197 billion. Chief executive Scott Strazik said he now expects the backlog to pass $200 billion in the fourth quarter, with better margins on the work.

Gas turbines are a big part of that pile, and the Power business is leading the way. Gas Power equipment backlog and slot reservation agreements rose from 116 gigawatts to 122 gigawatts, and the company expects to reach at least 130 gigawatts by the end of 2026. Strazik also pointed to rising demand for electricity infrastructure around the world.

Management raised its 2026 guidance for revenue, adjusted EBITDA margin and free cash flow, and the board doubled the share repurchase authorization from $10 billion to $20 billion. Chief financial officer Ken Parks said the higher guidance reflects that momentum.

The stock's price measured against that demand gets a full look in our analysis of GE Vernova's backlog and valuation .

2. Vistra (NYSE:VST)

Market Cap: $46.44 billion

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 111

Vistra will be the preferred power supplier to a new data center venture backed by KKR, Kuwait Investment Authority and Nvidia, and the company has committed up to $1.0 billion to it. The venture, called Helix Digital Infrastructure, gives Vistra a direct line to large technology buyers that need dependable electricity.

The core business is earning more. Second-quarter adjusted EBITDA from ongoing operations reached $1,767 million, up from $1,349 million a year earlier, a gain of more than 30%. Management reaffirmed 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $6.8 billion to $7.6 billion, and about 100% of expected 2026 generation was already hedged. That guidance leaves out both the pending Cogentrix acquisition and the agreements with Meta.

Vistra has signed power purchase agreements with Meta, and part of them is expected to add to 2027 earnings. Chief executive Jim Burke said the fleet was available more than 97% of the time during recent extreme heat in Texas and the PJM grid. Vistra has also bought back about $6.5 billion of its stock since late 2021.

Management's own buying drew attention in our piece on how Vistra's CEO bought stock after the selloff , which asked whether AI power demand is mispriced.

1. Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK)

Market Cap: $166.34 billion

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 128

Sandisk's revenue for the fiscal first quarter jumped 378% from a year earlier to $11,031 million, and management guided to $12,200 million to $12,600 million for the next quarter. Gross margin was 85.0%, which means most of each sales dollar stayed with the company.

news.Title: AI Stocks Slide: Are Tech ETFs Worth Watching?
news.Content:
The U.S. stock market endured a difficult October as mounting concerns over artificial intelligence (AI) spending, weakening free cash flow and elevated interest rates triggered a sharp selloff in technology and semiconductor stocks. More than $2 trillion in Nasdaq-100 market value evaporated during the month.

The correction has unsettled investors, who had grown accustomed to technology-led market gains. However, the recent weakness does not necessarily signal the end of the bull market or the AI investment cycle. Rather, it highlights a shift in investor priorities where the market is increasingly demanding justification behind massive investments in AI infrastructure that will translate into sustainable revenues, earnings and free cash flow.

For ETF investors, this distinction is crucial. Instead of abandoning equities amid the volatility, investors may find opportunities to reposition portfolios, diversify away from concentrated technology exposure and selectively accumulate fundamentally strong funds.

Why Is Tech Sector Under Pressure?

The latest selloff reflects growing concerns about the financial sustainability of the AI infrastructure boom. Major technology companies are committing substantial capital to data centers, advanced chips and computing infrastructure, but the returns on these investments remain uncertain.

Alphabet's GOOGL shares plunged more than 12% in one session after its quarterly capital expenditure reached approximately $51 billion, contributing to a negative free cash flow of around $9 billion, per Gadget Review, as quoted on Yahoo Finance.

Amazon AMZN also reported negative trailing 12-month free cash flow of $42.4 billion for the period ended Sept. 30 against a positive free cash flow of $14.8 billion a year earlier. Its projected capital expenditure of $220 billion for 2026 has added to investor concerns, per Gadget Review as quoted on Yahoo Finance.

Meta META has also faced pressure from its AI infrastructure commitments, while Microsoft's MSFT ability to remain cash flow positive has highlighted the differences in financial flexibility among the major technology companies.

The market is signaling that AI demand alone is no longer sufficient to justify elevated valuations. Investors want stronger evidence of monetization, better capital discipline and improved cash generation.

Big Tech Pressure Hits Other Corners of Tech Sector

The pressure has also extended beyond the largest technology companies. Intel's weak guidance, softer PC demand and manufacturing challenges have weighed on semiconductor sentiment. Meanwhile, concerns that AI-generated search results could weaken referral traffic have added another layer of uncertainty for companies dependent on digital advertising and online engagement.

Story Continues

Higher energy costs and interest-rate concerns have further complicated the outlook. Elevated oil prices can reinforce inflationary pressures, potentially keeping borrowing costs higher for longer. This creates an additional headwind for growth-oriented companies whose valuations depend heavily on future earnings.

Why Investors Should Not Lose Hope?

Despite the correction, there are reasons to avoid interpreting October's losses as a structural breakdown in the equity market. This is because tech behemoths like Alphabet's latest quarterly results highlighted the contrasting impact of its AI investments.

Google Cloud revenues more than doubled year over year to $30.7 billion, reflecting strong demand for AI and cloud services.

AI Still Has Enough Potential

The recent concerns are primarily about the pace, cost and profitability of AI infrastructure expansion rather than the disappearance of demand. Cloud computing, data centers, advanced semiconductors and high-bandwidth memory continue to be important areas of investment.

Strong demand from these segments could support a recovery in selected technology and semiconductor companies, provided revenue growth begins to justify capital expenditure.

Historical Seasonality Offers Cautiously Positive Signal

November has historically been a relatively strong month for U.S. equities. More importantly, historical analysis shows that the S&P 500 has finished higher 12 months after every U.S. midterm election since 1950, across 19 observations, according to Yahoo Finance. This provides a constructive historical backdrop.

However, the sample is small, and historical patterns are not guarantees of future returns. Current equity valuations are elevated, and the 2026 market's starting position differs from many previous midterm years. Therefore, seasonality should support investor perspective and not serve as a standalone reason to buy.

Tech ETFs to Watch

Invesco QQQ Trust Series I ETF QQQ is designed to track the Nasdaq-100 Index. Its portfolio is heavily tilted toward technology and growth-oriented companies, making it particularly sensitive to trends in AI, semiconductors, cloud computing and digital services.

QQQ warrants close attention, given its significant exposure to key AI-related stocks, including Microsoft (6.17%), Alphabet (2.61%), Amazon (4.12%) and Meta Platforms (2.91%).

QQQ has assets under management worth 487.61 billion and an expense ratio of 0.18%. The fund trades at a three-month average volume of 35.53 million shares. QQQ presently carries a Zacks ETF Rank #2 (Buy).

Invesco Nasdaq 100 ETF QQQM tracks the Nasdaq-100 Index. Hence, the fund is heavily exposed to the same large-cap technology and growth companies.

QQQ warrants close attention, given its significant exposure to key AI-related stocks, including Microsoft (6.17%), Amazon (4.12%), Alphabet (2.61%) and Meta Platforms (2.91%).

QQQM has assets under management worth $111.18 billion and an expense ratio of 0.15%. The fund trades an average three-month volume of 2.93 million shares. QQQM presently sports a Zacks ETF Rank #1 (Strong Buy).

State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust SPY provides exposure to the same mega-cap companies and tracks the S&P 500 Index.

SPY warrants close attention, given its significant exposure to key AI-related stocks, including Microsoft (5.91%), Amazon (3.74%), Alphabet (5.15%) and Meta Platforms (2.02%).

SPY has assets under management worth $816.07 billion and an expense ratio of 0.09%.

The fund trades an average three-month volume of almost 43 million shares. SPY presently has a Zacks ETF Rank #2 (Buy).

news.Title: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq recover from bruising sell-off as oil prices fall
news.Content:
US stocks climbed on Monday as investors regained risk appetite ahead of another packed week of earnings, midterm elections, and a key jobs report.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) rose 1%, while the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) added 0.6%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) jumped 0.8%, attempting a comeback after a tech rout dragged stocks last week.

Markets were poised to bounce back after an AI-fueled sell-off that saw the Nasdaq Composite lose 5.2% during the month of October. Chipmakers and other tech names rebounded ahead of the market open, though Apple ( AAPL ) shares dipped slightly in the lead-up to the iPhone maker's earnings report after the bell on Monday. Investors also got a a fresh look at Anthropic on Monday morning with the AI startup filing an amended version of its S-1 filing.

Bitcoin ( BTC-USD ) rose slightly to trade near $78,000 per token after cryptocurrencies took a hit following a $6.3 billion hack of Binance , which investigators are calling the biggest crypto hack in history .

Crude oil prices, meanwhile, dropped amid reports that the US and Iran are seeking a diplomatic resolution to the war in the Middle East. Brent crude futures ( BZ=F ), the international benchmark, traded near $106 per barrel.

On the economic data front, investors will get a reading on US manufacturing activity and prices paid. The calendar for the rest of the week will feature several pieces of labor market data, culminating in the government's October jobs report on Friday.

LIVE 10 updates

13 mins ago David Hollerith

US manufacturing expands in October as inflation pressures persist

US manufacturing activity expanded in October, though two closely watched surveys released Monday offered differing signals on the sector's momentum as factories grappled with persistent inflation pressures.

The Institute for Supply Management's manufacturing index rose to 55.5 from 54.5 in September, exceeding economists' expectations of 54.6 and marking the gauge's 10th consecutive month in expansion territory.

Factory production rose to its highest level since November 2021, with ISM's production index jumping 2.3 points to 59.0. New orders accelerated slightly (55.5 from Sept's 55.3) while employment growth slightly slowed (52.4 from Sept's 52.7).

Meanwhile, a measure of prices paid by manufacturers eased to 75.2 from 77.9, though it remained elevated as businesses grappled with higher energy prices, tariffs and supply chain bottlenecks.

A separate survey from S&P Global released Monday also pointed to continued factory expansion, though at a slower pace. Its manufacturing index fell to 54.9 in October from 55.9 in September, below an earlier preliminary reading of 56.0.

27 mins ago Grace O'Donnell

Hyperscaler debt offerings are back: Oracle and Google join Microsoft in new bond issuance

While stocks generally rose in early trading, Oracle ( ORCL ) stock is getting dented after the company announced a new $20 billion capital raise, suggesting that concerns about AI spending continue to churn beneath the surface.

Oracle plans to sell $10 billion in investment-grade bonds and a similar amount of stock, according  to Bloomberg , to fund AI capital spending and dividends.

It's not the only hyperscaler looking to issue debt at this time to pay for massive AI investments.

Bloomberg also reported that Alphabet ( GOOG ) is set to raise 6 billion euros (roughly $6.7 billion) in its second euro bond sale in 2026. The report stated that the Google parent company plans to offer higher yields than its bond offering in May.

The announcements also come just days after Microsoft ( MSFT ) announced a $25 billion bond offering of senior unsecured notes. Microsoft said it intended to use the proceeds to fund working capital, capital expenditures, repurchases of capital stock, acquisitions, and repayment of existing debt.

But the divergence in stock prices highlights the difference in the companies' balance sheets. While Google stock rose on Monday following its announcement, Oracle stock fell 5%, as investors view the company as more leveraged.

56 mins ago David Hollerith

US stocks start off November in recovery mode

US stocks opened higher Monday as investors begin November with another week packed with earnings , crucial labor market data and the midterm elections.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) rose 0.7%, while the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) added 0.5%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) jumped 0.7%.

Investors also got a fresh look at Anthropic on Monday morning. The artificial intelligence company filed an amended version of its S-1 filing shortly before Monday's open. Later Monday, investors will also get a reading on US manufacturing activity and prices paid in October.

Today at 2:10 PM UTC Ines Ferré

Binance sees more than $4.6 billion in withdrawals after largest crypto hack in history

Binance has seen $3.64 billion in outflows since it gradually restored user withdrawals following the largest crypto hack in history, which the FBI linked to North Korea.

The world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange said that it processed $4.649 billion in withdrawals and approximately $1.01 billion in deposits. Binance detailed that the resulting net outflows represent just 2.1% of its $171 billion in total assets under management.

Binance was hit late Thursday by a hack that investigators said impacted roughly $6.3 billion in funds, with roughly half of those assets frozen.

On Monday, the exchange said it has covered approximately 95% of the impacted amount. The outstanding 5% consists of smaller tokens outside of the top 10 cryptocurrencies, whose assets are less liquid and will take longer to source.

Today at 1:41 PM UTC Ines Ferré

SpaceX looking to acquire Boost Mobile in pursuit of wireless market: Report

In pursuit of plans to enter the US wireless market, Elon Musk-led SpaceX ( SPCX ) is reportedly exploring a potential acquisition of Boost Mobile or access to its network.

Verizon ( VZ ), AT&T ( T ) and T-Mobile ( TMUS ) have reportedly rejected SpaceX's requests to use their wireless networks, according to a report from the Washington Post.

SpaceX has since held discussions with EchoStar ( ECHO ), Boost Mobile's parent company, about a potential partnership or acquisition, the report said. Shares of EchoStar are up roughly 5% in premarket trading.

A deal could give SpaceX access to Boost Mobile's network agreements, providing an entry point into the estimated $235 billion US wireless market.

The move would expand Musk's business empire beyond rockets and Starlink, opening another potential revenue stream for SpaceX.

Today at 1:18 PM UTC Jared Blikre

Apple has turned into Wall Street's hedge against the AI trade: Chart of the Day

When AI stocks get hit, investors have found a place to hide. It's the company that has mostly sat out the AI spending race — Apple ( AAPL ).

Chip stocks have had plenty of rough days this year, and Apple has mostly shrugged them off. On the 46 days the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index ( ^SOX ) fell 2% or more, Apple rose on 30, about two out of every three.

That's new. From 1994 through last year, Apple rose on only about 1 in 6 of those days, and no year came anywhere close to this one, by Yahoo Finance's calculations.

Apple and chip stocks have basically stopped moving together. Apple's correlation with the chip index — a measure of how closely two assets move in step — turned negative in July and hit its lowest level on record in September.

Today at 12:00 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell

Apple to report Q4 earnings Monday, with iPhone 18 sales in the spotlight

Apple ( AAPL ) will report its fourth quarter earnings after the bell Monday, providing investors with a glimpse of early iPhone 18 Pro sales. Yahoo Finance's Dan Howley previews what to expect:

The iPhone Duo went up for preorder on Oct. 16 and went on sale Oct. 23, missing Apple's fiscal Q4, though the company could still offer color on demand.

This will also be Apple's first earnings call with new CEO John Ternus , who took over the role from Tim Cook on Sept. 1.

For the quarter, Apple is expected to report earnings per share (EPS) of $2 on revenue of $113.46 billion, according to Bloomberg analyst consensus estimates. The company saw EPS of $1.85 and revenue of $102.46 billion in the same period last year.

Today at 11:00 AM UTC Grace O'Donnell

These 3 sectors could be in focus next year in Washington — no matter who wins on Tuesday

Yahoo Finance's Ben Werschkul reports:

The 2026 campaign has featured bipartisan calls for action on pharmaceuticals, the housing market, and AI data centers, a sign that this trio of sectors may be in focus in Washington no matter which party prevails on Tuesday.

The critical comments are especially notable coming from Republicans as the campaign enters its final days. Democratic rhetoric about reining in big business is nothing new, but the GOP's focus indicates both an increased willingness within the party to adopt a populist stance and a potential openness to strike deals next year in the new power-sharing landscape.

And the high likelihood that Democrats will win control of at least one chamber of Congress could elevate these issues — with or without President Trump's support.

The coming year is likely to feature "meaningful opportunities and risks for key sectors," Stifel chief Washington policy strategist Brian Gardner wrote in a recent note to clients.

Today at 10:00 AM UTC Grace O'Donnell

Big Tech's sell-off wasn't about the actual fundamentals

With another Big Tech company reporting earnings today (Apple ( AAPL )) after the Street gave punishing post-earnings reactions to Alphabet ( GOOG ) and Amazon ( AMZN ) stocks last week, Yahoo Finance's Jake Conley offers some perspective on the market mood:

It was a deeply red week for the tech sector after a slew of earnings failed to give investors the signs of strength they were looking (and hoping) for.

At Alphabet, a miss on both revenue and profit sent shares falling 13% as Sundar Pichai said that while the company's search division had grown, the money wasn't keeping up as AI cuts into search monetization.

Down the street at Amazon, a double miss on both earnings and revenue triggered a sell-off that couldn't be stopped by strong cloud growth in AWS.

And we can't forget Intel, where a beat on earnings and in-line revenue were overshadowed by weakness in PC sales, attributed to heightened memory costs. That company lost a quarter of its value after the report, falling over 28%.

But there's a conundrum for investors in these earnings reports. As Barron's associate editor Al Root said to Yahoo Finance, the numbers weren't all bad; it's more like investors have gotten more demanding.

"It's not that the earnings were awful, it's just that it wasn't enough to support the market," Root said on "The 8:30." He added, "The level of nerves going into earnings season was so high, like everybody was waiting for the shoe to drop."

news.Title: Lumentum (LITE) Beats Q1 Earnings and Revenue Estimates
news.Content:
Lumentum (LITE) came out with quarterly earnings of $4.57 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $4.22 per share. This compares to earnings of $1.1 per share a year ago. These figures are adjusted for non-recurring items.

This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of +8.29%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this optical networking products maker would post earnings of $2.99 per share when it actually produced earnings of $3.23, delivering a surprise of +8.03%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has surpassed consensus EPS estimates four times.

Lumentum, which belongs to the Zacks Communication - Components industry, posted revenues of $1.26 billion for the quarter ended September 2026, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 0.98%. This compares to year-ago revenues of $533.8 million. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates four times over the last four quarters.

The sustainability of the stock's immediate price movement based on the recently-released numbers and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's commentary on the earnings call.

Lumentum shares have added about 128.1% since the beginning of the year versus the S&P 500's gain of 10.7%.

What's Next for Lumentum?

While Lumentum has outperformed the market so far this year, the question that comes to investors' minds is: what's next for the stock?

There are no easy answers to this key question, but one reliable measure that can help investors address this is the company's earnings outlook. Not only does this include current consensus earnings expectations for the coming quarter(s), but also how these expectations have changed lately.

Empirical research shows a strong correlation between near-term stock movements and trends in earnings estimate revisions. Investors can track such revisions by themselves or rely on a tried-and-tested rating tool like the Zacks Rank, which has an impressive track record of harnessing the power of earnings estimate revisions.

Ahead of this earnings release, the estimate revisions trend for Lumentum was mixed. While the magnitude and direction of estimate revisions could change following the company's just-released earnings report, the current status translates into a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for the stock. So, the shares are expected to perform in line with the market in the near future. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

It will be interesting to see how estimates for the coming quarters and the current fiscal year change in the days ahead. The current consensus EPS estimate is $5.01 on $1.47 billion in revenues for the coming quarter and $21.40 on $6.25 billion in revenues for the current fiscal year.

Story Continues

Investors should be mindful of the fact that the outlook for the industry can have a material impact on the performance of the stock as well. In terms of the Zacks Industry Rank, Communication - Components is currently in the top 19% of the 250 plus Zacks industries. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1.

One other stock from the same industry, Viavi Solutions (VIAV), is yet to report results for the quarter ended September 2026. The results are expected to be released on November 4.

This communications equipment company is expected to post quarterly earnings of $0.40 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of +166.7%. The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has remained unchanged over the last 30 days.

news.Title: X-Energy Has Amazon as an Anchor Customer and Went Public in April. Is It a Better SMR Stock Than Oklo?
news.Content:
Small modular reactors (SMRs) could change how nuclear energy is produced by shifting from custom-built nuclear power plants to factory-built, modular units. Two companies to watch in this space are X-Energy (NASDAQ: XE) and Oklo (NYSE: OKLO). Both develop SMR technology but use different designs and are at different stages in regulatory approvals and commercial agreements.

X-Energy stands out thanks to its anchor customer and early investor, Amazon , which has helped the company hit the ground running by funding early stage engineering, licensing, and permitting, and helping it secure commercial deals. For investors considering these two SMR stocks, the key question is whether Amazon's backing gives X-Energy an edge over Oklo.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Amazon is a major shareholder in X-Energy

Developing next-generation nuclear technology is no easy feat, and Amazon's early support for X-Energy is central to the company's investment thesis. In October 2024, Amazon led a $700 million Series C-1 funding round for X-Energy to further develop its reactor design, secure licensing, and fund the first phase of its fuel fabrication facility in Oak Ridge, Tennessee.

Amazon holds nearly 66 million shares in X-Energy, or roughly 23% of X-Energy's total shares outstanding. This gives Amazon significant voting power and a vested interest in X-Energy's success. As part of this deal, Amazon and X-Energy aim to deploy 5 gigawatts (GW) of SMRs across the U.S. by 2039.

X-Energy is further ahead in NRC regulatory reviews

Thanks to this financial assistance from Amazon, X-Energy is further along in both regulatory reviews and commercial agreements than Oklo. The Nuclear Regulatory Commission has accepted X-Energy's flagship project with Dow 's formal Construction Permit Application, completed its Environmental Assessment, and advanced toward its final Safety Evaluation milestones.

Oklo, in comparison, had its initial Combined License Application (COLA) for its Aurora powerhouse design at Idaho National Laboratory denied in January 2022 due to insufficient technical and safety information. It is in pre-application engagement with the NRC, but is looking to advance this project through the Department of Energy's authorization pathway.

X-Energy has more firm customer commitments thanks to Amazon's support

Story Continues

X-Energy also holds an edge in commercial agreements. The company's first project with Dow will deploy four units of X-Energy's 80-megawatt (MW) Xe-100 high-temperature gas-cooled SMR at its UCC Seadrift Operations manufacturing site in Texas. As noted above, the company is working through regulatory approvals and hopes to have full construction approval by the first quarter next year.

In addition, X-Energy has early stage agreements with American Electric Power and Energy Northwest. With AEP, it will look to deploy 12 reactors, with Amazon providing milestone-based development capital and a long-term power purchase agreement to cover all facility costs. For its Energy Northwest deal, X-Energy aims to deploy 12 reactors, with Amazon funding the first four units as the offtake customer.

In comparison, Oklo has a larger 14 GW pipeline and agreements with Meta Platforms , Equinix , and Switch. However, most of this pipeline (12 GW) is tied to Switch, and the agreement remains non-binding. The company hopes to deploy its Aurora Powerhouse at Idaho National Laboratory in 2028 as part of a pilot program. However, to sell power commercially, the company must still achieve NRC licensing.

X-Energy is a better buy than Oklo -- but there's a catch

Oklo is pursuing alternative pathways to get its Aurora powerhouses operational and could do so before X-Energy. However, X-Energy has significant backing from Amazon, which has helped it navigate the challenging NRC licensing and approval process.

That said, SMRs and microreactor technology are still in their early stages, and companies are only now laying the groundwork to deploy them commercially in the 2030s. While X-Energy has an early advantage, investors today still face execution and deployment risks, making investments in SMR stocks a very high-risk bet on the future of nuclear energy.

news.Content:
Investing.com -- Oppenheimer reiterated its Perform rating on Apple in a note on Monday ahead of the company's fiscal fourth-quarter results, warning that the stock's premium valuation leaves little room for disappointment.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

Analyst Martin Yang forecasts fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of $112.9 billion and EPS of $1.96, slightly below the consensus of $113.4 billion and $1.99.

However, he said the bigger debate is the fiscal 2027 earnings outlook. His 2027 EPS estimate of $8.91 is about 7% below consensus.

Yang stated that slowing iPhone growth, Services headwinds, and memory cost inflation are likely to constrain upside. He noted that Apple trades near the top of its 15-year forward P/E range.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

"The valuation already demands more durable growth than we underwrite," Yang wrote.

He said seven of nine sources in Oppenheimer's review sample advised owners to hold off on upgrading to the new Pro models. Counterpoint data showed Pro-series sell-through up 3.1% globally in the first three weeks, but down 4% in the U.S. and 27% in Japan.

"We see limited evidence of a broad replacement-cycle acceleration," the analyst said.

Oppenheimer forecasts 5 million to 6 million iPhone Duo shipments in 2026 and 15 million to 20 million in fiscal 2027, supporting 6% iPhone revenue growth. However, Yang warned the device could cannibalize Pro and Pro Max sales.

The firm also models a 150 basis point hit to products gross margin in the December quarter from higher DRAM and NAND costs. It sees Services reacceleration as unlikely due to slow App Store growth, regulatory pressure, and slowing Google search growth.
