news.Title: 美股閉眼買都賺的時刻到了？ 選後行情將開跑 專家卻示警3大警訊
news.Content:
美國期中選舉即將登場，美股一項延續超過70年的歷史上漲紀錄，今年恐怕面臨考驗。標普500指數過去在期中選舉後6個月及12個月均呈現上漲，但今年選前漲勢已相當強勁，加上AI投資回報疑慮、油價上揚及政治風險升高，市場能否延續過往行情備受關注。

據英國《金融時報》報導，超過75年來，投資人在期中選舉前最後一個交易日買進美股，持有6個月或12個月均能獲利，上一次選後出現下跌已要追溯至1946年。相較之下，自1950年以來，其他年份相同期間約有三分之一的時間呈現下跌。

選前漲勢強勁 歷史反彈條件與過去不同

過去期中選舉後美股經常上漲，主要原因在於選舉前的不確定性消退，投資人得以重新評估政治格局、政策及企業基本面。不過，今年選前市場表現與過去有所不同。

《金融時報》指出，自1942年以來，標普500指數在期中選舉年的平均高點回落幅度約18%，但今年截至選前最大跌幅僅約9%，顯示市場表現相對強勢。

估值方面，標普500指數的循環調整本益比（CAPE）已達40.7，不僅高於1998年期中選舉前的前次高點33.8，也遠高於自1942年以來約20的平均值。此外，今年前9個月僅5檔股票就貢獻標普500指數超過一半的漲幅，市場漲勢集中於少數大型企業。

AI投資、油價與伊朗局勢增添壓力

除了估值偏高，AI投資能否帶來相應回報，也是市場隱憂。10月科技股遭遇賣壓，投資人擔心AI產生的獲利不足以支撐龐大資金投入，第三季財報也尚未消除相關疑慮。

地緣政治方面，油價上周再度回升至4月以來未見水準，市場猜測美國總統川普可能在選舉結束後加強對伊朗的軍事行動。Jefferies經濟學家Mohit Kumar認為，川普選後重啟轟炸行動的風險偏高，也因此對短期風險資產採取審慎態度。

國會版圖牽動美股 專家解析歷史報酬

政治版圖同樣可能影響選後行情。卡森投資研究公司（Carson Investment Research）的資料顯示，自1951年以來，共和黨總統執政、國會由兩黨分別掌控時，標普500指數平均年報酬率為13.7%；若共和黨總統執政，民主黨同時掌控眾議院與參議院，平均年報酬率則僅有4.9%。

摩根士丹利財富管理美國政策與地緣政治策略主管Monica Guerra指出，重大政策變動減少，可能意味著市場受到的干擾也會降低。

摩根大通全球市場策略師Jordan Jackson則認為，選舉結束後政治格局更加明朗，市場通常能重新聚焦基本面與政策。

不過，今年美股面臨的高估值、AI投資回報疑慮及地緣政治風險，與過去選前市場疲弱的情況不同。即使選舉後不確定性消退，標普500指數能否延續長達數十年的上漲紀錄，仍有待市場檢驗。

news.Title: Morgan Stanley stands by Sandisk as CFO flags a low-end pullback
news.Content:
If you bought $1,000 worth of Sandisk Corp. (SNDK) stock at Wednesday's close, it was worth about $819 by Friday's close. Two trading days were all it took.

Shares fell roughly 18% across Thursday, October 29, and Friday, October 30, 2026, ending at $1,150.89 , according to StockAnalysis data . With about 142 million shares outstanding, that erased roughly $36 billion in market value.

The selling followed a record quarter. Sandisk's fiscal first-quarter revenue hit $11 billion, up 378% from a year earlier, according to its earnings release .

Also read: Sandisk CFO admits higher prices are hurting consumer sales

Sandisk's weak spot is the cheap end of the market

Edge, Sandisk's biggest unit, sells flash memory to phone and PC makers, and it grew just 7% from the prior quarter. Chief Financial Officer Luis Visoso explained why on the earnings call . He described resilience in premium and mainstream devices, "partially offset by contraction at the lower end."

That is the admission that matters, and it reaches past the consumer sales slump . Sandisk's quarterly filing shows Edge customers bought 20% less flash by volume than a year earlier. They still paid far more in total, because the price per gigabyte soared.

The squeeze is industry-wide. HP Inc. (HPQ) planned PC price hikes over memory costs, Reuters reported , and IDC says smartphone shipments fell a record 22% last quarter.

Big buyers aren't flinching. "To the contrary, we're seeing very strong demand from our customers," Visoso told Bank of America analyst Wamsi Mohan. To me, that split explains Friday's selling better than any headline number.

Morgan Stanley is betting cloud demand covers it

Morgan Stanley isn't worried, according to a research note shared with TheStreet. Analyst Joseph Moore kept an Overweight rating and a $1,750 price target in the October 30 report, titled " Earnings power grinding higher. " Like every price in this story, that target is pre-split; Sandisk's 8-for-1 stock split takes effect November 20.

Moore's case rests on supply, not shoppers. The note says consumer and client products fell to 56% of revenue from 90% a year earlier, a share it expects to keep shrinking.

In his view, data center growth "should ease concerns about a slowdown in consumer devices upsetting supply and demand." Put simply, cloud buyers will absorb whatever chips shoppers stop buying.

I agree with the math, but the note also reveals a cost. Sandisk's average selling prices rose only about 9% last quarter, trailing other memory makers, because it locked in contracts early, Moore wrote.

Story Continues

The bigger surprise sits in his model. Moore raised his 2027 earnings estimate to about $271 a share, from $212, yet left his target unchanged.

That's because Morgan Stanley values Sandisk on through-cycle earnings of $62.50 a share, less than a quarter of that estimate. Its model even shows fiscal 2029 earnings falling about 21%, so this bull expects leaner years too.

More SanDisk:

5-star analyst sets jaw-dropping price target on SanDisk stock

5-star analyst resets SanDisk stock price target by $175

Sandisk has $93.9 billion in deals: Now comes the hard part

The stock looks cheap until you check the math

Sandisk trades at 4.75 times forward earnings, per StockAnalysis. Against Morgan Stanley's through-cycle figure, Friday's price is about 18 times earnings, a more ordinary multiple.

The stock sits about 51% below its 52-week high of $2,354.39 but roughly six times its 52-week low of $183. It also closed Friday just 5% above Morgan Stanley's $1,100 bear case.

Options traders gave that level close to even odds of breaking within a year, the note shows.

Morgan Stanley sits below the Street. Sandisk carries a Buy consensus from 25 analysts with an average target near $2,105 , per StockAnalysis:

$3,000 is among the highest targets , set by Bernstein's Mark Newman with a Buy rating before the report.

$1,750 is Morgan Stanley's target , rated Overweight.

$1,000 is the lowest target on the Street , and three analysts rate the stock Hold while one says Sell .

After the split, Morgan Stanley's target works out to about $219. The bank also discloses a stake of 1% or more in Sandisk and investment banking ties to the company.

What Sandisk holders should do now

The split changes nothing about what you own; it cuts the same pie into more slices. Moore expects about $30 billion in buybacks next year, which he says "should continue to help keep a floor under the stock as long as end-market demand remains strong." That floor rests on demand investors now question.

If I held the stock, I'd watch two things before adding. One is whether the December quarter lands inside the 84.5% to 85.5% gross margin guide. The other is whether low-end weakness spreads to premium phones, where Moore's thesis would crack first.

The $1,100 bear case also works as a line in the sand. A sustained break below it would tell holders the market doubts even the bank's cautious through-cycle math.

Memory makers have chased an escape from boom and bust for decades, and Sandisk's long-term contracts are its answer.

Morgan Stanley still values the company on through-cycle earnings, a quiet sign that even its bulls expect the cycle to return. The next signal may come soon, since only about $10.5 billion remains on Sandisk's buyback authorization and Moore expects another large one.

news.Title: 5 ETF Winners of a Scary October
news.Content:
U.S. stocks closed October with sharp losses as disappointing earnings from Amazon AMZN and Alphabet GOOG, GOOGL reignited concerns over the mounting costs of Big Tech's artificial intelligence (AI) investments and the potential returns on such massive spending (read: Top ETF Stories of October).

Nasdaq Suffers Its Worst Monthly Performance Since March 2025

Despite the Dow's resilience, October proved challenging for the broader market. The Dow advanced 1.5% for the month, but the Nasdaq Composite and S&P 500 lost 5.2% and 1.2%, respectively. The Nasdaq recorded its steepest monthly decline since March 2025, as quoted on Yahoo Finance.

The latest bout of selling followed earnings reports from Amazon and Alphabet that failed to meet certain market expectations, raising questions about whether their enormous AI infrastructure investments would generate adequate returns.

Amazon shares fell 2% on Oct. 30, 2026, while Alphabet extended its losses after recording its steepest single-day decline in more than two decades on Oct. 29. Meanwhile, Intel INTC added to the technology sector's woes.

The chipmaker's shares came under severe pressure after its fourth-quarter outlook fell short of Wall Street expectations, with the stock plunging as much as 29% on Oct. 30.

AI's Cursed October

The AI trade has struggled in October for multiple reasons. The month saw AI-driven vulnerabilities that led to a series of high-impact cybersecurity incidents, a trend dubbed "Black October." The term refers to a series of high-impact cybersecurity incidents in October 2026 that were accelerated by AI.

Meanwhile, the AI debt boom emerged as a key concern. The 10-year Treasury yield climbed to around 5.3% at the start of the month, reviving concerns about borrowing costs and the massive debt financing used to build AI data centers.

Investors have constantly reassessed technology valuations amid rising rates and heavy corporate borrowing. Roundhill Generative AI & Technology ETF CHAT is off 18% over the past month (as of Oct. 30, 2026).

Energy Stocks Offer Some Relief

Energy shares provided a rare bright spot amid the broader market weakness. ExxonMobil XOM and Chevron CVX briefly touched record highs after both oil majors reported stronger earnings, thanks to wider refining margins amid the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

Bitcoin Falls as Binance Hack Rattles Crypto Market

The weakness extended beyond equities, with cryptocurrencies also coming under pressure. Bitcoin has declined more than 7% over the past month. Digital assets faced selling pressure following a reported $6.3 billion hack involving cryptocurrency exchange Binance on Oct. 30. The incident was described as the largest cryptocurrency heist in history. iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF IBIT is off 8.4% over the past month.

Story Continues

ETF Winning Areas of October

Against the somber backdrop described above, the following exchange-traded funds (ETFs) emerged as winners in October.

Breakwave Tanker Shipping ETF BWET – Up 20.7%

The closure of the Strait of Hormuz, along with ongoing disruptions in the Red Sea, has disrupted key shipping routes, driving a sharp surge in freight rates. Elevated shipping rates have positioned the shipping fund BWET as a clear beneficiary.

United States Brent Oil Fund LP BNO – Up 18.8%

Due to the ongoing tensions in the Middle East, Brent crude futures climbed to around $113 per barrel, while West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures reached around $103 per barrel (at the time of writing).

Munificent Seven ETF BBLS – Up 14.6%

It looks to offer long-term growth of capital through exposure to the energy and infrastructure helping drive AI growth.

iShares Cybersecurity and Tech ETF IHAK – Up 8.8%

Cybersecurity stocks are having a strong year, due to rising AI-related spending and growing warnings from technology leaders about the risks posed by powerful AI agents. The emergence of advanced AI models has raised concerns about increasingly sophisticated cyberattacks, making cybersecurity investments even more crucial. Note that IHAK is up about 66% this year.

WisdomTree Cloud Computing ETF WCLD – Up 8.2%

The widespread adoption of remote connectivity continues to fuel the need for scalable and reliable cloud solutions. In second-quarter 2026, global cloud infrastructure service spending grew to $143.4 billion (an increase of more than $43 billion from second-quarter 2025), marking the highest growth rate in eight years, per Synergy Research. Some major cloud providers recently revealed that AI cloud capacity is sold out through next year.

news.Title: 韓股翻紅大漲，台股卻失守4萬5！郭哲榮揭布局契機：逢低搶進這幾檔
news.Content:
台股失守4萬5千點，韓股卻逆勢大漲，亞洲股市走勢呈現明顯反差。面對台股短線震盪， 摩爾投顧投資長郭哲榮（哲哲） 認為，台股短線拉回屬正常修正，第四季多頭格局並未因此改變，投資人不必因為短線下跌恐慌出場，反而可以留意AI供應鏈的逢低布局機會，點名 鴻海（2317）、聯發科（2454）、智原（3035）、環球晶（6488）、華邦電（2344） 及 南亞科（2408） 等相關個股。

【韓股大漲台股仍收黑 郭哲榮：別在低點恐慌砍單】

台股今（2）日開低走高，早盤一度大跌812.73點，最低來到44,399.10點，隨後低接買盤進場，指數最高反彈至45,156.17點，盤中一度重新站回4萬5千點，終場仍未能守住整數關卡，下跌291.69點收在44,920.14點，成交金額約7,588.75億元。

相較之下，韓國股市在SK海力士回購計畫等消息帶動下，開低走高，終場上漲2.24%。郭哲榮認為，台股短線拉回屬於市場修正，不代表多頭行情就此結束，尤其第四季仍有機會延續多頭走勢，投資人不應因為幾天的下跌，就在相對低點恐慌賣股。

郭哲榮也提醒，投資最重要的是控制風險，應以現股操作為主，避免使用融資槓桿，並做好持股分散。只要沒有過度擴大槓桿，就不必因為短線震盪而承受過大的心理壓力，反而可以趁市場拉回重新檢視持股，尋找具備長期成長動能的標的。

【資安外洩事件頻傳 企業防衛型AI需求升溫】

郭哲榮看好AI產業的另一個重要理由，是AI應用已經從生成式工具，逐步延伸到企業資安防禦。隨著AI技術進步，駭客也能運用自動化工具發動攻擊，企業為了保護客戶資料、商業機密及內部系統，勢必得投入更多資源升級資安設備與AI防禦系統。

近期台灣電商服務商91APP發生資安事件，調查指出，可能影響近480萬名消費者；日本無印良品也公告，官方App部分顧客資料有外洩風險，顯示企業資料安全已成為不能忽視的課題。

郭哲榮認為，這類資安威脅將進一步推升企業對地端AI、運算設備及防禦系統的需求。換句話說，AI不只是企業提升效率的工具，也 逐漸成為維護營運安全的重要基礎建設，相關硬體供應鏈有機會持續受惠。

news.Title: Stock Market Today (Nov. 2, 2026): S&P 500, Nasdaq measure modest gains ahead of Apple earnings, U.S. midterm elections
news.Content:
This live blog is refreshed throughout the day with the latest updates

from the market. To find the latest Stock Market Today threads, click here .

Happy Monday. Stocks were climbing and oil prices were falling as markets looked to recover from last week's brutal tech sell-off while gearing up for Apple's (AAPL) fourth-quarter results.

Markets tumbled Friday as tech stocks slid amid disappointing earnings reports from companies including Amazon (AMZN) and Alphabet (GOOG) and concerns about massive AI spending. The tech-heavy Nasdaq posted its worst single-day performance since June.

"Global markets are starting November on a cautious note, attempting to recover from a difficult October dominated by technology weakness and concerns about AI investment," Daniela Hathorn, senior market analyst at Capital.com, said.

"Wall Street suffered another sharp sell-off on Friday as investors questioned whether the enormous sums being invested in AI infrastructure can generate sufficient returns."

Hathorn noted that U.S. futures were pointing to a rebound Monday morning and Asian markets were also recovering, led by South Korea, while European futures suggested a relatively subdued but stable opening.

"The recovery suggests investors remain willing to buy into weakness, although confidence in the technology sector remains fragile," she said. "Apple's results will be particularly interesting because of its relatively limited exposure to large-scale AI infrastructure spending compared with its peers."

The iPhone maker is scheduled to report fourth-quarter earnings after the market closes Monday.

"Strong results could help stabilize the Nasdaq, but disappointing guidance could quickly undermine this morning's tentative recovery."

Hathorn said Tuesday's U.S. midterm elections would be the biggest political event of the week, with investors watching how the balance of power in Congress could influence fiscal policy, government borrowing and Treasury yields.

news.Title: Prediction: This Will Be Sandisk’s Stock Price After 1 Year
news.Content:
Artificial intelligence (AI) stocks are witnessing a bloodbath on the market due to various reasons, including hotter-than-expected inflation, higher interest rates, concerns about access to financing amid higher capital costs, and the aggressive spending on AI infrastructure by hyperscalers that's hurting their cash flow.

Shares of Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) have been caught in the broader tech rout, and a strong earnings report from the company didn't help it arrest the slide. Let's take a closer look at Sandisk's results and check if its fortunes will turn around in the coming year.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Sandisk's latest results indicate that its red-hot growth is here to stay

Sandisk released fiscal 2027 first-quarter results (for the three months ended Oct. 2) on Oct. 29. The stock plunged over 13% the next day amid a broader sell-off in tech stocks . However, Sandisk's drop isn't justified when we take a closer look at its earnings and guidance.

Sandisk's revenue jumped by a whopping 378% year over year to $11.03 billion. Meanwhile, non- GAAP earnings per share (EPS) increased from just $1.22 in the year-ago period to $49.51 in the previous quarter. The numbers comfortably exceeded Wall Street's expectations. Even better, Sandisk's guidance for the current quarter is better than what analysts were looking for.

The company expects $12.4 billion in revenue in the current quarter at the midpoint of its guidance range. It anticipates earnings per share of $56.00. Analysts were looking for $54.69 in earnings per share on revenue of $12.29 billion. Moreover, Sandisk's outlook clearly suggests that its red-hot growth is sustainable.

The company reported $3 billion in revenue and $6.20 in non-GAAP earnings per share in the second quarter of fiscal 2026. So, its top and bottom lines are poised for an exponential jump once again. It is worth noting that Sandisk's revenue increased at a much slower pace of 61% in the same quarter last year, while earnings increased by 5x year over year.

So, Sandisk's growth continues to accelerate, which explains why analysts anticipate its bottom line to jump by 220% in fiscal 2027 to $226.85. However, Sandisk's EPS growth in Q1 and the guidance for Q2 indicate that it could outpace analysts' expectations, and that could set the stock up for big gains over the coming year.

Story Continues

Wall Street expects big gains from Sandisk, but it could do better

Sandisk's 12-month median price target of $2,167 implies 88% gains, which is quite healthy. However, the stunning earnings growth the company has been clocking indicates that it can do better than that.

I say this because of the stock's dirt cheap valuation. Sandisk trades at just 9 times earnings, well below the S&P 500 index's earnings multiple of 23. The S&P 500's average earnings are anticipated to increase by 33% this year. Sandisk, therefore, deserves to trade at a premium to the S&P 500.

Let's say the stock trades at even 15 times earnings at the end of fiscal 2027, which will end in early July next year, and it clocks $226.85 in EPS (in line with consensus expectations); its price could reach $3,403. That's nearly 3x Sandisk's price right now, indicating that it has the potential to become a multibagger given its red-hot growth and attractive valuation.

news.Title: 油價暴跌 台指期夜盤45K失而復得 道指飆漲600點
news.Content:
（23：20更新）伊朗最高領袖批准政府開啟談判，有望化解擾亂中東能源供給、持續數月的衝突，消息帶動油價大幅走低，跌幅逾6%。原本陷入多空交戰的台指期夜盤瞬間狂拉近300點，一度報45487點。但在美股開盤後，隨著費半驟跌，台指期夜盤一度暴跌近400點，報44832點，而隨著費半早盤翻紅走強，台指期夜盤又重新站上45000點以上。

周一（2日）美股一開盤，主要指數同步走高。道瓊工業指數早盤大漲逾600點，那斯達克指數強彈逾300點。與台股連動密切的費城半導體指數開盤小漲後，突然回落，但早盤迅速翻紅，漲幅逾1%。

截至台北時間2日晚間11點20分，道瓊工業指數上漲582.44點（或1.13%），暫報52352.75點；那斯達克指數上漲280.016點（或1.10%），暫報25717.014點；標普500指數上漲66.30點（或0.87%），暫報7646.37點；費城半導體指數上漲102.58點（或0.96%），暫報10791.38點。

5大科技巨頭當中，僅蘋果走跌1.03%，谷歌母公司Alphabet漲2.17%，微軟漲1.09%，亞馬遜漲5.09%，臉書母公司Meta漲0.81%。半導體類股普遍走強，輝達漲2.29%，超微漲0.27%，台積電ADR漲1.08%，聯電ADR漲1.11%。

上周五科技股遭遇猛烈拋售後，周一出現止跌回彈跡象。與此同時，國際油價下跌也為股市提供了支撐，幫助市場在新的一個月迎來相對積極的開局。

不過荷蘭國際集團首席投資策略師Simon Wiersma指出，這次反彈的幅度相對於上周五的拋售來說較為溫和，「我目前還不會將其解讀為具有說服力的『逢低買入』訊號。圍繞AI投資、利率及地緣政治的不確定性依然充足，足以令投資者保持謹慎。」

news.Content: 美股主要指數周一(2日)開盤走高。市場對美伊透過外交途徑結束衝突的期待升溫，帶動國際油價大跌，緩解投資人對通膨的疑慮，美債價格也隨之上揚。 歷經10月賣壓後，科技股與AI概念股在11月首個交易日反彈，帶動美股三大指數開高。投資人本周還將迎來美國期中選舉及密集出爐的企業財報，觀察這波反彈能否延續。 截稿前， 道瓊工業指數 漲逾400點或近0.8%， 那斯達克綜合指數 漲近200點或近0.8%， 標普 500 指數 漲近0.5%， 費城半導體 指數漲0.3%，台積電ADR漲0.4%。 美股周一盤前走高。市場傳出，美國總統川普有意給對伊朗的外交斡旋更多時間。伊朗官方通訊社隨後報導，伊朗最高領袖已同意展開談判，布蘭特原油跌幅擴大至近6%，報每桶約107美元。油價回落提振市場情緒，那斯達克100指數期貨上漲0.9%，標普500指數期貨上漲0.5%。 追蹤晶片股的ETF盤前走勢顯示，半導體類股在上周五重挫後有望小幅反彈。個股方面，甲骨文(ORCL-US)宣布發行100億美元股票，並啟動同額債券發行計畫，盤前股價下跌3%。邁威爾(MRVL-US)宣布以總值1,150億美元的交易收購光通訊元件商Lumentum(LITE-US)後，盤前股價也轉跌。 本周市場將迎來美國期中選舉及一連串就業數據。長天期美債價格上揚，美元下跌0.2%，黃金升至每盎司約3,950美元。 科技股反彈力道有限 市場緊盯AI融資需求 荷蘭國際集團(ING-US)首席投資策略師Simon Wiersma指出，相較於上周五的跌幅，這波反彈力道有限，尚難視為明確的逢低買進訊號。AI投資能否帶來足夠回報、利率走向及地緣政治風險，仍讓投資人保持謹慎。

news.Title: Earnings Results Wrap with Apple After the Close
news.Content:
Monday, November 2nd, 2026

Pre-market futures are seeing some investors buying-in following Friday's heavy selloff, particularly in the tech-heavy (and AI-play) Nasdaq, which dumped nearly -2.9% on the day, nearly -750 points by the close. At this hour, the Nasdaq is back up +279 points, the blue-chip Dow +361 and the S&P 500 is adding +43 points. The small-cap Russell 2000 is up +21 points currently.

With the U.S. midterm elections one day away (thankfully!), we're seeing renewed hope on the peace front in the ongoing war with Iran. This has helped ease spot oil prices roughly -4% — to $97 per barrel (/bbl) on WTI and $106/bbl on Brent crude. Bond yields have also cooled from their inflamed levels four weeks ago: the 10-year is now +4.908% while the 2-year, back inside a 40-bps margin with the 10-year, sits at +4.598%.

Morning Earnings at a Glance: EL, MAR

Ahead of today's open, Estee Lauder EL reported a big positive earnings surprise of +38.46% in its fiscal Q1: $0.72 versus $0.52 in the Zacks consensus. Revenues of $3.72 billion in the quarter outpaced estimates by +1.86%. The cosmetics giant increased its guidance for the ongoing quarter, and the share price is up +2.8% on the news this morning. For more on EL's earnings, click here.

Global hotelier Marriott MAR posted a mixed Q3 report this morning, with earnings of $3.02 per share outperforming expectations by +5.59% versus $7.01 billion in quarterly revenues, which came in -0.54% shy of the Zacks consensus. Yet shares are up +5% in early trading on raised full-year earnings guidance, adding to the +28% stock gains year to date. For more on MAR's earnings, click here.

What to Expect from the Market Today: Apple Earnings After the Close

Roughly a half hour after today's closing bell, we'll see fiscal Q4 results from Apple AAPL, one of the so-called "Mag 7" companies — and the one that, interestingly, did not jump into the AI buildout race. Expectations are for earnings to have gained +7% year over year to $1.98 per share, on $112.95 billion in revenues which would be +10.23% above the year-ago tally. iPhone 18 numbers will be key in this report. Apple shares currently have a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

We'll also see results from two Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) companies after today's close: Roku ROKU and Lattice Semiconductor LSCC. While we await word on the progress on Roku's $22 billion buyout from Fox FOX, we expect the smart-TV streaming service to have brought +243% earnings growth from a year ago on +16.5% in sales. news.Title: 3 Reasons to Buy Alphabet Stock Right Now
news.Content:
Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL) stock hit an all-time high earlier this year, but it's been downhill ever since. Shares are currently down 11% year-to-date, even as the S&P 500 has gained 10%. What's going on with Alphabet? Many investors are worried about the company's significant spending on artificial intelligence (AI), and the tech leader's latest earnings report has exacerbated these fears, leading to a post-earnings dip.

Despite these challenges, Alphabet remains a great stock to buy and hold for the long term. Here are three reasons why.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: The Motley Fool.

1. Cloud sales growth continues to accelerate

In the third quarter, Alphabet's revenue grew by 25% year over year to $127.6 billion. That came in below analyst estimates, and it is one of the reasons why the market's reaction to the company's quarterly update was negative. But it gets worse. Alphabet's net earnings per share dropped by 26% year over year to $2.12, while its free cash flow was a negative $9.1 billion, significantly worse than the (positive) free cash flow of $24.5 billion recorded in the prior-year quarter.

Alphabet is investing heavily, but the company's spending isn't yielding top-line growth in line with Wall Street's expectations, and earnings and free cash flow are declining rapidly. That's a bad combination. However, there was at least one bright spot for Alphabet: Its cloud computing segment, Google Cloud.

During the period, cloud sales came in at $30.7 billion, 103% higher than the year-ago period. It's worth highlighting just how much Alphabet's cloud sales have been accelerating in recent quarters.

Notice also that the jumps have gotten bigger since Q4 2025. Google Cloud is proving to be a major growth driver for Alphabet, and there is more to come. The company noted that Cloud backlog was $561 billion as of the end of the period, an increase of 262% year over year. The company expects to recognize 55% of that -- or about $309 billion -- over the next 24 months -- that's roughly eight quarters at an average of $38.6 billion per quarter.

This points to sustained demand for the company's cloud services, and by the looks of it, the company will continue to capitalize on it at least over the next few years. That's great news for investors.

Story Continues

2. The AI tailwind is just getting started

Alphabet's AI business is booming. It is helping boost cloud sales growth, for instance. Alphabet noted that demand for enterprise AI solutions contributed meaningfully to the performance of its cloud computing business. Alphabet is also making progress elsewhere. For instance, the company highlighted that the Gemini app now has reached one billion users.

This grants the company significant monetization opportunities, which it will seek to exploit in the coming years. Further, Alphabet has started selling its custom AI chips, and according to management, this business is experiencing strong demand and meaningfully contributing to the top line.

Custom AI chips can sometimes be cost-efficient for corporations, and as AI infrastructure spending continues to grow, demand for these chips could rise. That gives Alphabet yet another meaningful growth avenue. The company's AI-related investments may be harming profits and free cash flow now, but they could pay for themselves several times over in the medium term.

That's why the post-earnings dip is not justified, in my view, and represents a great buying opportunity for long-term investors.

3. The price is right

Beyond cloud and AI, Alphabet has plenty of opportunities. Its search business remains rock solid; it remains a leader in streaming thanks to YouTube; it has a promising autonomous-vehicle business with Waymo; and more. The company's outlook appears bright, and the stock looks fairly valued right now.

Alphabet is trading at 18x forward earnings, versus an average of 17x for communication services stocks. Alphabet is worth a much steeper premium given the company's prospects, and buying the company's shares at current levels could yield above-average returns over the next five years.

news.Title: Amazon's latest report left stock investors with one big question
news.Content:
Amazon just handed investors a reason to worry and a reason to get excited in the same report. Third-quarter earnings fell short of estimates, free cash flow sank deeper into the red than expected, and management said it plans to spend meaningfully more on AI next year. The company also kept its full-year capital spending forecast unchanged.

The market's first reaction was not kind. Revenue and earnings per share both came in just shy of estimates, and in a nervous market for AI stocks, small misses can sting. Shares fell more than 6% in after-hours trading after the results were released. Look past the dip, though, and there is a business that still has plenty going for it.

Amazon is still doing the heavy lifting

Amazon Web Services remains the star of the show. The cloud unit grew revenue 39.3% from a year earlier to $46 billion, its sixth straight quarter of faster growth, and it now runs at an annualized pace of about $184 billion. Operating income for the unit came to $17.8 billion, according to Amazon .

Also read: Morgan Stanley just made a bold call on Amazon stock

That result edged past Wall Street's forecast of about $45.6 billion. CEO Andy Jassy has long argued that most global IT spending, about 85%, still sits on premises, and that the next decade should see much of it shift to the cloud.

Demand does not look like it is fading. The AWS backlog reached $578 billion, growing at a triple-digit rate, and Jassy described it as well diversified. Amazon says it is installing an AI accelerator about every 14 seconds as customers take up new capacity nearly as fast as it arrives, according to Amazon .

Wall Street had started warming to this story earlier in the year. Back in March, Citi and JPMorgan raised their price targets on the stock as AWS growth picked up, and Amazon's custom Trainium and Graviton chips were reportedly bringing in more than $10 billion a year. Citi also pointed to partnerships with Anthropic and OpenAI as a boost for AWS.

The spending bill keeps getting bigger

All of that growth costs money. On the earnings call, Jassy said Amazon still expects about $220 billion in cash capital spending this year and plans to spend meaningfully more in 2027, while the company spent $75.9 billion in the third quarter alone. CFO Brian Olsavsky said the AI investments have the potential to drive long-term revenue and free cash flow, The Motley Fool reported .

The cash impact is easy to see. Free cash flow over the trailing 12 months swung to an outflow of $42.4 billion, as reported by TheStreet . Investors who once counted on Amazon to throw off cash are now watching it pour that cash into data centers.

Story Continues

The cash pressure did not arrive suddenly. Back in 2025, Amazon's free cash flow had already dropped to about $11.2 billion from $38.2 billion the prior year, driven largely by a roughly $50.7 billion jump in property and equipment outlays. AI was a big part of that increase, alongside logistics and data center buildout.

Amazon is not the only giant feeling it. Alphabet posted negative free cash flow of $9.1 billion in the third quarter, after spending about $51.4 billion on capital projects. Even so, Google Cloud revenue more than doubled in the period.

Why some investors are getting nervous

Amazon's own founder has not been shy about the risks. Speaking at Italian Tech Week in October 2025, Jeff Bezos described AI as a kind of industrial bubble, one where separating the strong bets from the weak ones is genuinely hard for investors. His view on the technology itself remains optimistic.

That worry has now spread to the companies doing the building. Investors have started to fear that the eventual revenue from AI may not justify such heavy spending, which has made them more cautious about cloud giants like Amazon that are leading the infrastructure ramp-up, as reported by The Motley Fool .

More Amazon:

Amazon is coming for your quick Walmart run

Amazon's Alexa shopping tool faces its first big October test

Amazon pulls a best-selling pain reliever again, and customers need to check their medicine cabinets

Jassy has tried to answer that concern head-on. He said Amazon keeps shortening the time its infrastructure needs to break even, though returns still differ between its core cloud business and its AI build-out, according to Amazon . "Almost as fast as we install capacity, customers are gobbling it up," he said.

Analysts are watching the same issue. Bank of America flagged rising capital spending as a risk for Amazon, while noting that results should show strong returns on the capacity it is adding. Jassy said Amazon has a lot of capacity coming over roughly the next eight quarters.

Jassy is betting on a trillion-dollar cloud

Jassy is clearly not backing down. He said Amazon has a clear line of sight to attractive financial returns on its spending, and that AWS could grow more than 40% in each of 2027 and 2028 on its way to becoming a trillion-dollar revenue business in the next five to 10 years.

Some analysts are even more upbeat. Morgan Stanley's Brian Nowak expects AWS to grow 47% in 2027 and 42% in 2028, and he has a $350 price target on the stock. Jassy also said Amazon may end up with two trillion-dollar revenue businesses within five to 10 years, with its online stores as the other candidate, TheStreet reported .

The valuation may help make the case. Amazon stock trades at about 30 times forward earnings estimates and sits around 14% below its August high. That is not the cheapest the stock has ever been, but it looks reasonable given how fast AWS is growing. For investors who can stomach some bumps along the way, that may be an attractive entry point.

news.Title: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq recover from bruising sell-off ahead of busy week
news.Content:
US stocks climbed in premarket trading on Monday as investors regained risk appetite ahead of another packed week of earnings, midterm elections, and a key jobs report.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) rose 0.7%, while the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) added 0.5%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) jumped 0.7% higher after the index briefly entered into a correction.

Markets were poised to bounce back after an AI-fueled sell-off late last week that saw the Nasdaq Composite lose 5.2% during the month of October. Chipmakers and other tech names rebounded ahead of the market open, though Apple ( AAPL ) shares dipped slightly in the lead-up to the iPhone maker's earnings report after the bell on Monday. Investors also got a second look at an amended version of Anthropic's S-1 filing.

Bitcoin ( BTC-USD ) rose slightly to trade near $78,000 per token after cryptocurrencies took a hit following a $6.3 billion hack of Binance , which investigators are calling the biggest crypto hack in history .

Crude oil prices, meanwhile, dropped amid reports that the US and Iran are seeking a diplomatic resolution to the war in the Middle East. Brent crude futures ( BZ=F ), the international benchmark, traded near $109 per barrel.

On the economic data front, investors will get a reading on US manufacturing activity and prices paid. The calendar for the rest of the week will feature several pieces of labor market data, culminating in the government's October jobs report on Friday.

LIVE 7 updates

24 mins ago Ines Ferré

Binance sees more than $4.6 billion in withdrawals after largest crypto hack in history

Binance has seen $3.64 billion in outflows since it gradually restored user withdrawals following the largest crypto hack in history, which the FBI linked to North Korea.

The world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange said that it processed $4.649 billion in withdrawals and approximately $1.01 billion in deposits. Binance detailed that the resulting net outflows represent just 2.1% of its $171 billion in total assets under management.

Binance was hit late Thursday by a hack that investigators said impacted roughly $6.3 billion in funds, with roughly half of those assets frozen.

On Monday, the exchange said it has covered approximately 95% of the impacted amount. The outstanding 5% consists of smaller tokens outside of the top 10 cryptocurrencies, whose assets are less liquid and will take longer to source.

53 mins ago Ines Ferré

SpaceX looking to acquire Boost Mobile in pursuit of wireless market: Report

In pursuit of plans to enter the US wireless market, Elon Musk-led SpaceX ( SPCX ) is reportedly exploring a potential acquisition of Boost Mobile or access to its network.

Verizon ( VZ ), AT&T ( T ) and T-Mobile ( TMUS ) have reportedly rejected SpaceX's requests to use their wireless networks, according to a report from the Washington Post.

SpaceX has since held discussions with EchoStar ( ECHO ), Boost Mobile's parent company, about a potential partnership or acquisition, the report said. Shares of EchoStar are up roughly 5% in premarket trading.

A deal could give SpaceX access to Boost Mobile's network agreements, providing an entry point into the estimated $235 billion US wireless market.

The move would expand Musk's business empire beyond rockets and Starlink, opening another potential revenue stream for SpaceX.

The critical comments are especially notable coming from Republicans as the campaign enters its final days. Democratic rhetoric about reining in big business is nothing new, but the GOP's focus indicates both an increased willingness within the party to adopt a populist stance and a potential openness to strike deals next year in the new power-sharing landscape.

And the high likelihood that Democrats will win control of at least one chamber of Congress could elevate these issues — with or without President Trump's support.

news.Title: Marvell Agrees to Buy Lumentum in $115 Billion All-Stock Deal
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Marvell Technology ( NASDAQ:MRVL ) agreed to buy Lumentum ( NASDAQ:LITE ), which makes lasers and optical components for AI data centers, in an all-stock deal valued at $115 billion including debt. Lumentum shares fell 2.93% and Marvell shares fell 0.96% in premarket.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 3 Warning Sign with MRVL.

Is MRVL fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Lumentum shareholders will receive 4.5 Marvell shares for each share they own, valued at $1,132, a 23.9% premium to Lumentum's unaffected close on October 28, and will own about 33% of the combined company. The deal carries an equity value of $102.54 billion and is expected to close in the first half of 2028. Marvell expects more than $1 billion in annual run-rate cost synergies and said the deal should add to non-GAAP EPS in its first year after closing.

CEO Matt Murphy said AI infrastructure is shifting toward optical connectivity, an opportunity that comes along once in a generation. Marvell said the deal expands the combined company's addressable market to $550 billion. news.Title: 單日再砍349億元！台積電外資持股比創20年新低 鉅額交易卻驚現漲停價
news.Content:
權值龍頭台積電（2330）2日繼續遭外資無情調節，單日面臨逾1.5萬張提款、賣超金額高達349.7億元。盤中股價一度重挫至2,310元，距離2,300元整數大關僅差10元；尾盤雖在政策買盤加碼護盤下收斂跌幅，終場仍下跌40元，收在2,330元。值得市場關注的是，盤後鉅額交易意外出現以「漲停價」2,605元成交的紀錄，引發多頭「仙人指路」的聯想。

台積電今年以來持續面臨外資拋售壓力。據統計，截至2日收盤，外資持股比率已進一步滑落至68.45％，寫下自2005年底以來、近20年的歷史新低紀錄；今日盤中低點險守2,310元，市場對2,300元關鍵防線是否失守的擔憂情緒顯著升溫。

與集中市場疲弱走勢形成對比的是，台積電今日鉅額交易頻現多空對峙。盤後出現1筆以今日漲停價2,605元成交的配對交易，共計10張。由於台積電過往強勢時，鉅額高價成交常被市場視為多方先行指標，本次高價交易是否意在為股價突圍指路，備受投資人關注。

另外，16筆盤後鉅額交易中，有6筆配對、合計201張成交價低於收盤價的2,330元，其中最低成交價為2,300.47元，精準壓在2,300元整數心理關卡之上。

據證交所統計，台積電今日鉅額交易總計成交16筆、共2,078張，成交總金額達48.5億元，平均每股成交價格為2,334.11元。法人分析，在外資籌碼持續鬆動之際，鉅額交易多空分歧擴大，後續2,300元整數支撐能否有效築底，仍將是短線盤勢多空的觀察指標。

news.Title: OpenAI Makes Unusual Move as AI Backlash Grows
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Microsoft ( NASDAQ:MSFT ) backed OpenAI is preparing a broader policy and public-relations push around its massive infrastructure buildout, including a proposal to rebrand traditional data centers as AI compute campuses.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 4 Warning Sign with MSFT.

Is MSFT fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

The company says the new term better reflects the scale and role of the facilities, which combine computing capacity, energy infrastructure and skilled jobs.

An OpenAI spokesperson said the projects are meant to be long-term investments rather than simply server farms, while the company also wants host communities to have a greater role in shaping developments and sharing in the economic benefits.

The timing is important.

The rebranding forms part of a wider campaign OpenAI plans to launch after the Nov. 3 U.S. midterm elections , as artificial intelligence infrastructure becomes a more visible political issue.

Public opposition has been building around large data-center projects because of their electricity demand, water usage and impact on local communities.

A recent Pew Research poll cited by Business Insider found 54% of Americans believe AI data centers are bad for the environment , highlighting the reputational problem OpenAI is trying to address.

The campaign goes beyond branding.

OpenAI is also expected to push for community agreements around infrastructure projects, stronger safeguards for advanced AI systems, worker training programs and a larger U.S. role in setting global AI standards. Chief Global Affairs Officer Chris Lehane has described potential safeguards for more powerful AI systems as speed limits.

Lehane said OpenAI has been developing policy proposals since August and plans to advance them during Congress's lame-duck session beginning Nov. 9.

Investor Takeaway

I think the most important part of this story is that AI infrastructure is becoming a political constraint, not just a capital constraint .

OpenAI and other AI companies already have to secure chips, electricity, land and financing.

Now they increasingly have to win over local communities and policymakers too.

Calling data centers compute campuses does not change their power or water requirements, but it does show how seriously OpenAI is taking the public-perception problem.

For investors, the key things to watch are local permitting battles, electricity costs, community-benefit agreements, state regulation and whether political resistance slows the pace of AI infrastructure deployment .

The AI race still depends on building more compute.

OpenAI is now trying to make that buildout easier to sell politically.

news.Title: Intel's Strong Buy Case Takes a Sudden Hit
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Intel ( NASDAQ:INTC ) suffered a sharp deterioration in investor sentiment after its Seeking Alpha Quant Rating was downgraded to Hold from Strong Buy following the company's third-quarter results and a weaker-than-expected fourth-quarter outlook.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 5 Warning Signs with INTC.

Is INTC fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

The Quant Score fell to 3.26 , a notable reversal for a stock that had previously ranked much more favorably on Seeking Alpha's factor-based system.

The downgrade reflects a broader problem for Intel heading into year-end: expectations had risen, but management's near-term outlook failed to keep pace.

That matters because Intel's recent recovery story has depended heavily on investors believing that the company can stabilize earnings, improve execution, and benefit from stronger AI and data-center demand.

A weaker Q4 outlook challenges that narrative.

When a stock has already rerated on improving expectations, even a modest disappointment can have an outsized impact because investors are no longer judging the company against a depressed baseline.

They are judging it against a much higher bar.

Investor Takeaway

I think the most important part of the Quant downgrade is not the number itself.

It is what the drop to 3.26 says about Intel's changing setup.

The company may still have meaningful long-term catalysts, but the near-term earnings picture has become less supportive just as expectations were rising.

That creates a tougher risk-reward profile.

For investors, the key things to watch are Q4 revenue and margin trends, data-center demand, foundry execution, cost controls, and whether analyst estimates continue moving lower .

Intel's turnaround story is not necessarily broken.

But the market is becoming much less willing to give it the benefit of the doubt.

news.Title: S&P Flags New Risk Behind Meta's AI Push
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Meta Platforms ( NASDAQ:META ) received a fresh warning from the credit market after S&P Global Ratings cut its outlook on the company to negative from stable , citing uncertainty around capital spending and free operating cash flow.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 8 Warning Signs with TSLA.

Is META fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

The ratings agency said Meta's ambitious AI investment plans could push leverage higher and keep free cash flow under pressure for longer than previously expected.

That is a notable shift for a company that has historically generated enormous amounts of cash.

S&P said the concern is not simply that Meta is spending heavily.

It is that investors still have limited visibility into how high capital expenditures could ultimately go and how quickly those investments will translate into meaningful AI monetization.

The agency expects Meta to post a free operating cash flow deficit of roughly $39 billion in 2026 , widening to about $71 billion in 2027 if spending remains elevated.

That could have consequences for the balance sheet.

S&P warned that leverage could rise above 1.0 times if AI monetization takes longer than expected or if Meta continues funding infrastructure through debt.

The ratings agency said the outlook could move back to stable if Meta keeps adjusted leverage below 1.0x and returns to positive free operating cash flow in 2028. That could happen through lower spending, stronger AI monetization, or more non-debt financing.

The warning comes as Meta accelerates investment across data centers, chips and AI infrastructure while also raising external capital to fund the buildout.

Investor Takeaway

I think the biggest change in the Meta story is that the AI buildout is no longer just an earnings and valuation issue .

It is becoming a credit-quality issue too.

That matters because the market has largely tolerated massive capex as long as Meta's balance sheet remained exceptionally strong.

S&P is now warning that this cushion could start shrinking if spending stays elevated and monetization lags.

The key risk is not that Meta suddenly runs out of money.

It is that higher leverage, weaker free cash flow and more external financing could reduce the flexibility investors have become accustomed to.

For investors, the key things to watch are 2027 capex guidance, free cash flow, debt issuance, AI monetization and whether adjusted leverage stays below S&P's 1.0x threshold .

Meta's AI ambition remains enormous.

Now the credit market is asking whether the balance sheet can keep up.

news.Title: Marvell Just Bet $115 Billion On AI's 'Once In A Generation' Opportunity. Should You Buy The Stock?
news.Content:
Marvell (NASDAQ:MRVL) stock fell 13% on Thursday when word of a Lumentum (NASDAQ:LITE) takeover leaked, and the official terms, announced Monday, show what holders are paying. Marvell, which designs chips for data infrastructure, agreed to buy the optical-parts maker for about $115 billion in an all-stock deal, handing Lumentum's owners about a third of the combined company.

What Marvell Holders Give Up

Lumentum shareholders will receive 4.5 Marvell shares for each Lumentum share, or about $1,132 a share, a premium of about 23.9% to the October 28 closing prices, the last trading day before deal speculation began. After closing, current Marvell holders will own about 67% of the combined company on a fully diluted basis, and Lumentum holders about 33%.

So that's roughly a third of the ownership handed over. In the meantime, the deal is not expected to close until the first half of 2028, and it needs approval from both companies' shareholders and from regulators. Both boards approved it unanimously.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Lumentum: A Fast-Growing AI Supplier

Lumentum makes lasers and optical components that link AI chips inside data centers. Its latest quarter, which ended on September 26, brought revenue up 136.5% to $1.26 billion, and it guided to roughly $350 million more next quarter, according to the Monday release.

Marvell CEO Matt Murphy, who stays chairman and CEO, called the moment one that "comes along once in a generation," adding that the companies that move first "will set the standard for decades to come." The companies say the combination expands their addressable market to $550 billion. Three Lumentum directors, including CEO Michael Hurlston, will join Marvell's seven-member board.

Meanwhile, Marvell's own targets are rising: It lifted its fiscal 2028 revenue outlook to $20 billion at its October 6 investor day and set a fiscal 2031 goal of $70 billion to $90 billion in revenue and earnings per share of $30 or more. Its fiscal 2026 diluted earnings per share was $3.07.

Marvell also points to more than $1 billion a year in cost savings, but that is a target the companies see "line of sight" to, rather than a result.

Who the Deal Works For

The sell-off came on higher volume, totaling about 40.4 million shares, which was well above the three-month average of 21.6 million. Investors worried over integration risk specific to the deal, but also more broadly about the massive amounts of AI spending that's impacting cash flow across the sector, as exemplified by Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) stock's record plunge on Friday. Marvell shares are down about 3% in pre-market trading on Monday, suggesting that investors still aren't sure about the deal's potential.

If you believe AI data-center spending has years to run, Marvell just bought a larger slice of it. But if you worry that spending will slow, you now own more of the part of AI that depends on it most, with a long wait and regulatory approval between you and the payoff.

Story Continues

Long-term investors, however, should find comfort in how much demand Marvell has already locked in. In August, it signed a deal to supply chips that sit alongside Google's AI processors, worth up to $120 billion in sales through fiscal 2033. Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA), the company at the center of the AI boom, invested $2 billion each in Marvell and Lumentum earlier this year. And despite the dilution, Marvell says the deal should add to its adjusted earnings per share in the first year after closing.

There's also the price. Since talks were first reported, Marvell shares have tanked over 20% amid the broader chip sell-off. Still, Wall Street hasn't walked away, with Stifel and Piper Sandler both reaffirming bullish ratings during the sell-off, and management, meanwhile, is aiming for $70 billion to $90 billion in revenue and $30 or more in earnings per share by fiscal 2031, up from $3.07 in fiscal 2026. Those targets are ambitious and far from guaranteed. But for investors who can hold through a 2028 closing, today's sell-off means buying into Marvell's biggest AI bet at a lower price than before anyone knew about it.

Marvell's next scheduled earnings report is expected on November 26.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again

In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. If you'd invested $5,000 then, you'd be sitting on $2,660,110 today.*

Now, for the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. It's a key player in the $1.8 trillion space race, and with the stock recently sitting 20% off its highs, the window to get in early is closing fast.

Continue »

news.Title: Tesla's China Problem Gets Harder to Ignore
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Tesla ( NASDAQ:TSLA ) is facing another competitive test in China after BYD, Xiaomi and XPeng all posted strong October sales while Tesla's domestic performance remained under pressure.

BYD sold 490,168 new energy vehicles in October , up 11% from a year earlier and 5.7% from September. It marked the company's highest monthly sales total of 2026 and its sixth consecutive month of year-over-year growth.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 8 Warning Signs with TSLA.

Is TSLA fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

The international picture was even stronger.

BYD's overseas sales jumped 102.8% to 170,194 vehicles , showing that the Chinese automaker is not only competing with Tesla at home but also expanding aggressively abroad.

Xiaomi and XPeng also posted record or near-record numbers.

Xiaomi delivered more than 50,000 vehicles in October, its highest monthly tally of the year and only the second time it has crossed that level.

XPeng delivered 50,237 vehicles , up 19.6% year over year and 21.8% from September, beating its previous monthly record.

Tesla's picture looks less comfortable.

China Passenger Car Association data cited by TipRanks showed Tesla's retail sales in China fell 11.9% year over year during the first nine months of 2026 to 381,088 vehicles . Globally, Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles in the third quarter, down 2% from a year earlier.

Tesla is increasingly relying on exports from its Shanghai factory to keep utilization high.

From January through August, exports from China rose 115% year over year and accounted for about 51% of Tesla's China wholesale sales .

That strategy helps absorb weaker domestic demand, but it also underlines how much more competitive China's EV market has become.

BYD overtook Tesla as the world's largest EV seller in 2025, delivering 2.26 million vehicles compared with Tesla's 1.64 million.

Investor Takeaway

I think the biggest concern for Tesla is not simply that one Chinese rival is growing.

It is that multiple rivals are gaining scale at the same time .

BYD has the volume, Xiaomi is ramping quickly, and XPeng is setting new delivery records. That makes China a much harder market for Tesla to defend without either new products, lower prices, or stronger differentiation.

The rising export mix from Shanghai is useful because it keeps the factory productive.

But it also suggests Tesla is becoming more dependent on overseas demand to offset weaker domestic sales.

For investors, the key things to watch are China retail sales, Shanghai export mix, pricing, Model Y and Model 3 demand, and whether local rivals continue gaining share into year-end .

Tesla still has enormous scale.

But China is becoming a much less forgiving market.

news.Title: Alphabet Makes Another Massive AI Funding Move
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Alphabet ( NASDAQ:GOOG ) is returning to Europe's debt market for the second time this year, launching a seven-part euro bond sale as the Google parent looks for more capital to fund its enormous artificial-intelligence buildout.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 8 Warning Signs with TSLA.

Is GOOG fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

The offering includes maturities ranging from two to 19 years , according to a report cited by Seeking Alpha.

Initial pricing on the shortest fixed-rate tranche was around 60 basis points above mid-swaps , while the longest 19-year notes were being marketed at roughly 205 to 210 basis points above mid-swaps . Barclays, BNP Paribas and Deutsche Bank are managing the transaction, which is expected to price Monday.

The bond sale comes at an important moment.

Alphabet's AI spending has become one of the biggest concerns hanging over the stock after the company's latest earnings report showed rising capital expenditures and deteriorating free cash flow. Reuters recently reported that Alphabet expects 2026 capital spending of up to $205 billion , while its third-quarter free cash flow turned negative as infrastructure investment accelerated.

That makes the new debt issuance more than a routine financing exercise.

Alphabet is increasingly using external capital to support an AI infrastructure race that requires massive investments in data centers, chips and power.

The company already raised about 9 billion through a six-tranche euro bond sale in May , making the latest transaction its second major trip to the European debt market this year.

The broader technology sector is doing the same.

Microsoft recently moved to raise around $25 billion in its first U.S. bond sale in more than nine years, while other hyperscalers have also increased borrowing to preserve cash while maintaining AI investment.

Investor Takeaway

I think the biggest story is not simply that Alphabet is issuing more bonds.

It is that Big Tech's AI boom is increasingly becoming a financing story .

For years, companies such as Alphabet generated so much cash that outside funding barely mattered.

Now the scale of AI infrastructure spending is large enough that even the strongest balance sheets are tapping debt markets repeatedly.

That does not mean Alphabet is facing a liquidity problem.

But it does change the economics of the AI trade.

Higher borrowing spreads, negative free cash flow and enormous capital commitments mean investors increasingly need to see clear returns from Google Cloud, TPUs and AI products to justify the spending.

For investors, the key things to watch are final bond pricing, investor demand, capex guidance, free cash flow and whether borrowing costs continue rising across the technology sector .

Alphabet can still raise the money.

The bigger question is how expensive the AI race becomes.

news.Title: INTC Q3 Earnings Call Highlights AI Demand and PC Weakness
news.Content:
Intel Corporation INTC highlighted surging server processor demand during its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, while warning that memory shortages and weakening PC demand will pressure near-term performance.

Intel reported adjusted earnings of $0.52 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $0.39. Revenues of $16.51 billion surpassed the consensus estimate of $16.44 billion. Management emphasized improving manufacturing execution but acknowledged persistent supply constraints and substantial investment requirements.

Intel Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Intel Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Intel Corporation Quote

Intel's Server Demand Outpaces Available Supply

CEO Lip-Bu Tan said demand for data center processors continues to exceed Intel's manufacturing capacity, supported by expanding AI infrastructure and agentic computing workloads.

Data Center and AI (DCAI) revenues increased 78% year over year to $7.3 billion. CFO David Zinsner attributed the strength to improved server output and broad-based demand across hyperscale, enterprise and cloud customers.

Tan estimated that the server CPU market could expand from $40 billion to more than $200 billion over five years, driven largely by agentic workloads.

INTC Faces a Prolonged PC Market Correction

Zinsner warned that elevated memory prices and constrained availability are forcing PC manufacturers to reduce purchases and inventories.

Client Computing and Physical AI Group revenues declined 5% year over year to $8.1 billion. Management expects industry PC unit shipments to fall approximately 12% in 2026 and roughly 10% in 2027.

During the analyst Q&A, a Bernstein analyst questioned the timing of recovery. Zinsner clarified that inventory adjustments could extend into the second quarter of 2027, while memory-related market weakness is expected to persist throughout the year.

Intel's Fourth-Quarter Outlook Reflects Multiple Pressures

Intel projected fourth-quarter revenues between $15 billion and $16 billion, with non-GAAP earnings of $0.25 per share and gross margin of 38% at the midpoint.

Zinsner expects DCAI revenues to grow at a mid-teens sequential rate, supported by server demand and purpose-built silicon. However, client revenues are projected to decline more than 20% sequentially.

An incident at Intel's Israeli manufacturing facility is expected to reduce fourth-quarter revenues by approximately $300 million and gross margin by 200 basis points.

Responding to a Melius Research analyst, Zinsner indicated that the disruption could have a similar revenue impact in the first quarter of 2027.

Story Continues

INTC Accelerates Manufacturing and Foundry Investments

Tan highlighted improving Intel 3 and Intel 18A yields, alongside expanding manufacturing capacity in Ireland, Oregon and Arizona.

Intel Foundry revenues increased 58% year over year to $6.7 billion, although the segment recorded a $1.9 billion operating loss. Zinsner said Intel 18A production costs have declined approximately 40% since the first quarter.

The company released its Intel 14A process design kit to selected customers in October. Tan also highlighted growing external customer engagement for Intel 18A-P and advanced packaging technologies.

Management expects 2027 capital expenditures to increase substantially from the approximately $20 billion planned for 2026.

Intel's Cash Flow Outlook Draws Analyst Scrutiny

During the Q&A, a UBS analyst questioned whether higher capital spending would prevent positive free cash flow in 2027.

Zinsner acknowledged that 2027 would be an investment-intensive year and indicated that positive free cash flow was not expected.

He emphasized that simultaneous investments in Intel 3, Intel 18A and Intel 14A are necessary to expand production capabilities.

Intel's $23 billion August equity offering strengthened its financial resources. The company ended the third quarter with approximately $54 billion in cash and short-term investments.

INTC's Product Roadmap Supports Long-Term Priorities

Tan highlighted Clearwater Forest server processor shipments and plans to ramp Diamond Rapids in 2027. The company also announced a collaboration with Oracle Cloud Infrastructure supporting future Xeon deployments.

On the client side, Panther Lake production continues expanding, while Nova Lake remains ahead of schedule.

Management also emphasized purpose-built silicon, advanced packaging and external foundry services as longer-term growth opportunities.

Intel Maintains Its Focus on Execution

Management's overall message balanced strong server demand against persistent supply limitations and PC market weakness.

Tan emphasized manufacturing improvements, disciplined capital deployment and product competitiveness, while Zinsner highlighted the investment requirements accompanying Intel's expansion plans.

INTC's Zacks Rank and Style Scores Signal Mixed Strength

Intel currently carries a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), indicating favorable earnings estimate revision trends and stronger near-term performance potential. Its Growth Score of A and Momentum Score of A highlight attractive growth characteristics and favorable price momentum. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here .

However, its Value Score of F indicates weak relative valuation attractiveness, while its VGM Score of C reflects a less compelling combination of value, growth and momentum characteristics.

news.Title: Tower Semiconductor rises on strong Q4 revenue guidance
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Tower Semiconductor ( TSEM ) shares are higher premarket on Monday after reporting its latest quarterly results.

The company reported third-quarter adjusted earnings per share of $1.05, slightly missing the analyst estimate of $1.06, while revenue of $526.2 million beat the consensus estimate of $522.1 million. Revenue grew 33% YoY from $395.7 million in the third quarter of 2025.

The company issued fourth-quarter revenue guidance of approximately $600 million, with an upward or downward range of 5%, significantly above the analyst consensus of $579.7 million. The midpoint of the guidance range represents a 36% increase YoY and a 14% increase quarter-over-quarter.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

"We are entering the strongest growth phase in our history, according to fourth quarter guidance, closing the year at $2 billion annual revenue and a $2.4 billion annualized revenue run rate," said Russell Ellwanger, Chief Executive Officer of Tower Semiconductor.

Third-quarter gross profit reached $178.8 million, up 92% from $93 million in the prior-year period. Operating profit was $127.1 million, excluding non-recurring items, compared to $50.6 million in the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted net profit was $131.3 million, or $1.16 per share on a basic basis, compared to $62.8 million, or $0.56 per share, in the year-ago quarter.

The company highlighted exceptional growth in its high-speed connectivity business, particularly in silicon photonics. Tower targets an annualized $1.1 billion run rate in the fourth quarter of 2026 for SiPho revenue alone, representing 5X the 2025 SiPho annual revenue.

news.Title: Intel stock plunges nearly 29%,  its worst day since 1974
news.Content:
Intel's data center business just grew almost 80% in a year. Its outlook for the fourth quarter just handed the stock its worst day in more than half a century, erasing nearly $140 billion in market value Friday.

Intel ( INTC ) stock closed down nearly 29% Friday after the chipmaker's forecast for the final three months of the year came in well short of Wall Street's expectations.

Only one day in Intel's history was worse, according to Yahoo Finance calculations from Norgate Data closing prices going back to May 1973: July 5, 1974, when the stock fell nearly 30%. Friday's drop topped the roughly 26% plunge on Aug. 2, 2024.

The sell-off caps a wild year. Intel stock nearly quadrupled from the start of 2026 to its June 22 record. Even after Friday's drop, it's still up nearly 80% this year, but it has lost more than half its value since that peak.

It also broke below the $80 zone that held at its July low and closed at its lowest level since April 22. That wipes out April 24, when Intel had its best day since at least 1973, a gain of about 24%.

The selloff is also costing Washington. Intel's drop has shaved more than $10 billion off the value of the US government's 9.9% stake, which it bought last August at $20.47 a share. Even so, the stake is still worth about three times what the government paid.

It has also broken below the $80 zone that held at its July low, and it closed below where it stood before April 24, when Intel had its best day since at least 1973, a gain of about 24%.

The quarter itself was strong. Intel topped estimates with adjusted earnings per share of $0.52, and data center revenue jumped to $7.3 billion.

The outlook is what broke the stock. Intel expects fourth quarter revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion, below the roughly $17 billion analysts expected, and earnings per share of $0.25 against forecasts of $0.43.

The PC market is the problem . AI data centers are soaking up the world's memory chips, pushing up prices for laptops and desktops. Intel now expects PC shipments to fall about 12% this year and another 10% in 2027. An accident at its Israel factory will cost about $300 million in fourth quarter revenue on top of that.

Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon called the outlook "(in a word) terrible" and cut his price target to $75 from $110.

PC makers Dell ( DELL ) and HP ( HPQ ) slid too, adding to a tech stock rout that has hit Alphabet ( GOOGL , GOOG ) and Amazon ( AMZN ) after their reports this week.

Intel said the PC slump won't let up until memory supply and prices return to normal.

Story Continues

"Rebuilding Intel is going to be a multiyear journey, and I remain firmly committed to making it happen," CEO Lip-Bu Tan said on Thursday's earnings call.

news.Title: 台股失守4萬5千點！外資賣超735億 美期中選舉牽動後市
news.Content: 財經中心／綜合報導 台股震盪加劇，外資賣壓持續籠罩市場！台股最新交易日開低走低，儘管尾盤跌幅收斂，終場仍下跌291點，收在44,920點，失守45,000點整數關卡。隨著美股回檔，加上美國期中選舉即將登場，市場觀望氣氛升溫。不過，儘管短線股市承壓，AI產業長期成長趨勢仍受到關注，後續法人資金動向及企業基本面，將成為影響台股走勢的重要關鍵。 受到美股走弱及科技股賣壓影響，台股近期持續修正。從法人籌碼觀察，外資單日賣超高達735億元，連續3個交易日站在賣方，成為壓抑大盤的重要因素。不過，外資期貨空單也同步減少2,862口，淨空單降至89,379口，顯示部分空方部位開始回補。相較之下，投信則持續站在買方，單日買超達360億元，寫下史上第三大買超紀錄，並連續15個交易日加碼，形成外資賣、投信買的不同調局面。短線台股仍容易受到外資賣超權值股影響，造成指數震盪，但從中長期角度觀察，企業營運表現與產業發展趨勢，仍是評估個股投資價值的重要依據。 美國11月3日登場的期中選舉，進一步牽動美股及台股表現。（圖／民視財經網）除了外資動向，美國11月3日登場的期中選舉，也成為全球金融市場關注焦點。若選後國會權力結構改變，可能影響美國未來政策推動，進一步牽動美股及台股表現。從歷史統計來看，過去23次美國期中選舉年當中，有20次第四季美股呈現上漲，比例約87%。其中，政治不確定性逐步消除，被視為推動市場回穩的重要因素之一。不過，今年市場環境與過往不同，除了利率壓力仍在，部分選舉結果也可能已提前反映在股價當中，加上郵寄選票可能拉長計票時間，一旦選舉結果遲遲無法確定，恐怕進一步加劇金融市場波動。 近期AI概念股也出現明顯修正，引發市場對產業成長動能的疑慮。不過，目前AI供應鏈面臨的挑戰，除了股價估值調整，也包括部分關鍵零組件供應不足，導致下游廠商無法按照原定時程出貨。包括CPU、高頻寬記憶體（HBM）等關鍵零組件供應吃緊，都可能影響AI伺服器組裝進度。從供應鏈營收表現觀察，先進封裝、銅箔基板（CCL）等上游產業需求仍相對強勁，但部分零組件及組裝廠商的月營收卻出現下滑，反映出貨排程可能受到影響。因此，接下來公布的10月營收，將成為觀察AI供應鏈能否改善缺料、恢復正常交貨的重要指標。若中下游廠商營收重新轉強，將有助於確認出貨動能回升；反之，若上游與下游營收同步走弱，就需要進一步留意需求是否出現變化。 另一方面，隨著AI技術快速發展，網路攻擊及資訊安全問題也受到市場關注。日本近期遭遇密集資安攻擊事件，凸顯企業在數位轉型過程中，必須更加重視系統防護與第三方供應商管理。AI技術不只帶動運算需求，也可能增加企業面臨的資安威脅，促使政府及企業提高資訊安全預算，進一步帶動資安軟體、系統防護及相關服務需求。不過，資安支出增加也可能提高企業營運成本，因此相關商機能否轉化為實際獲利，仍有待後續觀察。

news.Title: Marvell to purchase Lumentum for $115 billion in record-breaking tech deal
news.Content:
What happened: Marvell Technology ( MRVL ) fell more than 3% on Monday after the chipmaker announced it will acquire optical component maker Lumentum ( LITE ) for $115 billion, in what would be the largest merger between two publicly traded companies on record. Lumentum shares also slipped following the announcement.

What's behind the move: The record breaking agreement is expected to expand the combined company's total addressable market to $550 billion, according to the announcment.

"AI infrastructure is undergoing a fundamental architectural shift toward optical connectivity, creating an opportunity that comes along once in a generation," Matt Murphy, chairman and CEO of Marvell, said on Monday.

Lumentum shareholders will receive four and a half shares of Marvell stock for every share of Lumentum stock they own. The deal values Lumentum at approximately $115 billion, or $1,132 per share, representing a 23.9% premium over its Oct. 28 closing share price.

Marvell's market cap stood at $176 billion on Monday morning, while Lumentum's hovered near $76 billion.

What else you need to know: The acquisition gives Marvell greater access to optical technologies and manufacturing capacity, which have become critical bottlenecks of the AI infrastructure build-out.

Lumentum makes lasers and other optical components as increasingly powerful AI systems require faster connections. Marvell, which competes with Broadcom ( AVGO ), designs high-speed infrastructure and custom chips that enable AI computers to communicate with one another.

Earlier this year, Marvell stock rallied sharply after AI chip heavyweight Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang described the chip designer as "the next trillion-dollar company."

The company joined the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) index in June. Marvell shares are up more than 130% year to date. Lumentum shares have rallied 128%.

news.Title: Nomura flags this tech pocket as ’portfolio shelter’ from AI spending pressure
news.Content:
Investing.com -- One corner of the tech sector offers "portfolio shelter" from the AI spending race, Nomura analysts say, pointing to deteriorating cash flow in big tech while cash piles up at companies on the other side of the trade, whose valuations assume earnings have peaked.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

Analysts led by CW Chung said third-quarter results from five big tech companies reaffirmed that "AI investment cannot stop." But the companies' financial strength is pulling apart. Quarterly free cash flow turned negative at Meta, at minus $2.1 billion, its first time since its IPO, and at Alphabet, at minus $9.1 billion for a second straight quarter.

Amazon's trailing 12-month free cash flow was minus $42.4 billion. Only Microsoft stayed positive, at $18.6 billion.

Meta, Alphabet and Amazon have halted buybacks and are widening their funding through equity and debt. Markets rewarded only positive free cash flow at Microsoft and investment backed by revenue visibility at SpaceX, Nomura analysts said.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

None of the five companies gave a 2027 capex figure, though all signaled an increase. Applying the 60% growth in 2027 cloud-provider capex cited by SK Hynix would imply about $1.2 trillion for the four hyperscalers, versus market expectations of 30% to 35% growth.

Under that scenario, their combined free cash flow would turn negative at $144 billion in 2027, from $289 billion in 2025, with the gap filled by debt and equity. "Resources will flow to the winners with the capacity to raise funds," the analysts wrote.

Nomura's answer to where investors can find shelter is memory. The analysts said big tech's negative free cash flow "is only beginning," with the deficit likely to widen over the next one to two years as investment rises. In contrast, they expect shareholder returns at memory makers to "multiply" and cash holdings to grow several-fold.

"Ironically," analysts said, memory makers trade at 2 to 3 times 2027 estimated earnings, an 85% to 90% discount to the four big techs at about 20.9 times. Samsung Electronics trades at about 3.2 times and SK Hynix at about 2.8 times.

Current valuations treat today's memory earnings as the peak, Nomura noted, but with shortages lasting through 2028 and more long-term supply agreements, "the market's assumption about how long these earnings will last is too weak."

news.Title: Down 44.9% in 4 Weeks, Here's Why Intel (INTC) Looks Ripe for a Turnaround
news.Content:
Intel (INTC) has been on a downward spiral lately with significant selling pressure. After declining 44.9% over the past four weeks, the stock looks well positioned for a trend reversal as it is now in oversold territory and there is strong agreement among Wall Street analysts that the company will report better earnings than they predicted earlier.

We use Relative Strength Index (RSI), one of the most commonly used technical indicators, for spotting whether a stock is oversold. This is a momentum oscillator that measures the speed and change of price movements.

RSI oscillates between zero and 100. Usually, a stock is considered oversold when its RSI reading falls below 30.

Technically, every stock oscillates between being overbought and oversold irrespective of the quality of their fundamentals. And the beauty of RSI is that it helps you quickly and easily check if a stock's price is reaching a point of reversal.

So, by this measure, if a stock has gotten too far below its fair value just because of unwarranted selling pressure, investors may start looking for entry opportunities in the stock for benefiting from the inevitable rebound.

However, like every investing tool, RSI has its limitations, and should not be used alone for making an investment decision.

Why a Trend Reversal is Due for INTC

The heavy selling of INTC shares appears to be in the process of exhausting itself, as indicated by its RSI reading of 25.03. So, the trend for the stock could reverse soon for reaching the old equilibrium of supply and demand.

The RSI value is not the only factor that indicates a potential turnaround for the stock in the near term. On the fundamental side, there has been strong agreement among the sell-side analysts covering the stock in raising earnings estimates for the current year. Over the last 30 days, the consensus EPS estimate for INTC has increased 2.5%. And an upward trend in earnings estimate revisions usually translates into price appreciation in the near term.

Moreover, INTC currently has a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), which means it is in the top 5% of more than 4,000 stocks that we rank based on trends in earnings estimate revisions and EPS surprises. This is a more conclusive indication of the stock's potential turnaround in the near term. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here >>>> .

news.Title: My Top 3 AI Stock Picks for November
news.Content:
2026 is coming to a close, but that doesn't mean investors should ignore the remaining months. In fact, November averages the highest S&P 500 (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC) monthly returns of any month. Now, whether this will hold in 2026 is still a mystery, but I believe there are several attractive stocks that investors should consider buying at today's levels.

At the top of my shopping list are Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA), Micron (NASDAQ: MU), and Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO). All three of these companies have deep roots in the AI build-out, and each looks like a smart buy right now.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Huge demand is coming for these three

All three of these stocks are central pieces of the AI build-out.

Nvidia makes the world's leading AI computing units. Its graphics processing units (GPUs) have become the industry standard for AI computing, and every other computing unit is compared to their price and performance. Nvidia has been the top AI investment since the AI build-out kicked off in 2023, yet 2026 hasn't been its best year, at least from a stock perspective. Nvidia has delivered incredible growth, with it reporting a 106% growth rate last quarter. The future is also bright, because Nvidia informed investors that 2027's revenue growth will be about 70%. Those are strong future projections and make Nvidia a smart stock to invest in now.

Broadcom is an Nvidia challenger. While Nvidia's GPUs excel in just about any situation, Broadcom is taking a different approach to AI computing. It's working directly with AI hyperscalers to design computing units tailored to their workloads. This allows its custom AI chips to outperform Nvidia GPUs in these scenarios and drives down usage costs.

While not every application can use a custom AI chip, a growing number of them can, and Broadcom expects to deliver monster growth over the next few years. For 2026, it expects AI semiconductor revenue to be about $58 billion. That figure will double to $115 billion in 2027, and $230 billion in 2028. That's huge growth in the next few years, and shareholders should see massive gains in the near future.

Both Broadcom's and Nvidia's computing units require memory chips inside them to function properly, and one of the biggest manufacturers of those is Micron. The memory chip industry came under scrutiny in 2026, as it didn't have enough supply to meet demand. It's not going to get any better, as Micron's CEO noted that market conditions will likely get tighter in 2027 and 2028 than they were in 2026.

Story Continues

While that's not great news for its clients, it's great news for Micron, and as a result, its investors. Micron will likely continue to experience huge revenue and earnings growth over the next few years as the AI build-out stays intense. Even after the AI build-out is wrapped up, Micron has now started to get its clients to sign supply agreements that will decrease the severity of any market downturns. This is great for Micron's future and will likely lead to strong performance.

But just how good of a return can investors expect?

2027 will be huge for this trio
