news.Title: Buy, Sell, or Hold Alphabet Stock After Its $505 Billion Meltdown?
news.Content:
Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG) (NASDAQ: GOOGL) fell 12.6% last Thursday, bringing its market cap down $505 billion in a single session.

Alphabet now has a negative year-to-date return and is down 30.5% from its all-time high.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Here's why investors are reacting so negatively to Alphabet's third-quarter results, and if the sell-off is a buying opportunity for the communication services stock .

Alphabet's capital expenditures increased 114%

At first glance, Alphabet's results were excellent. Revenue jumped 25% year-over-year to $128 billion, giving Alphabet a half-trillion annual run rate. Google Cloud revenue more than doubled, and operating income shot up a staggering 30%.

What investors didn't like, however, was that capital expenditures (capex) skyrocketed 114% to $51.36 billion, pushing Alphabet's free cash flow (FCF) in the quarter down to a negative $9.07 billion. In the third quarter of 2025, Alphabet's FCF was $24.46 billion. The cash burn will get worse before it gets better. On its Q3 earnings call, Alphabet said it expects full-year 2026 capex to be $195 to $205 billion and capex to increase significantly in 2027.

Alphabet turning FCF-negative has impacts on its capital return program and balance sheet. In the first three quarters of 2025, Alphabet spent $39.81 billion on stock purchases. Through Sept. 30, 2026, year-to-date buybacks have been $0. As of Dec. 31, 2025, Alphabet had $46.55 billion in long-term debt. As of Sept. 30, 2026, its long-term debt jumped to $125.5 billion -- which is a red flag, considering interest rates are rising and will make the cost of taking on additional debt even more expensive.

Alphabet has been taking on debt and issuing stock to fund its artificial intelligence (AI) build-out . During the three months ended Sept. 30, 2026, Alphabet issued 12 million shares of Class A stock and 24 million shares of Class C stock for a combined net proceeds of $12.4 billion, with $27.6 billion remaining for future issuance.

So in the span of just one year, Alphabet has gone from managing its AI ramp-up with FCF while still reducing its share count throughout buybacks to turning FCF negative, taking on debt, and diluting shareholders.

The leverage and lack of FCF put significant pressure on Alphabet to prove to investors that it is getting a good return on its spending. And to be fair, there are already many positive signs -- including excellent Gemini traction, positive updates with self-driving car company Waymo, and a boom in Google Cloud. But part of the surge in Google Cloud revenue is due to one-time chip sales, as Alphabet includes sales of its custom Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) chips under its Google Cloud revenue.

Story Continues

Google Search revenue was up 12% year-over-year, and YouTube ads revenue increased 9.2% -- which isn't bad but, it's a slowdown compared to Q3 2025 when Google Search revenue increased 14.5% and, YouTube ads jumped 15% year-over-year.

An AI ecosystem unlike any other

Alphabet is at a crossroads. Investors who don't believe in the payoff of its record capex may choose to sell the stock. Others who are skeptical but want to see how things play out may simply want to hold. I think Alphabet is misunderstood and a high conviction buy.

Operationally, Alphabet is at the top of its game -- with 32% operating margins in its latest quarter. On the earnings call, Alphabet said that around 65% of capex is in technology infrastructure like servers and networking equipment, which generally have useful lives of six years, and the remaining 35% is for data centers with useful lives ranging from seven to 40 years. Meaning that those investments aren't contributing to Alphabet's near-term results, but they will benefit the company over the long term.

Of all the hyperscalers, Alphabet is arguably the best positioned to invest aggressively in AI because it controls almost every layer of the AI ecosystem. It partners with Broadcom to manufacture TPUs, which have proven excellent for AI training and inference. As mentioned, Alphabet isn't just using TPUs in-house, but is now also selling them to third parties, which is contributing to Google Cloud revenue. In April, Anthropic expanded its partnership with Google and Broadcom for multiple gigawatts of TPU capacity. That same month, Broadcom and Google entered into a long-term TPU agreement through 2031.

In addition to its TPU boost, Google Cloud is now taking market share from Amazon and Microsoft in the cloud computing industry. Alphabet also has Gemini, powered by Google DeepMind, which is a legitimate heavyweight in frontier models alongside Anthropic's Claude, OpenAI's ChatGPT, and xAI's Grok, owned by Space Exploration Technologies .

And to top it all off, Alphabet has consumer and enterprise apps in Gemini, Google Search, Android, and YouTube, and is a massive investor in physical AI through Waymo.

The perfect AI stock for long-term investors

Alphabet's results look bad now because it's in the midst of a historic AI spending build-out, but it's not just throwing money at ideas and hoping it sticks. Rather, it has multiple levers to pull to monetize AI.

For that reason, I think Alphabet stands out as arguably one of the best AI stocks for patient long-term investors to buy now. But I could also see the sell-off worsening before it gets better, given Alphabet's accelerated cash burn.

news.Title: Apple has turned into Wall Street's hedge against the AI trade: Chart of the Day
news.Content: When AI stocks get hit, investors have found a place to hide. It's the company that has mostly sat out the AI spending race — Apple ( AAPL ). Chip stocks have had plenty of rough days this year, and Apple has mostly shrugged them off. On the 46 days the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index ( ^SOX ) fell 2% or more, Apple rose on 30, about two out of every three. That's new. From 1994 through last year, Apple rose on only about 1 in 6 of those days, and no year came anywhere close to this one, by Yahoo Finance's calculations. Apple and chip stocks have basically stopped moving together. Apple's correlation with the chip index — a measure of how closely two assets move in step — turned negative in July and hit its lowest level on record in September. The payoff showed up Friday. Over the past month, Apple gained about 3% while the iShares Semiconductor ETF ( SOXX ) tumbled about 17%. That gap pushed Apple back past Nvidia ( NVDA ) as Wall Street's most valuable company Friday. It isn't just a one-month thing, either. Apple is up about 27% this year, more than double the S&P 500's ( ^GSPC ) gain. So why Apple? Follow the money. Over their past four reported quarters, Amazon ( AMZN ), Alphabet ( GOOGL ), Microsoft ( MSFT ), and Meta ( META ) spent more than $600 billion on capital expenditures — the money companies invest in long-lasting assets like data centers and chips — much of it to build out artificial intelligence. Apple spent about $10 billion. Investors have started to sweat that bill. Alphabet, Amazon, and Meta all just reported negative free cash flow , meaning they spent more than their businesses brought in. Amazon's cash burn hit a record , and Alphabet's stock just wrapped up its worst month ever . No wonder investors have been rushing into Apple's AI-light arms . But a hedge isn't a force field. Friday was chip stocks' worst day since June, and Apple still fell about 1%. Apple can't fully escape the AI boom, either. It's paying more for memory chips, the same parts AI data centers are snapping up. Bank of America's Wamsi Mohan estimated those costs will take a real bite out of iPhone profit margins, and he thinks Wall Street's margin forecasts are too high into next year. "Our estimates are below Street heading into earnings," BofA wrote in a note on Friday that kept a Buy rating on the stock. Apple reports its fiscal fourth quarter results after the bell Monday, with iPhone 18 sales in the spotlight . Its outlook for December quarter margins will show whether the market's favorite AI hedge has an AI problem of its own. news.Title: 跌破半年線慘了！陳嘉偉示警台股剛進「初跌段」　揭這時間爆奪命回馬槍
news.Content:
台北股市近期隨國際走勢陷入劇烈震盪，分析師陳嘉偉於《股市總司令》節目中指出，加權指數在跌破半年線關鍵支撐後，市場氣氛已正式「由多轉空」，宣告行情僅剛進入「初跌段」。他分析，大盤近期雖靠金融與塑化等非電子股撐盤，但電子權值股與高槓桿標的早已率先下修；投資人應採取鋸齒狀空頭思維，在大跌時適度回補過度超跌的個股，並把握美國大選期間可能出現的急彈逃命波（奪命回馬槍）重新佈局空單，慎防後續「年線對稱跌幅」的長線修整壓力。

鋸齒狀下跌靈活應變 空單獲利回補等待再放空

針對短線的操作策略，陳嘉偉強調股市下跌必定呈現「鋸齒狀走勢」，當個股出現長黑急殺且短線跌幅已達 30% 以上時，盲目追空容易遭遇強烈反彈吞噬獲利。因此，團隊在上週五已將連跌數日、獲利豐厚的晶圓代工與記憶體族群（如聯電、世界先進、華邦電、南亞科及矽晶圓等）空單進行獲利回補，鎖定戰果；然而針對矽光子與被動元件等族群則維持空單，預期在 10 月營收陸續公布後，基本面壓力將持續加重相關個股的補跌風險。

台積電三個缺口露疲態 灰犀牛引爆融資籌碼賣壓

針對大盤指標台積電，陳嘉偉直言其技術面已呈現典型的大空頭架構，不僅短線連續留下三個跳空缺口，季線與月線更相繼下彎，但市場融資餘額卻逆勢創下新高，籌碼面極度不安。他指出，這次大盤的重挫並非無法預期、急跌後會創新高的「黑天鵝」，而是市場長期無視 AI 資本支出過熱與籌碼過度槓桿所導致的「灰犀牛」風險；當灰犀牛利空開始發酵，即便權值股也難以單靠市場樂觀情緒抵禦整體產業的修正週期。

美選恐現「奪命回馬槍」 長線慎防年線對稱跌幅

展望後續行情，陳嘉偉預測隨著美國期中選舉等政治變數登場，台股在短期連續重挫後，極可能隨國際消息面順勢拉出一根急強反彈的長紅 K 棒，即所謂的「奪命回馬槍」。但他特別提醒，此類急彈絕非趨勢翻多止跌，而是提供多頭逃命與空方絕佳的加碼空點。若對照 1997 年亞洲金融風暴與 2008 年金融海嘯等歷史經驗，大盤在失守半年線後，未來恐面臨「年線對稱跌幅」、甚至向五年線尋求支撐的深層修正風險，投資人切勿輕易盲目摸底。

Factors Shaping Upcoming Results

During the quarter, Qualcomm completed the acquisition of Modular, adding an AI-native software platform designed to optimize and deploy generative and agentic AI workloads across CPUs, GPUs, NPUs and custom silicon. It has also announced a multi-generational collaboration with Amazon to develop customized silicon for AI inference and advanced optical connectivity for AWS data centers. Despite these positive developments, Qualcomm's prospects are impacted by several factors.

Memory pricing, supply constraints and OEM builds continue to weigh on the smartphone business. The semiconductor supply chain is operating near full utilization, with shortages and cost increases across wafers, assembly, test, advanced packaging, memory and other materials. Profitability also remains a concern. Higher costs across wafer fabrication, assembly, testing and advanced packaging have already weakened QCT margins, while the benefits of product price increases are likely to take time to materialize.

Moreover, Qualcomm's expansion into data center infrastructure involves considerable execution risks. Its ambitious revenue targets will require successful product development, timely commercialization and sustained customer adoption.

Qualcomm's efforts to establish a stronger presence in automotive, IoT and AI computing markets have expanded its long-term growth opportunities. However, the company's dependence on the smartphone market, declining Apple-related revenues and industry-wide supply constraints continue to create significant challenges. The pressure on QCT margins, combined with higher operating expenses and the uncertain profitability of its emerging data center business, raises concerns about the sustainability of earnings growth. news.Title: 00949擬配3.02元配息率衝破13% 掀起日股ETF高息話題
news.Content:
近期全球科技股波動加劇，市場資金開始重新檢視投資組合的風險分散與收益來源。日股ETF配息表現也成為市場關注焦點，其中復華日本龍頭(00949-TW)最新宣布配發每受益權單位3.02元，以今(2)日收盤價 22.1 元推算，年配息率突破 13%，不僅展現亮眼的收益表現，更寫下台灣掛牌日股ETF的配息新紀錄。

過去台灣掛牌的日本股票ETF，多以追蹤日本主要股價指數、掌握日股長期成長機會為訴求，配息並非市場關注的主要焦點。相較之下，00949此次宣布配發3.02元，以推估年配息率超過13%的水準來看，明顯有別於過往日股ETF的配息表現。若與市場既有日股ETF歷史配息紀錄比較，過去尚未出現年化配息率突破10%的案例，此次配息因此格外受到矚目。

值得注意的是，近期美國大型科技股及AI相關族群受到市場對企業資本支出、獲利成長與評價水準的重新檢視，股價波動明顯加大。在全球股市連動性提高的環境下，投資人若過度集中於單一市場或科技產業，投資組合可能承受較大的短期波動。因此，透過不同國家與產業的資產配置分散風險，重要性也隨之提升。

日本股市近年受惠於企業治理改革、股東報酬意識提升，以及企業積極推動資本效率改善，逐漸吸引國際資金關注。相較於高度集中在少數大型科技企業的投資組合，日本市場涵蓋金融、工業、消費、汽車及電子等多元產業，可作為投資人拓展海外股票配置的選項之一。

市場人士指出，對於已持有美股科技ETF、台灣科技型ETF或AI相關投資部位的投資人而言，適度納入日股ETF，不僅有助於拓展投資區域，也能增加不同產業與企業獲利來源的曝險。若搭配具備配息機制的產品，更可兼顧海外股市參與及現金流需求，提升投資組合的配置彈性。

不過，投資人仍須留意，ETF配息率並不等同於投資報酬率，單次高額配息也不代表未來能持續維持相同水準。評估日股ETF時，除觀察配息金額與年化配息率外，也應綜合考量基金淨值變化、配息來源、總報酬表現、匯率風險及標的指數特性，避免單純以高配息率作為投資依據。

news.Title: Intel Logs Worst Daily Drop Since 1970s: Buy the Dip With ETFs?
news.Content:
Chip behemoth Intel 's INTC shares plunged 29% on Oct. 30, 2026, marking their worst single-day decline since the 1970s, per CNBC. The sharp selloff followed weaker-than-expected guidance from the chipmaker, which cited a plant shutdown in Israel and continued weakness in the PC market.Intel's client business is also facing memory shortages.

The steep decline is a major setback for the company, which has been trying to turn around its business after it missed out on the early stages of the artificial intelligence (AI) boom. INTC shares are up 29% over the past five years, compared with chip behemoth NVIDIA NVDA's 588% gains (as of Oct. 30, 2026).

Before Thursday's earnings announcement, Intel shares had enjoyed a strong rally since April this year.  The rally was supported by rising demand for central processing units (CPUs), which are becoming increasingly important for agentic AI workloads. However, the disappointing outlook quickly changed investor sentiment.

AI Spending Concerns Add to Investor Nervousness

Intel's selloff comes at a time when investors are questioning whether massive AI investments by big technology companies will generate adequate returns.

Weak PC Market Weighs on Intel's Outlook

A key reason behind Intel's cautious forecast is the slowdown in the PC market. Surging prices of memory chips and other components are putting pressure on the industry. Management expects the PC slowdown to continue at least through the first half of next year.

Intel expects adjusted earnings of 25 cents per share in the current quarter, on revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion. Both forecasts fell short of analysts' expectations. According to LSEG, analysts had projected earnings of 43 cents per share and revenue of $17.1 billion, as quoted on the same CNBC article.

Foundry Business Remains Critical to Intel's Turnaround

Intel's foundry business remains central to its turnaround strategy, although the segment has struggled to attract external customers. Foundry revenues climbed 58% year over year. External foundry revenues were $411 million, up $118 million sequentially, primarily due to a non-recurring customer program.

The company is the only U.S.-based manufacturer of advanced logic chips. This gives U.S. customers an alternative to Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC), the world's leading contract chipmaker, as mentioned by CNBC.

Intel's next Arizona fab is expected to begin operations by the end of 2028. However, the company has yet to secure external customers for its new chips.

Story Continues

Any Bright Points in the Earnings Results?

Intel's third-quarter 2026 adjusted earnings and revenues beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate. Strong demand for server processors supported top-line growth despite weakness in the PC market.

Non-GAAP earnings surged 126.1% year over year to 52 cents per share, surpassing the consensus estimate of 39 cents. Revenues increased 20.9% to $16.51 billion, beating the consensus estimate of $16.44 billion.

Data Center and AI revenues jumped 78% year over year, reflecting strong demand across hyperscale, enterprise and neo-cloud customers.

AI PC revenues grew 35% year over year. Wildcat Lake processor shipments increased approximately 70% sequentially, with available supply selling out.

Bottom Line

The company may be making progress despite the challenges. Global memory shortages are already well known to all. However, Intel's valuation had become stretched, with a trailing 12-month price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 47.65X, compared with the semiconductor-general industry's P/E of 22.60X.

The latest selloff probably corrected some of Intel's rich valuation. Intel's expected growth rate of more than 200% for this year outpaces the industry average of 12.7%. Intel is a strong-growth stock, though it falls short in terms of its Value Score.

Investors can consider buying the dip in Intel through ETFs with significant exposure to the stock. The ETF or basket approach minimizes company-specific concentration risks. INTC-heavy ETFs include Defiance Global Foundries ETF AIFR, iShares Semiconductor ETF SOXX, First Trust Nasdaq Semiconductor ETF FTXL, Invesco Semiconductors ETF PSI and State Street SPDR NYSE Technology ETF XNTK.

news.Title: Intel Stock Cratered 28%, Opening a Massive Buying Opportunity for Investors Looking for a Stock That Could Nearly Double
news.Content:
Shares of Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) have been in phenomenal form on the stock market since the beginning of 2025, rising by 225% as of this writing, but Chipzilla's investors received a huge shock after the release of its third-quarter 2026 results on Oct. 29.

Intel stock plunged more than 28% the following day. Investors were spooked by the company's guidance, which was affected by the poor performance of its personal computer (PC) business. However, a closer look at Intel's numbers and guidance suggests that the stock is only taking a breather.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Let's look at the reasons why this semiconductor stock could overcome this setback and soar once again.

Image source: Getty Images.

Intel's PC business is struggling, but its data center business has taken off

Intel's Q4 revenue increased 21% year over year to $16.5 billion. Even better, its non-GAAP earnings per share jumped by an incredible 126% from the year-ago period to $0.52. Wall Street would have settled for $0.40 in adjusted earnings per share on revenue of $16.5 billion, suggesting that Intel's bottom-line performance was well ahead of expectations.

However, the company's guidance led investors to press the panic button. The company expects revenue of $15-$16 billion in the current quarter, along with adjusted earnings per share of $0.25. Analysts were anticipating $0.43 in earnings per share on $17.1 billion in revenue. So, it is easy to see why Intel stock was hammered badly following its results.

The primary reason behind Intel's poor outlook is the PC business. The company's client computing and physical artificial intelligence (AI) business segment saw revenue drop 5% from the year-ago period to $8.1 billion. Intel management noted on the earnings call that the pace of the PC market slowdown has accelerated over the past couple of months, driven by high component costs that are weighing on IT budgets.

Intel noted that it expects "the current environment to persist until memory availability and prices begin to normalize." This statement indicates that Intel's client computing business faces sustained pressure, especially given its expectation that the PC market will shrink by 10% in 2027. However, Intel's data center business is more than making up for the decline in PCs.

Story Continues

Its data center and AI (DCAI) segment revenue jumped 78% year over year to $7.3 billion, driven by solid demand for its server central processing units (CPUs) that handle inference and agentic AI workloads in data centers. Importantly, Intel's server CPUs are gaining popularity among customers, with Oracle deciding to deploy its next-generation Diamond Rapids platform to power its cloud infrastructure.

At the same time, Intel's custom AI processor business is also gaining solid traction. The company noted that this is its "fastest growing business segment, tripling over the last 3 years and poised to triple again over the next few years." As such, there is a strong chance that the robust performance of the DCAI business will enable Intel to offset the weakness of the PC segment until the latter stabilizes.

Market research firm IDC expects the PC market to start growing again from 2028, so the pain Intel is facing in this segment may not last beyond next year. Additionally, Intel notes that it expects stronger demand from data center customers and that the market for data center chips will remain tight on supply in both 2027 and 2028.

This should help Intel deliver strong earnings growth on the back of favorable pricing. In fact, the company's earnings are expected to jump once again in the current quarter despite the challenging PC environment. The midpoint of its Q4 revenue guidance implies a 13% jump from the year-ago period, along with an impressive 67% increase in earnings per share.

So, Intel continues to clock impressive earnings growth even though it isn't firing on all cylinders. Once the PC market starts recovering from 2028, I won't be surprised to see Intel's growth accelerating further.

Investors are getting a solid deal on this growth stock right now

If you're looking to construct a million-dollar portfolio and want to buy a top growth stock trading at an attractive valuation right now, Intel seems like an ideal candidate. That's because Intel trades at an attractive 31 times forward earnings, which isn't very expensive considering that the iShares Semiconductor ETF , which tracks the semiconductor sector, has a price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 46.

Moreover, analysts expect Intel's earnings growth to continue at a solid pace.

INTC EPS Estimates for Current Fiscal Year data by YCharts

Even better, the long-term earnings-per-share growth estimates for Intel are a handsome 75%.

INTC EPS LT Growth Estimates data by YCharts

As such, there is a strong likelihood that this AI stock will regain its mojo. Let's say Intel's earnings per share reach $3.14 in 2028 (based on YCharts estimates), and it trades at 40 times earnings; its stock price could jump to $126. That's 90% higher than Intel's price right now, suggesting that this beaten-down chipmaker could almost double in just over two years.

So, the recent slide in Intel seems like a golden opportunity for investors to buy a top stock that could make them significantly richer.

news.Title: TSM Soars 33% in the Past Year: Is It a Solid Investment Proposition?
news.Content:
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company TSM has surged 33.2% in the past year compared with the broader sector's growth of 6.8%. It has outperformed GLOBALFOUNDRIES Inc. GFS but lagged United Microelectronics Corporation UMC during this period. While GFS has jumped 17.5%, UMC gained 112.7%.

TSM is benefiting from accelerating artificial intelligence (AI) investments, growing demand for advanced semiconductor technologies and aggressive global manufacturing expansion. The company's technological leadership, strong profitability and robust demand outlook position it favorably for sustained growth, making the stock an attractive investment proposition.

One-Year TSM Stock Price Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

AI Boom Fuels Long-Term Growth Prospects

TSM remains a key beneficiary of accelerating investments in AI infrastructure. Growing demand for AI accelerators, custom chips, networking processors and agentic AI applications is driving the adoption of its advanced manufacturing technologies. Management previously projected AI accelerator revenues to grow at a mid-to-high-50% compound annual rate between 2024 and 2029. On the third-quarter 2026 earnings call, management indicated that growth could exceed this projection, reflecting robust customer demand.

High-performance computing (HPC) revenues increased 22% sequentially in the third quarter, accounting for 68% of total revenues, up from 57% a year earlier. This expanding contribution underscores TSMC's increasing exposure to high-growth AI markets.

Advanced Process Leadership Strengthens Competitive Position

TSM's leadership in cutting-edge semiconductor manufacturing provides a significant competitive advantage. Advanced technologies, comprising 7-nanometer and smaller nodes, contributed 79% of wafer revenues in the third quarter of 2026.

The 2-nanometer technology accounted for 8% of wafer revenues, up from 3% in the preceding quarter. Management expects N2-family annual capacity to more than double in 2027, supported by robust smartphone and HPC/AI demand. Its next-generation A14 technology remains on track for risk production in 2027 and volume production in 2028, strengthening long-term growth opportunities.

Aggressive Capacity Expansion Supports Rising Demand

TSM is accelerating manufacturing investments to capitalize on sustained semiconductor demand. The company reiterated its 2026 capital expenditure budget of $60-$64 billion and expects investments during 2026-2028 to significantly exceed those of the preceding three years.

The company is developing nearly 20 fabrication facilities globally. Its second Arizona fab is scheduled to begin volume production in the third quarter of 2027, while additional 3-nanometer capacity in Taiwan is expected to become operational during 2027 and 2028. These investments should strengthen supply capabilities and support future revenue growth.

Story Continues

Robust Financial Performance Reinforces Growth Momentum

TSM's third-quarter 2026 revenues surged 41.2% year over year to $46.72 billion, while net income jumped 68.7%. Gross margin expanded 690 basis points year over year to 66.4%. Management expects fourth-quarter revenues of $52.3-$54.3 billion, representing approximately 58% year-over-year growth at the midpoint. The company also projects full-year 2026 revenue growth of roughly 44% in U.S. dollar terms.

Strong Profitability and Cash Generation Support Investments

TSM generated approximately NT$920 billion in operating cash flow during the third quarter, demonstrating its ability to finance substantial capacity investments. Its 58.7% operating margin highlights strong profitability despite rising manufacturing complexity.

Although overseas expansion and the N2 ramp-up could pressure near-term margins, favorable demand trends, technological leadership and solid cash generation reinforce TSM's compelling financial flexibility.

Estimate Revision Trend

TSM is currently witnessing an uptrend in estimate revisions. Earnings estimates for TSM for 2026 have moved up 38.9% to $17.07 over the past year, while the same for 2027 has increased 56.6% to $22.44. The positive estimate revision portrays bullish sentiment about the stock's growth potential.

End Note

Leveraging its competitive position and solid progress in leading-edge process technologies and advanced packaging, TSM has maintained a wide lead over its pure-play foundry peers. The company is expected to maintain this healthy momentum riding on the immense growth opportunity in agentic AI, which is increasing the role of CPUs in AI data centers and adding to demand beyond AI accelerators.

TSM currently sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here .

Riding on robust growth dynamics and a favorable Zacks Rank, TSM appears primed for further price appreciation. Consequently, investors are likely to profit if they bet on this high-flying stock now.

news.Content:
台積電(2330-TW)供應鏈設備大廠迅得(6438-TW)營收在半導體業務推進一如預期，10 月營收維持在 6 億元以上高檔，今(2)日揭露以 6.73億元改寫歷史單月次高，也創同期新高，月減3.15%、年增28.08%；累計 2026 年 1-10 月營收達61.86億元，年增 10.93%。

迅得 2026 年第三季營收達 19.45 億元，季增 6.64%、年增 13.62%，單季營收刷新歷史紀錄。法人預估，第四季營收將可維持在此一歷史高檔水準之上。

隨著迅得安排出貨的半導體設備於第四季步入出貨高峰，加上產品組合優化，下半年營運將顯著優於上半年。法人預估，迅得 2026 全年營收將較 2025 年的 64.67 億元成長 10%–15%，續創歷史新高；在產品組合有利因素加持下，獲利成長幅度更有望達到營收增幅的倍數呈現。

迅得同時具備半導體與 PCB 設備雙重成長動能，在 PCB 領域，公司鎖定高階載板與板廠需求，目前已握有臻鼎-KY(4958-TW)及景碩(3189-TW)等大廠確立訂單。

news.Title: Marvell to purchase Lumentum for $115 billion as AI boom drives demand for connectivity
news.Content:
What happened: Marvell Technology ( MRVL ) declined less than 1% on Monday on reports that the chip producer said it would buy optical component maker Lumentum ( LITE ). Shares of Lumentum also dipped on the announcement.

What's behind the move: The deal is expected to expand the combined company's total addressable market to $550 billion, the companies said.

"AI infrastructure is undergoing a fundamental architectural shift toward optical connectivity, creating an opportunity that comes along once in a generation," Matt Murphy, chairman and CEO of Marvell, said in a press statement.

Lumentum shareholders will receive four and a half shares of Marvell stock for every share of Lumentum stock they own. The deal values Lumentum at approximately $115 billion, or $1,132 per share, representing a 23.9% premium over its Oct. 28 closing share price.

What else you need to know: The acquisition gives Marvell greater access to optical technologies and manufacturing capacity, which have become critical bottlenecks of the AI infrastructure build-out.

Lumentum makes lasers and other optical components as increasingly powerful AI systems require faster connections. Marvell, which competes with Broadcom ( AVGO ), designs high-speed infrastructure and custom chips that enable AI computers to communicate with one another.

Earlier this year, Marvell stock rallied sharply after AI chip heavyweight Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang described the chip designer as "the next trillion-dollar company."

The company joined the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) index in June. Marvell shares are up more than 130% year to date. Lumentum shares have rallied 128%.

news.Title: European stocks edge down, oil drops as midterm caution prevails
news.Content:
By Stefano Rebaudo

Nov 2 (Reuters) - European stocks edged down on Monday after Friday's tech rout, with investors looking ahead to Apple's earnings and taking comfort from a sharp fall in oil prices amid hopes for a deal to end the Iran war.

Markets face a pivotal week, ‌with investors digesting the Federal Reserve's and the European Central Bank's latest policy decisions, earnings season in full swing and the US midterm elections on ‌Tuesday.

Euro zone government bonds were slightly lower after last week's rally, while investor sentiment remained fragile amid concerns over France's fiscal outlook and continuing street unrest.

MSCI's main world stocks index <.MIWD00000PUS> was roughly unchanged, while ​Europe's STOXX 600 was down 0.10%, with tech stocks rising 0.30%.

Nasdaq futures climbed 0.73% and S&P 500 futures increased 0.42%. The S&P 500 index <.SPX> fell 1.82% on Friday, while the Nasdaq tumbled 2.86%.

Brent crude futures fell 4.5% to about $108 as Iranian negotiators have left talks with Qatari mediators and a draft proposal is being circulated with a follow-up meeting possible. Trump recently threatened new attacks against Iran.

Investors remain cautious ahead of the US vote, with European stock markets facing a different set of challenges from their US counterparts.

"Further ‌expected downside for the euro area PMI is a ⁠drag on our Stoxx 600 forecast trajectory," wrote Sebastian Raedler, head of European equity strategy at BofA.

"However, the main reason for our caution on European equities is the risk of disappointment in the AI capex cycle as AI models commoditise and competitive moats ⁠prove limited."

While earnings outlooks remained in focus, investors expect US equities to come under pressure in the event of a Democratic sweep, as markets price in the risk of higher corporate taxes and tighter AI regulation.

Opinion polls suggest Democrats are favoured to win the House, while the Senate remains too close to call, leaving the party well short of a veto-proof ​two-thirds ​majority.

"The combination of deteriorating cash flows and rising capital commitments means the debate over whether ​AI returns can ultimately justify the scale of investment may not ‌be resolved anytime soon," Emmanuel Cau, head of European equity strategy at Barclays, said.

Apple will face scrutiny over three key issues: its crucial holiday-quarter outlook, CEO remarks on AI and the revamped Siri, and rising memory-chip costs that analysts expect to drag quarterly profit growth to its weakest in six quarters.

Story Continues

Goldman Sachs analysts expect capital spending by hyperscalers to nearly double to $800 billion this year and rise further to $1.2 trillion in 2027. At the same time, they see S&P 500 earnings per share growth slowing to 18% next year from nearly 30% in 2026.

"The next phase will be less about identifying who is exposed to AI and more about distinguishing who is ‌already converting that demand into cash, who is still funding the build-out, and what valuation ​investors are being asked to pay for each," Kristofer Barrett, head of global equities at Carmignac, said.

US DOLLAR ​SAFE-HAVEN STATUS UNDER SCRUTINY

In foreign exchange markets, major currencies were largely subdued. ​The euro rose 0.46% to $1.1199, while the dollar was up 0.16% at 157.90 yen.

Rising oil prices tend to hurt the euro ‌and yen as they worsen the outlook for energy-importing economies.

Investors are ​also questioning the dollar's safe-haven status, concerned ​that a renewed tech-driven market selloff could weaken the US currency.

George Saravelos, global head of forex strategy at Deutsche Bank, said the US's reliance on foreign equity inflows was historically unprecedented and evidence showed that when the source of an equity shock is US-centric the dollar-equity correlation flips to positive.

Among ​central banks meeting this week, markets are pricing in rate ‌increases from the Reserve Bank of Australia, Bank of England and Riksbank, while the Norges Bank is seen on hold.

Data due this week ​include the US ISM manufacturing survey for October later on Monday and the closely watched non-farm payrolls report on Friday.

(Reporting by Stefano Rebaudo; ​additional reporting by Wayne Cole. Editing by Muralikumar Anantharaman, Mark Potter and Chizu Nomiyama )

news.Title: Vertiv and Centerra Gold have been highlighted as Zacks Bull and Bear of the Day
news.Content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – November 2, 2026 – Zacks Equity Research shares Vertiv Holdings VRT as the Bull of the Day and Centerra Gold CGAU as the Bear of the Day. In addition, Zacks Equity Research provides analysis on Micron Technology MU and NVIDIA Corp. NVDA .

Here is a synopsis of all four stocks.

Bull of the Day:

Everybody wants to talk about AI chips. NVIDIA this, NVIDIA that. But here's the thing, kids. Those fancy chips need electricity. They generate a TON of heat. Without the infrastructure to power and cool them, they're nothing more than expensive paperweights.

That's where today's Bull of the Day comes in. I'm talking about Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) Vertiv Holdings . Vertiv provides critical digital infrastructure, including power management, thermal management, and liquid cooling solutions for data centers. With hyperscalers spending billions building out AI capacity, business is absolutely booming.

Just look at the company's latest earnings report. Vertiv delivered adjusted EPS of $2.21, crushing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 21.43%. Revenue surged 61% year over year to $4.31 billion, beating expectations by 14.61%. Those are some monster numbers. But here's where things get really interesting.

Analysts have been scrambling to catch up. Over the last sixty days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year has jumped from $6.67 to $7.12. Next year's number has climbed from $8.88 to $9.50. That's the sort of earnings estimate revision activity that gets me excited. It's also why VRT is sitting pretty with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy).

Those estimates translate into earnings growth of roughly 69.5% this year, followed by another 33.5% next year. Revenue growth isn't exactly taking a back seat either. Current projections call for $14.31 billion in sales this year, with next year's number swelling to $18.78 billion. That's over 31% revenue growth next year on top of an already enormous expansion this year.

A quick look at the Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise Chart tells the story. Earnings estimates continue marching higher while the stock has experienced some serious volatility. Despite gaining more than 43% year to date, VRT remains well below its 52-week high. That's an interesting divergence. The earnings picture keeps improving, but the stock hasn't kept pace with those upward revisions recently.

Vertiv Holdings Co. price-consensus-chart | Vertiv Holdings Co. Quote

Now, nobody's confusing Vertiv with a bargain-basement value stock. Shares trade around 32.7 times current-year earnings. That's a premium multiple, no doubt. But with projected earnings growth approaching 70% this year and a PEG ratio around 0.75, there's plenty of growth supporting that valuation.

Story Continues

The Zacks Style Scores back up the bullish case too. Vertiv sports an A for Growth, an A for Momentum, and an A for its overall VGM Score. Of course, AI infrastructure spending won't grow at this pace forever. Execution risks and elevated expectations remain. But right now, the earnings revisions are moving in exactly the direction we want.

Bear of the Day:

Gold has been one of the hottest trades on Wall Street. Investors have piled into the yellow metal looking for protection against inflation, geopolitical uncertainty, and a weakening dollar. Gold miners have been along for the ride, with some stocks putting up absolutely monster gains.

But here's the thing, kids. Just because gold is going higher doesn't mean every gold miner is a winner. Eventually, earnings matter. And when analysts start cutting their estimates, that's a warning sign you don't want to ignore.

That's exactly what's happening with today's Bear of the Day, Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell) Centerra Gold . Centerra Gold is a Canadian-based gold mining company with operations centered around its Mount Milligan mine in British Columbia and Öksüt mine in Turkey. The company operates in the Mining – Gold industry, which currently ranks in the Bottom 27% of our Zacks Industry Rank.

Centerra Gold Inc. price-consensus-chart | Centerra Gold Inc. Quote

The reason for the unfavorable Zacks Rank comes down to earnings estimate revisions. Over the last sixty days, two analysts have lowered their earnings estimates for the current year. Two have also cut their numbers for next year. Not a single upward revision in either period. Those bearish moves have pushed the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year down from $1.62 to $1.52 per share. That's nearly a 6% haircut in just two months.

Next year's estimate currently sits at $1.97, up from $1.90 sixty days ago, but the individual downward revisions are a reminder that analysts aren't exactly seeing eye to eye on the company's prospects.

Centerra actually delivered a positive earnings surprise in its latest quarter. Earnings came in 12.12% better than expectations. Revenue growth has been respectable too, with quarterly sales increasing nearly 27% year over year.

You'd think that would be enough to get analysts excited. Apparently not. Despite those numbers, the current-quarter earnings estimate has slipped from 38 cents to 34 cents over the last sixty days. That's more than a 10% decline in expectations.

A quick look at the Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise Chart tells the story. The stock has enjoyed an impressive rally, gaining more than 40% year to date and over 72% during the last twelve months. Meanwhile, current-year earnings expectations have been heading in the opposite direction. That's the sort of divergence that makes me nervous.

news.Title: Why investors are dumping tech stocks, in one image
news.Content:
Tech stocks aren't getting shredded for any old reason. It's actually very fundamental: Free cash flow is drying up for Big Tech leaders, and capex is rising dramatically.

Investors are questioning whether this ratio is totally out of whack, given more realistic growth projections for AI.

The combined capex of Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Microsoft rose by $36.9 billion in the third quarter to $201.9 billion, the team at The Kobeissi Letter calculated (chart below). This figure has more than doubled over the past 12 months, and is up a staggering 356% since the first quarter of 2024.

Big Tech has now spent $1.6 trillion on capex over the last three years, the strategists say.

At the same time, the combined free cash flow of these companies fell $33.1 billion last quarter to a negative $26.4 billion, its lowest on record.

Free cash flow among these tech beasts has fallen by $88.2 billion over the last year.

Only Microsoft reported positive free cash flow in the third quarter.

Looking ahead, the strategists estimate these four companies plan to spend another $232 billion on capex in the fourth quarter.

The AI trade saw a serious slamming on Friday, with more than $1 trillion in market value wiped away as investors fretted about the weakening cash flow profiles of Big Tech.

"The AI narrative is cracking as profitability concerns intensify," warned Miller Tabak chief markets strategist Matt Maley.

news.Title: Meet the Spectacular Vanguard ETF With 44.6% of Its Portfolio Parked in Nvidia, Alphabet, Apple, and Microsoft
news.Content:
The Morningstar U.S. Total Market index is made up of all 3,476 companies listed on American stock exchanges. But then there is the Morningstar U.S. Mega Cap Growth index, which exclusively holds America's 52 most valuable growth companies, and they account for almost half the value of the entire U.S. Total Market Index.

That's right -- those 52 companies are worth almost as much as the other 3,424 listed companies combined. Perhaps that isn't a surprise given the four largest members in the Mega Cap Growth index are Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA), Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOGL)(NASDAQ: GOOG), Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL), and Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT), which have a combined market capitalization of $17.6 trillion.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

The Vanguard Morningstar Mega Cap Growth ETF (NYSEMKT: MGK) is an exchange-traded fund (ETF) that mimics the Large Cap Growth index by holding the same stocks. Here's how adding it to a diversified portfolio can supercharge an investor's long-term returns.

A concentrated group of America's best growth stocks

Given the substantial value of the four largest members of the Mega Cap Growth index (and by extension, the Vanguard ETF), they represent an eye-popping 44.6% of the value of its portfolio.

Stock

2. Apple

12.53%

3. Microsoft

4. Alphabet

Data source: Vanguard. Portfolio weightings are accurate as of Sept. 30, 2026, and are subject to change.

The four companies operate very different businesses, but they are powering the artificial intelligence (AI) revolution in their own unique way.

Nvidia supplies the world's best graphics processing units (GPUs) for data centers, which are the main chips used in AI training and inference workloads. Its new Vera Rubin GPU systems recently started shipping, and they will significantly reduce the cost of deploying AI software, which is a key factor in driving widespread adoption of this technology.

Apple's latest iPhones, iPads, and Mac computers are fitted with custom chips that are designed to handle the Apple Intelligence suite of AI features and applications. More than 2.5 billion Apple devices are currently active worldwide, so this company could soon be the largest distributor of AI to consumers.

Alphabet developed features like AI Overviews and AI Mode to bring its Google Search platform into the AI era. Google Cloud is also growing rapidly as demand soars for its data center infrastructure and its portfolio of ready-made foundation models that enterprises can use to build AI software.

Microsoft has integrated its Copilot AI assistant into legacy software products like Windows and 365 (Word, Excel, Outlook, and more). Like Google Cloud, Microsoft's Azure cloud platform is also experiencing incredible demand for its portfolio of AI services, and it's consistently the fastest growing segment in the entire organization.

Story Continues

AI stocks are currently pulling back after posting blistering gains over the last few years. But Nvidia, Alphabet, Apple, and Microsoft are still sitting on a median return of 195% since the AI boom started gathering momentum in January 2023, when OpenAI's ChatGPT application crossed 100 million users for the first time. Therefore, these stocks have been a major source of upside for the Vanguard ETF.

NVDA data by YCharts

This Vanguard ETF also holds a number of other AI titans including Meta Platforms , Broadcom , Amazon , Advanced Micro Devices , and Palantir Technologies . But it does offer some diversification through positions in payment giants Visa and Mastercard , industrial powerhouse Boeing , and consumer products company Monster Energy , to name just a few of its non-technology holdings.

Should investors buy the Vanguard ETF right now?

The Vanguard Morningstar Mega Cap Growth ETF has delivered a compound annual return of 13.8% since it was established in 2007, beating the S&P 500 index which gained an average of 10.9% per year over the same period. However, given its highly concentrated portfolio of just 52 stocks, investors probably shouldn't bet the farm on this fund alone.

Adding this ETF to a diversified portfolio of other funds and individual stocks might be a better strategy, because it can help minimize any potential downside risks. Technology companies are currently spending hundreds of billions of dollars on AI data center infrastructure each year, and concerns are mounting about a potential slowdown. If that happens, there could be further downside ahead for most of the stocks at the top of the Vanguard ETF.

Investors who put $20,000 into an S&P 500 index fund in 2007 would have $142,800 today. But had they split the $20,000 by placing $10,000 in the S&P 500 and the other $10,000 in the Vanguard ETF, they would have $188,000 today instead. At the same time, they would have smoothed out some of the volatility associated with having significant exposure to the tech industry.

In summary, this Vanguard ETF could be a great long-term investment, but diversification might be the key to yielding the best results.

news.Title: Micron vs. SanDisk: China's DRAM Scare Hit Both Stocks, but 1 Is the Better Buy
news.Content:
The AI memory boom just hit a wall of worry as big as China this month. When word broke that Chinese chipmaker ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) had achieved a breakthrough in DRAM technology, it triggered shockwaves through the industry. Fears surged that a strong new rival might soon shake up established players, spark a price war, and flood the market with fresh supply. Investors wasted no time dumping top memory stocks like Micron Technology (MU) and SanDisk (SNDK), even though each faces a very different threat from this news.

The reaction highlights just how high the stakes have become in an industry powering the AI revolution, where soaring demand has sent both stocks rocketing to triple-digit gains in 2026. But is China's advance a real threat to their profits, or is the market jumping the gun? For investors anxious about the future of these memory stocks, understanding the differences between Micron and SanDisk's business models could reveal which is the smarter pick for the decade ahead.

More News from Barchart

Why It's Time to Buy the Pullback in Alphabet Stock

Dear Roku Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 2

Dear ON Semiconductor Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 2

Tired of missing midday reversals? The FREE Barchart Brief newsletter keeps you in the know. Sign up now!

The Case for Micron (MU)

The selloff followed reports that China's CXMT is developing a breakthrough DRAM design that packs more memory into the same space. With plans to launch its server-focused technology by the end of 2026, the company has sparked concerns that Chinese manufacturers could soon disrupt the market, challenge established players, and drive prices down.

MU stock fell 16% in October alone, despite surging 213% year-to-date (YTD).

Micron is a major manufacturer of DRAM, NAND flash memory, and high-bandwidth memory (HBM). Its products power computers, smartphones, data centers, and AI accelerators. NAND provides long-term data storage, DRAM serves as working memory, and HBM delivers the high-speed data access that demanding AI workloads require. This broad product portfolio gives Micron multiple ways to benefit from AI spending. However, this same advantage has also exposed it directly to China's ambitions in DRAM.

In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, Micron's revenue soared to a record $54.23 billion, up 379% year-over-year (YoY) and 31% sequentially. DRAM generated a record $39.8 billion, making up 73% of total sales. NAND contributed $14.1 billion, about 26% of revenue. DRAM revenue rose 27% sequentially, while NAND revenue climbed 42%. Since DRAM makes up nearly three-quarters of Micron's sales, any sustained increase in competing supply could pressure its pricing power and profitability.

Story Continues

But DRAM is not a single, interchangeable product. Micron also delivers HBM, the powerhouse fueling AI computing by channeling data to processors at lightning-fast speeds. HBM revenue is included in Micron's DRAM total. Micron's Q4 earnings call highlighted HBM's growing importance as AI demand expands. Management said the company secured agreements covering the vast majority of its HBM bit supply for calendar year 2027. These commitments provide greater visibility into future demand and reflect the strategic significance of advanced memory to AI customers.

Investors should understand that China's progress in conventional DRAM does not automatically translate into the ability to match Micron's advanced HBM products. HBM production requires demanding manufacturing processes, sophisticated packaging, and strict performance standards.

However, the bigger vulnerability is pricing. Micron's DRAM revenue soared 27% sequentially in fiscal Q4, driven by average selling prices that climbed sharply into the high teens. This stresses just how much pricing still drives the company's revenue engine. If CXMT accelerates production and rolls out attractive alternatives at tempting prices, a flood of new supply could chip away at Micron's hard-won pricing power in conventional DRAM.

That said, Micron has spent years perfecting its processes and forging strong ties with leading tech giants. It has built a formidable HBM business that may be harder to replace in the near term. Still, this advantage cannot fully shield the company from any new shifts that may reshape the DRAM supply-and-demand landscape.

For now, Micron's financial results offer investors plenty of reassurance. Adjusted gross margin reached 87%, while adjusted diluted earnings per share climbed to $33.42. The company generated $43.97 billion in operating cash flow and $33.20 billion in adjusted free cash flow in Q4. Management expects momentum to continue into fiscal year 2027 because memory supply could remain tight through calendar years 2027 and 2028. That outlook reveals that the current upcycle still has room to run even as investors begin to price in tougher competition ahead.

The Case for SanDisk (SNDK)

SanDisk's selloff tells a somewhat different story. Distinguished for its NAND flash memory and storage expertise, the company powers data centers, computers, and countless other devices with its solid-state drives (SSDs).

Unlike Micron, SanDisk doesn't manufacture DRAM, yet it still suffered the fear-driven consequences of a widespread selloff across the memory sector. SNDK stock is down 31% this month alone, even though it has soared 405% so far this year.

SanDisk's recent fiscal Q1 earnings show why the selloff wasn't justified. Revenue reached $11.03 billion, up 23% sequentially and 378% YoY. Adjusted earnings climbed to $49.51 per share from $39.25. About 60% of the sequential increase came from higher bit shipments, and 40% came from pricing. Data center revenue rose 61% sequentially to $4.8 billion, reflecting the increasing contribution of AI-related demand.

As AI inference workloads expand, data centers need more capacity to store and retrieve information. SanDisk believes NAND will play an increasingly important role in meeting these needs and is developing High Bandwidth Flash (HBF) to complement HBM. It expects to provide samples of its first HBF products in 2027. A key pillar of SanDisk's strategy rests in its New Business Model (NBM) agreements. By forging these long-term partnerships, the company locks in customer commitments and protects itself from the uncertainty of fluctuating quarterly orders. Management says these agreements already account for roughly half of its bits in fiscal 2027 and will cover two-thirds by fiscal 2028. This approach gives SanDisk a much clearer view of future demand.

On the balance sheet, SanDisk ended the quarter with $5.1 billion in cash and no debt. It also generated $5.7 billion in adjusted free cash flow and repurchased $5 billion worth of shares during the quarter. The memory maker remains committed to using all excess cash for shareholder returns.

Overall, SNDK stock holds a consensus "Strong Buy" rating on Wall Street. Of the 25 analysts covering the stock, 21 recommend "Strong Buy," one recommends "Moderate Buy," and three suggest "Hold." Based on its average target price of $2,125, analysts expect the stock to rise 77% from current levels. Its high price estimate of $3000 suggests the stock could climb 150% over the next 12 months.

Which Is the Better Buy for the Next Decade?

While SanDisk is less directly exposed to CXMT's DRAM advances, its business remains more concentrated in NAND. Therefore, Micron remains the better buy for investors seeking diversified exposure to AI memory. With its blend of DRAM, HBM, and NAND, Micron unlocks opportunities in multiple market segments. Its strong cash flow and enduring customer partnerships further reinforce its edge over competitors.

On Wall Street, MU stock holds a consensus "Strong Buy" rating. Out of the 42 analysts covering MU, 34 rate it a "Strong Buy," five rate it a "Moderate Buy," and three recommend a "Hold." Its average target price of $1,563.22 still gives it room for 76% more growth. And the high price target of $3,000 suggests MU stock has an upside potential of 238% from current levels.

news.Title: 〈美國期中選舉〉國會若換手哪些美股受影響？一次看懂軍工、醫療、加密貨幣與AI
news.Content:
洛克希德馬丁(LMT-US)約七成營收來自美國政府，但未來十年供應850架F-35戰機的計畫，仍須國會批准並撥款。這也是華爾街關注本周期中選舉的原因：若民主黨拿下參眾兩院任一院，就能在預算談判中爭取讓步，並取得委員會調查權。從軍工廠能拿到多少訂單、健保業者能保住多少收入，到AI資料中心該由誰負擔電網升級費用，都可能受到影響。

摩根士丹利(MS-US)統計，在共和黨總統執政期間，若期中選舉後兩黨分掌參眾兩院，標普500指數在選後一年平均上漲23%；若民主黨掌控兩院，平均漲幅為16%。不過，該行美國公共政策研究主管Ariana Salvatore認為，這次未必會重演歷史走勢。即使民主黨取得國會多數，總統川普仍握有否決權，在關稅及聯邦監管上也保有相當大的裁量空間。

軍工看訂單 醫療看給付

白宮已為2027會計年度提出1.5兆美元國防預算要求，另為2026會計年度尋求876億美元追加撥款，主要用於與伊朗相關的軍事行動。若民主黨在國會取得優勢，可能檢視部分涉及伊朗及以色列的支出，同時爭取增加對烏克蘭的援助。相較之下，嚇阻中國、核武現代化及飛彈防禦都有跨黨派支持。以洛克希德馬丁為例，該公司與五角大廈簽的是F-35採購框架協議，國會是否授權多年期採購並編列經費，才決定這批戰機能否成為正式訂單。

醫療業對聯邦預算同樣敏感。健康政策研究機構KFF根據國會預算處估算，川普去年簽署的減稅與支出法案，到2034年將使聯邦醫療補助計畫(Medicaid)支出累計減少9,110億美元。健康保險商Molina Healthcare(MOH-US)去年有322億美元保費收入來自Medicaid，占其保費收入的75%。民主黨即使只拿下一院，也能在預算談判中爭取延後部分刪減，協助保險商維持投保人數，並減輕醫院照護無保險病患的負擔。但同一批議員也可能加強檢視保費、藥價與業者獲利，醫療股受到的影響並不一致。

幣圈等立法 銀行看資本規定

加密貨幣業希望把川普任內的監管政策寫進法律，降低政策隨政府更迭而改變的風險。9月，川普支持的加密貨幣市場結構法案《CLARITY法案》未能在參院取得進展，交易平台Coinbase(COIN-US)與穩定幣發行商Circle(CRCL-US)股價當時一度跌達11%。若民主黨席次增加，業界要爭取法案過關，可能得接受更嚴格的消費者保障，以及對付息型穩定幣的限制。

銀行業則關注資本規定。聯邦監管機構估計，現行提案可使大型銀行的資本要求降低約4.8%，騰出數十億美元用於放款或回饋股東。相關規則由聯準會(Fed)訂定，參院則能透過人事同意權影響未來由誰填補職缺。民主黨若掌控任一院，也可透過委員會調閱企業文件、傳喚高層出席聽證會。部分民主黨議員已就白宮宴會廳捐款及關稅豁免索取資料。

AI資料中心擴建 電網升級誰買單

摩根士丹利估計，微軟(MSFT-US)、亞馬遜(AMZN-US)、Google母公司Alphabet(GOOGL-US)(GOOG-US)及臉書母公司Meta(META-US)等雲端業者，2027年資本支出將超過1兆美元。隨著資料中心用電需求攀升，居民也愈來愈在意電費。《CNBC》10月調查顯示，63%的登記選民反對在住家方圓10英里(約16公里)內興建資料中心，僅13%支持。

爭議已進入國會。眾院9月以417票對3票通過一項法案，要求各州監管機構評估是否應由大型資料中心負擔新增的電力設施成本。部分民主黨議員主張應訂定強制規範，該案最終未能跨過參院程序表決門檻。若選後民主黨影響力上升，科技公司可能得承擔更多電網升級費用；至於個別設施能在哪裡接上電網、何時動工，仍取決於州政府、地方政府及公用事業。

news.Title: 台股失守4萬5！外資狂賣「這檔」逾11萬張　葉育碩：接下來盯緊3大訊號
news.Content:
台北股市今（2）日開盤遭遇強烈賣壓，盤中一度狂瀉 812 點、最低下探至 44,399 點，直接跌破 45,000 點大關。所幸低檔買盤隨後進場承接，終場台股大盤跌幅收斂，下跌 291.69 點，收在 44,920.14 點，跌幅 0.65%，成交金額為 7,588.75 億元。面對盤勢大幅震盪與外資持續瘋狂提款， 財經專家葉育碩 指出，大盤展現出出乎預期的韌性，但外資爆砍單一檔 ETF 超過 11 萬張，投資人接下來必須密切關注 「三大觀察點」 。

【韓股反彈與暗盤訊號 恐慌情緒早盤逐步收斂】

葉育碩分析，今日台股走勢雖然開低跌破關鍵整數關卡，但呈現「開低走高」的抗跌態勢，從早盤最低點到收盤已成功拉回超過 500 點。事實上，從假日部分交易所的暗盤交易即可提前觀察到個股反彈跡象；加上今日早盤韓國股市隨著三星、SK海力士等記憶體權值股反彈帶頭翻紅，有效緩和了亞洲市場的恐慌氣氛。提前掌握暗盤等資訊，能幫助投資人避免在開盤恐慌時將持股砍在最低點。

【外資連3日提款2548億 00406A慘遭狂砍11萬張】

然而，市場籌碼面仍存隱憂。今日三大法人合計賣超 526.91 億元，其中外資再度賣超 735.2 億元，已連續三個交易日站在賣方，累計提款高達 2,548.03 億元。葉育碩特別點出外資今日賣超標的，最驚人的正是 00406A（主動中信台灣收益） ， 單日慘遭外資爆砍 11 萬 199 張 ；此外，0050（元大台灣50）遭賣超 3 萬 1,078 張、00981A（主動統一台股增長）賣超 2 萬 5,140 張、00631L（元大台灣50正2）賣超 1 萬 6,442 張、6770（力積電）賣超 1 萬 6,392 張、2330（台積電）賣超 1 萬 5,005 張以及 2887（台新新光金）賣超 1 萬 1,374 張。顯示外資調節範圍涵蓋 主動型、指數型、槓桿型 ETF 及 大型權值股 。相較之下，投信今日買超 361.17 億元、連續 15 個交易日加碼，內外資形成強烈對比。

【成交量偏低防超跌搶短 葉育碩提醒：接下來注意三件事】

葉育碩提醒，今日大盤成交量僅約 7,600 億元，顯示追價意願尚不強烈，短線反彈可能僅是超跌後的搶短買盤。面對本週即將迎來的美國期中選舉與科技巨頭財報等國際變數，投資人接下來應 重點關注三件事 ：第一，45,000 點大關失守後能否迅速重新站回；第二，外資在連續大舉提款後，賣超規模是否開始縮小；第三，投信連續買超的內資力量能否持續支撐大盤。面對震盪行情，切勿急著認定落底，做好資產配置並保留操作空間才是上策。

news.Title: Intel's 29% Plunge Sparks a Contrarian Buying Case
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Semiconductor maker Intel Corp. ( INTC , Financials ) continues under pressure as downturn in personal computers and supply-chain restrictions impact on its near-term profit projections.The PC market is still a big worry. Industry unit volumes are estimated to decrease by around 12% in 2026 and another 10% in 2027, which might prolong the time it takes for Intel's client business to recover.But the company's data center and artificial intelligence efforts provide a counterweight.Continued development in those areas provides Intel considerable long-term optionality, even if its PC market continues under pressure, the person believes.The stock's drop has also reset valuations dramatically. According to the study, Intel already trades at about 21 times expected fiscal 2028 earnings, suggesting that the market has already priced in much of the near-term risks.That doesn't reduce the execution risk. Earnings may remain erratic because of a weakened PC market, supply bottlenecks and sustained investment needs.The investment thesis is increasingly based on whether Intel can utilize data-center expansion to buy time until its broader recovery improves.The next driver is proof of server and AI growth continuing to offset downturn in PCs.

news.Title: Meta's AI Spending Push Triggers Negative S&P Outlook
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

S&P Global Ratings lowered Meta Platforms Inc.'s ( META , Financials ) credit outlook to negative, stoking concerns about the size of the Facebook and Instagram parent's artificial intelligence expenditure.S&P noted that given the company's multi-year AI goals, it is less likely that Meta would cut capital expenditures as it had previously planned.Meta had a $2.12 billion free cash flow loss in the third quarter, but it expects to invest $135 billion to $145 billion in capital expenditures for the year.S&P estimates free operational cash flow shortfalls of around $39 billion in 2026 and $71 billion in 2027.The agency also highlighted that leverage might exceed 1.0x if spending continues to be high and AI monetization takes longer than planned.The rise in debt is mostly due to Meta's usage of leased data-center capacity, S&P said.The negative outlook doesn't mean a lowering of the rating but sets a higher bar on how soon Meta can convert its AI investments into financial returns.S&P said the outlook might revert to stable if leverage remains below its downgrade level and free operational cash flow becomes positive in 2028.The next driver is Meta's forward capex projection and proof that AI investment is starting to pay off in greater cash returns.

news.Title: Marvell Reaches $115 Billion Deal for Lumentum Holdings
news.Content:
(Bloomberg) -- Marvell Technology Inc. has reached a deal to buy data center optics maker Lumentum Holdings Inc. at an enterprise value of $115 billion, one of the biggest tech tie-ups ever, in a race to capitalize on the artificial intelligence boom.

Most Read from Bloomberg

Ray-Ban Heir Rejects $3.9 Billion Offer for Stake in Family Firm

Wall Street Eyes Biggest Treasury Sales Overhaul in Years

Feud Erupts in Michigan as El-Sayed Rival Backs GOP's Rogers

Valero to Buy, Restart Idled Texas Refinery as Fuel Rallies

Wash Trades and 5,000% Gains: Inside Indonesia's MSCI Hustle

The all-stock transaction will give Marvell shareholders 67% of the combined company, according to a statement confirming an earlier Bloomberg News report that the two Silicon Valley companies were nearing a pact.

On an equity basis, it's the top M&A deal of the year and the largest ever in the global tech sector, excluding the SpaceX-xAI merger, data compiled by Bloomberg show. The transaction shows how AI is driving deals across almost all major sectors and regions, from chipmakers and other specialist tech suppliers, to data center operators and power utilities.

Lumentum shares closed at $840.70 on Friday after gaining 128% this year, giving the San Jose-based company a market value of about $76 billion. Marvell, up 131% this year, was valued at $172.2 billion on Friday.

Lumentum makes lasers and other optical technology for moving enormous amounts of data at high speeds. That hardware underpins the AI boom, as it lets data centers and telecommunications firms move information between servers, facilities and other destinations.

Marvell already purchases laser technology from Lumentum, and the larger company has been increasing its bets on optical and photonic technology for connecting data center gear. Earlier this year, Marvell purchased photonics maker Celestial AI.

Nvidia Corp. announced an agreement to take a $2 billion stake in Lumentum in March as part of a deal that included collaboration on photonics, which use light instead of traditional copper wiring to move data faster and more efficiently.

Marvell also works with Amazon.com Inc.'s cloud unit and Microsoft Corp. to help build custom AI chips. In August, the company struck a chip deal with Alphabet Inc.'s Google to support Google's tensor processing units.

news.Title: What Are Wall Street Analysts' Target Price for Meta Platforms Stock?
news.Content:
Menlo Park, California-based Meta Platforms, Inc. (META) operates as a social technology company. The company develops products that enable people to connect and share with friends and family through mobile devices, personal computers, virtual reality headsets, and wearables. With a market cap of $1.6 trillion, Meta is also involved in advertisements, augmented, and virtual reality.

Shares of this social media giant have underperformed the broader market over the past year. META has declined 7.7% over this time frame, while the broader S&P 500 Index ($SPX) has rallied nearly 11.1%. In 2026, META stock is down 6.8%, compared to the SPX's 10.7% rise on a YTD basis.

More News from Barchart

Why It's Time to Buy the Pullback in Alphabet Stock

Micron vs. SanDisk: China's DRAM Scare Hit Both Stocks, but 1 Is the Better Buy

Dear Roku Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 2

Tired of missing midday reversals? The FREE Barchart Brief newsletter keeps you in the know. Sign up now!

Narrowing the focus, META's outperformance is apparent compared to the Vanguard Communication Services Index Fund ETF (VOX). The exchange-traded fund has declined about 8% over the past year. Moreover, META's single-digit dip on a YTD basis outshines the ETF's 11.5% losses over the same time frame.

META's performance was driven by strong top-line growth, fueled by record video engagement, ad impression increases, and the rapid adoption of its Muse personal AI agent, which surpassed 10 million users in North America within six weeks. However, operating margins plunged to 20.1% due to a $9.9 billion multi-state legal charge and heavy capital expenditures on AI data centers and infrastructure. Looking ahead, management expects sustained revenue expansion through global Muse scaling, enhanced commerce and subscription monetization, and AI tool rollouts for small and enterprise businesses, while pivoting Reality Labs toward AI-integrated hardware like Meta Glasses.

On Oct. 21, META reported its Q3 results, and its shares closed down by 7% in the following trading session. Its adjusted EPS of $7.40 surpassed Wall Street expectations of $6.52. The company's revenue was $64.6 billion, beating Wall Street forecasts of $63.4 billion. For Q4, META expects revenue in the range of $73 billion to $76 billion.

For the current fiscal year, ending in December, analysts expect META's EPS to fall 2.3% to $29.01 on a diluted basis. The company's earnings surprise history is mixed. It beat the consensus estimate in three of the last four quarters while missing the forecast on another occasion.

Story Continues

Among the 55 analysts covering META stock, the consensus is a "Strong Buy." That's based on 46 "Strong Buy" ratings, two "Moderate Buys," and seven "Holds."

This configuration is more bullish than a month ago, with 45 analysts suggesting a "Strong Buy."

On Oct. 28, John Blackledge from TD Cowen maintained a "Buy" rating on META, with a price target of $850, implying a potential upside of 38.2% from current levels.

The mean price target of $858.25 represents a 39.6% premium to META's current price levels. The Street-high price target of $1,050 suggests an ambitious upside potential of 70.7%.

news.Title: 跟著台積電買房就對了？台灣資金跨海掃地 美廠周邊房價狂漲53％
news.Content:
台積電赴美設廠，不只改變美國半導體產業布局，也讓亞利桑那州鳳凰城北部郊區成為台灣投資人關注的房地產市場。看過台積電帶動台南房價上漲的經驗，部分台灣資金開始跨海布局，當地房仲甚至經常在半夜接到亞洲投資人的來電詢問，而他們最關心的問題，就是土地距離台積電廠區有多近。

彭博社報導指出，根據大鳳凰城經濟發展委員會資料，自2021年以來，台灣投資人已在當地投入5億美元（約新台幣162.87億元），投資規模與加拿大投資人相當。這波資金進場，與台積電持續擴大在美投資密切相關。

台積電投資2650億美元 台灣資金搶先布局

台積電2020年選定鳳凰城作為美國首座先進製造基地，目前已完成1座晶圓廠，另外2座晶圓廠也預計陸續投入營運。今年稍早，公司再宣布增加1000億美元（約新台幣3.26兆元）投資，使亞利桑那州總投資金額達到2650億美元（約新台幣8.63兆元）。

隨著台積電擴建，供應商也陸續進駐鳳凰城西北部郊區，帶動倉儲及製造設施需求。根據高力國際（Colliers International）資料，當地空屋率從前一年的16%降至今年6月的8%，降幅明顯高於鳳凰城整體市場。

世邦魏理仕（CBRE Group）駐鳳凰城執行副總裁Kevin Calihan指出，親眼見證過台積電在台灣帶來的經濟效應後，台灣投資人對鳳凰城市場的看法，比長期在亞利桑那州經營的業者更加樂觀，而且已經領先其他投資人。

砸8800萬美元購地 房價6年漲幅達53%

台灣投資人看好鳳凰城，與過去在台南的房地產投資經驗有關。房仲公司Funwoo負責人Nancy Tseng表示，部分客戶原本對鳳凰城並不熟悉，但台積電擴大台南廠區後，當地房價漲幅超越台灣其他地區，讓曾經在台南投資獲利的買家，希望將類似策略複製到美國。

具體投資案例已經出現。由台商共同創立、總部位於華盛頓特區的Taicoon地產公司（Taicoon Property Partners），以8800萬美元（約新台幣28.66億元）買下距離台積電廠區約10分鐘車程的兩塊土地，初步規劃投入10億美元（約新台幣325.73億元），興建住宅及多層樓購物中心，並考慮引進鼎泰豐、誠品書店等台灣品牌。

大魯閣集團也正與Taicoon洽談，希望在開發案中加入打擊練習場、亞洲風格SPA及親子娛樂設施，讓當地逐漸形成結合住宅、商業與休閒用途的複合式開發。

房價數據也反映這波投資熱度。根據房地產平台Zillow資料，鳳凰城North Gateway與Desert View兩區過去6年房價平均上漲約53%，高於鳳凰城全市同期約42%的漲幅。即使疫情後房市降溫，距離晶圓廠較近的住宅仍展現相對保值的表現。

台積電目前已在亞利桑那州聘僱約3500名員工，並計畫再增加2500人。隨著員工及供應鏈進駐，當地住宅需求也持續增加，部分地區預計新增3300戶住宅。

房市熱潮背後 土地、勞工與居民衝突浮現

不過，台積電帶來的投資與就業機會，也伴隨土地開發及勞動市場問題。台積電表示，鳳凰城當地目前仍無法完全提供晶圓廠所需的專業人才，因此部分職缺由持公司擔保簽證的台灣員工填補，公司也正透過全美大學及當地半導體培訓計畫招募人才。

news.Title: 台股跌深有原因！單周遭倒貨53億美元亞股最慘 富蘭克林揭資金新去向
news.Content:
美國大型科技股財報結果重燃投資人對於AI人工智慧龐大支出與回報的疑慮，引發科技類股賣壓與全球股市回檔壓力。就資金流向而言，過去一週整體股票型ETF仍續獲到市場重新檢視AI概念股龐大資本支出效益影響，全球資金近期出現明顯流向變化。根據富蘭克林證券投顧最新統計，台股上周遭外資淨賣超53.2億美元，不僅遠高於南韓、印尼等市場，更成為主要亞洲股市中賣壓最沉重地區；反觀美股則持續吸引資金回流，顯示國際資金正加速撤離亞股、重返美國市場。

富蘭克林證券投顧表示，雖然美、歐、日三大央行利率決議均符合市場預期，但Amazon、Alphabet（Google）及Intel等美國科技巨頭財報發布後，市場再度浮現對AI投資支出過高、報酬率能否兌現的擔憂，拖累科技類股走弱，也使全球股市出現震盪。

在資金流向方面，儘管市場波動升溫，但整體股票型ETF近一周仍吸引665.7億美元淨流入，其中美國市場獨攬349.04億美元，成為最大贏家；亞洲股市也有207.28億美元資金流入，但主要受中國市場117.85億美元資金挹注帶動。

若從產業觀察，科技類ETF仍以34.83億美元淨流入居冠，其次為金融及醫療保健類股；反觀通訊服務、公用事業及原物料類股則呈現資金流出。

值得注意的是，亞洲股市外資操作呈現明顯分化。統計顯示，台灣單周遭外資賣超53.2億美元，為主要亞股之最；南韓遭賣超2.1億美元、印尼1.68億美元、越南1.04億美元、菲律賓500萬美元。相較之下，印度卻逆勢吸引11.5億美元外資買超，馬來西亞也獲7900萬美元資金流入。

進一步觀察今年以來外資動向，台股累計遭外資賣超734.19億美元，在亞洲市場中仍屬相當龐大的撤出規模。

對於後市看法，富蘭克林證券投顧指出，目前AI疑慮雖使科技股波動加劇，但能源、金融、公用事業及醫療保健等防禦型產業近期仍展現支撐力道。接下來市場將持續關注美國選舉結果、企業財報以及就業數據表現，這些因素都將影響資金是否進一步由科技股擴散至其他產業。

富蘭克林證券投顧認為，在高利率環境下，AI資本支出的融資成本上升，加上未來現金流折現價值下降，形成科技產業的雙重壓力，短線仍可能增加股債市場波動。不過，若觀察全球股票評價及企業獲利基本面，目前並未出現系統性風險。

在投資策略上，富蘭克林建議採取分散配置方式，以美國或全球平衡型基金作為核心配置，同時搭配新興市場平衡型基金參與亞洲AI供應鏈成長機會。在股票布局方面，除AI科技主題外，也可留意受惠AI基礎建設需求的公用事業，以及產業配置較多元的美股與日本股市；此外，可趁金價回檔時分批布局黃金及貴金屬基金，以提升投組抗震能力。

富蘭克林坦伯頓全球平衡基金經理人道格拉斯·葛蘭表示，全球企業獲利持續改善，加上市場漲勢已從少數科技巨頭擴散至更多產業與國家，仍有助支撐全球股市長期表現。其中，日本、歐洲及部分新興市場企業評價相對美國更具吸引力，而AI需求持續擴張，也將帶動深度參與科技供應鏈的新興市場受惠。

另一方面，富蘭克林坦伯頓科技基金經理人強納森·柯堤斯認為，目前AI基礎建設投資已逐漸開始轉化為實際獲利，產業仍處於高速成長初期階段，長線趨勢並未改變，短期修正反而提供投資人重新布局機會。

news.Title: 槓桿狂潮+AI燒錢焦慮！策略師：持續四年的美股牛市恐在6-12個月內進入尾聲
news.Content:
隨著法人機構與散戶瘋狂加槓桿，加上巨頭們在AI基礎建設上燒錢帶來的回報焦慮，持續約四年的美股牛市恐正接近尾聲，一位長期關注市場週期的宏觀策略師最新示警，美股可能在未來6至12個月完成由牛轉熊的轉變。

《MarketWatch》報導，宏觀研究機構Macro Ops創辦人Alex Barrow最新撰文指出，市場風險正逐漸累積，但牛市尚未完全結束，未來股市仍可能上漲，不過投資者需面對更劇烈的價格波動。

Barrow認為，最值得警惕的是各類投資者的總體風險部位持續攀升。避險基金和散戶不斷擴大股票持倉，借款投資規模也不斷增加。這種高槓桿在逆轉時可能引發集中平倉，放大跌勢。今年7月和10月的調整已暴露問題，那斯達克10月跌近7%，創去年4月最差表現。

Barrow指出，夏季波動或標誌牛市進入尾聲，但築頂通常需要8-9個月，目前仍有上漲空間，只是波動將明顯增加。避險基金近期已增加空頭部位，接近市場中性。

AI投資熱潮及融資壓力是另一關鍵變量。Macro Ops曾較早佈局AI和記憶體晶片，但在2-3月漲勢加速時兌現大部分利潤。

Barrow表示，AI基建巨額資本支出令企業日益依賴債務融資。在AI投資與財政赤字共同作用下，通膨恐持續高漲，Fed恐需更大幅度緊縮。融資成本提高將增加資金難度，若AI投資增速進入平台期，恐衝擊經濟和金融市場。

近期，Meta、Alphabet和亞馬遜繼續提高AI資本開支，但市場對回報週期的擔憂增加，高盛預計AI投資增速接近峰值。

儘管對期中前景謹慎，Barrow未完全退出股市，而是側重短期戰術安排。記憶體晶片仍是看好領域，團隊近期已重新建立美光科技等寸。

他認為，AI結構性需求或延長半導體週期，韓股KOSPI遠期本益比處於低位。此外，估值下降的建築材料企業、受資料中心需求推動的天然氣生產商也在關注範圍內。電網不足制約資料中心建設，相關能源和建築領域存在機會。AI醫療及生物技術同樣在視野中，貴金屬則長期關注但仍在尋底。

Barrow警告，標普500對少數大型科技股依賴度高，部分公司股價營收比超10倍，估值集中度需警惕，其當前策略包括提高現金比例、分散持倉並關注今年遭拋售的優質企業如波克夏海瑟威，同時保留部分AI部位應對後期上漲。

news.Title: Flex Stock Down Post Q2 Earnings: Should You Buy, Hold or Offload?
news.Content:
Shares of Flex Ltd. FLEX have declined approximately 7% following second-quarter fiscal 2027 results reported on Oct. 28. The company's shares have plunged 25.9% compared with the Zacks Electronics – Miscellaneous Products industry's 21.4% decline over the past month. The stock also lagged the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector and the S&P 500 composite, which decreased 12.5% and 3.4%, respectively, during the same period.

Flex's performance has also been disappointing relative to some of its industry peers. While Cisco Systems CSCO has declined 7.3%, Jabil JBL witnessed a fall of 9.3%. However, FLEX managed to outperform Sanmina SANM, whose shares fell 26.4% over the same timeframe.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Despite the recent weakness, Flex's strong operating momentum, accelerating AI infrastructure demand and improving profitability remain encouraging. Moreover, robust demand across its Cloud and Power Infrastructure (CPI) segment and the company's raised fiscal 2027 outlook underscore its solid growth prospects.

Against this backdrop, a closer examination of Flex's underlying fundamentals, growth opportunities, competitive positioning and potential headwinds is essential to assess whether the recent share price correction presents a buying opportunity or warrants a cautious stance.

Earnings Snapshot

Flex reported strong second-quarter fiscal 2027 results, with adjusted earnings surging 49.4% year over year to $1.18 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $1.05. Revenues climbed 24.8% to $8.49 billion, surpassing the consensus mark of $8.18 billion. Growth was driven by robust AI-related demand across CPI and strength in high-value markets.

CPI revenues surged to $2.51 billion from $1.63 billion, while Integrated Technology Solutions (ITS) and Regulated Manufacturing Solutions (RMS) revenues increased 22% and 9%, respectively. Adjusted operating margin expanded 110 basis points (bps) to 7.1%.

Flex expects third-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues of $8.87-$9.17 billion, adjusted operating income of $685-$715 million and adjusted earnings of $1.19-$1.25 per share. Management anticipates CPI revenues to grow 105-115% year over year, supported by sustained AI infrastructure investments. Despite strong operating performance, free cash flow declined to $261 million from $305 million, partly due to costs associated with the planned CPI spin-off.

Factors to Consider

Flex is grappling with persistent supply-chain constraints, which could impede its ability to capitalize fully on rising demand for AI infrastructure. Management indicated that component shortages, prevalent over the past 12 months, could persist for several more years as demand continues to outpace supply. These challenges could complicate production schedules, increase procurement costs and constrain the timely execution of high-growth programs. Moreover, supporting expanding operations has increased inventory requirements. In the second quarter of fiscal 2027, inventory rose 39% year over year and 13% sequentially, while inventory days, net of working capital advances, increased five days to 60. Sustained inventory accumulation could intensify working capital requirements and pressure cash generation.

Story Continues

The company is also facing substantial capital expenditure requirements to support its expanding CPI operations. Flex expects fiscal 2027 capital expenditures of $1.5-$1.6 billion, with approximately two-thirds allocated to CPI. These investments, primarily directed toward manufacturing capacity and power infrastructure, could constrain near-term free cash flow. Second-quarter free cash flow totaled $261 million, including a $61 million impact from one-time costs associated with the planned separation. Furthermore, the EPC Power acquisition involved $4.4 billion of debt financing, resulting in elevated near-term interest expenses. Although the planned $2 billion Axiom preferred stock transaction should partly alleviate this burden, financing costs remain a concern.

Flex is also grappling with weakness in consumer-related markets and increasing customer concentration risks. Management highlighted incremental softness in the lifestyle business, partially offsetting robust communications demand. Meanwhile, the CPI business is increasingly dependent on large hyperscale customers, reflecting concentrated AI infrastructure spending. Such exposure could increase vulnerability to shifts in customer investment priorities. Additionally, the planned separation of CPI into Axiom, targeted for early 2027, introduces execution risks, including potential operational disruptions and separation-related expenses. These uncertainties could weigh on financial flexibility and near-term performance.

Nevertheless, Flex is gaining from accelerating demand for AI infrastructure, particularly across power, cloud and cooling solutions. Second-quarter fiscal 2027 CPI revenues surged 54% year over year to $2.5 billion, while adjusted operating margin expanded 240 bps to 10.7%. Power operating margin reached approximately 16%, benefiting from higher volumes and improved capacity utilization. The acquisition of EPC Power further strengthens its end-to-end power capabilities, complementing investments in 800-volt architecture and solid-state transformers. Management expects CPI revenues to increase 75-85% in fiscal 2027, supported by sustained AI-related infrastructure investments.

The company is benefiting from healthy momentum across its RMS and ITS businesses. RMS revenues increased 9% year over year to $2.7 billion, supported by industrial demand, particularly energy infrastructure and robotics. ITS revenues climbed 22% to $3.3 billion, driven by advanced networking and communications. Together, these segments delivered their fourth consecutive quarter of year-over-year growth. Continued investments in health care, automation and communications should reinforce Flex's exposure to attractive, higher-value markets.

A Look at FLEX's Valuation

The stock trades at a forward 12-month price-to-sales (P/S) of 0.79X, below the industry's average of 7.29X. CSCO, JBL and SANM trade at a forward 12-month P/S of 5.63X, 0.61X and 0.52X, respectively.

FLEX's Upward Estimates

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for FLEX's earnings for fiscal 2027 has been revised marginally upward over the past 60 days.

What Should You Do With FLEX Stock Now?

Flex's strong AI infrastructure demand, expanding margins, upwardly revised fiscal 2027 outlook and attractive valuation support its long-term growth prospects. However, persistent supply-chain constraints, elevated capital expenditures, rising customer concentration and execution risks surrounding the planned Axiom spin-off warrant caution.

Existing investors should hold, while new investors should wait for a better entry point.

Currently, Flex carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).
